items.s: Staines leads league revival Report and results of the third Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 match on Wimbledon Common, won by Gary Staines with Belgrave's men 5th and the young athletes 2nd and 3rd. Staines leads league revival REEBOK SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 3 WIMBLEDON COMMON, 6 JAN 96 We know the Common well but there are some areas rarely visited by our runners - and for good reasons. Whether the area now known as the "Butts" really was used for military purposes in the 18th and 19th century is unknown (the area around the Windmill certainly was) but anyway, this series of muddy clay banks hemmed in by thick bushes makes for decidedly unfriendly running conditions - although Thames Hare & Hounds seem to delight in taking their courses right across them. We were pleased to see Gary Staines turning out. He felt a little below par but was soon locked in battle with training partner Jon Solly as they toured the first circuit. Jim Estall, Roger Alsop, Bruce Barton and Phil Carstairs were well forward, and showing that if you've got class it soon makes itself evident, Dave Beaver was not far behind. Limping along prior to coming out at half way, Nick Kello had badly twisted an ankle, putting paid to his running activities for a few weeks. Into the second half of the race and Gary applied the pressure on the hills. It was too much for Herne Hill's Solly and as the leaders swept down along the edge of the playing fields the crowd waiting at the finish could see that the Belgrave man had levered open a comfortable 50 metre gap. We missed our Captain and his customary place just inside the top ten (he was away in Sweden for a few days) so next Belgravian was Jim Estall, doing his bid for the veteran title no harm at all by crossing the line in 18th. The rest of the team had mostly preserved their places. Charlie Dickinson found the jarring conditions tough for 45 year-old bones but nevertheless had the beating of Alex Luce; Steve Hewes was out for the first time but not eligible to score, so it was left to Mikes Webb and Nouch to close in our team in the 80's. At 5th the team result was better but we still had plenty of room for improvement. James Venning added his weight to the under 17 team and with our regulars in action again it was another 2nd place with 3rd for the under 13s led home again by David Bates. Report on the Veterans AC cross country championships at Wimbledon, with gold for Laurie O'Hara and bronze for Carl Cross in the over-sixties and Mike Nouch first Belgravian in 9th. VAC C.C. CHAMPS. WIMBLEDON, 13 JAN 96 There was the usual strong Belgrave presence in the VAC Championships, eleven runners in a field of 112. The only medals again came from our over sixties with Laurie O'Hara winning yet another gold but a surprise and welcome bronze for Carl Cross. At the front Bob Treadwell won his third Championship in 25:11 from Grenville Tuck, first M45 in a new record time of 25:37. First Belgravian home was Mike Nouch in 9th, running slightly slower than his best time in 26:50. Laurie, now 63, finished 17th in the race in 28:38 and was only 40 seconds outside his record time. Carl Cross ran a strong 34:00 for his third M60. It was nice to see Rex Bale (29:54) new to the M50 age group, and also Tony Hardy (31:20) back again after injury and now M55. items.s: South of Thames "Senior" CC Champs. Report on the South of Thames senior cross country championships at Brockwell Park, won by late entry Gary Staines from Herne Hill's John Solly. SOUTH OF THAMES "SENIOR" CC CHAMPS. BROCKWELL PARK, 10 FEB 96 Now this was a race in which few of our number showed any interest - so we didn't enter a team. And then Gary Staines found himself looking for an outing so a swift and late entry by the Team Manager, with help from the SoT officials, got Belgrave tacked onto the tail-end of the programme at the last minute. It's deceptively hard, is Brockwell Park. Parkland it might be but there is hardly a level stretch to be found anywhere. Perhaps the sharp inclines had something to do with the untimely death of the MP for Norwood who had a great deal to do with purchasing the grounds for the public in 1892: he died at the Park's opening ceremony. Nevertheless, the slopes suited our man well as he once more had the beating of John Solly who in turn led his Herne Hill team to an overwhelming victory on their home ground. With the Hill's John Gebbels being President of the South of Thames CC Association this winter it was a fitting team win. Gary did not have such a team to back him up. Dave Beaver took off like a rocket but found the extra distance painful while Don Anderson, who will tackle anything, was our only other runner. 1, G.Staines (Belgrave) 36:32; 2, J.Solly (Herne Hill) 37:05; 3, J.Hyde (Windsor S&E) 37:42; ... 51, D.Beaver 41:58; 109, D.Anderson 45:56; 164 finished. items.h: Our best men's league result in years
items.sum: Report and results of the final 1995-96 Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 match at Coulsdon, won by Gary Staines with Belgrave's men 4th, their best result in years, and Jim Estall taking the veterans' series title.
items.s: Our best men's league result in years Report and results of the final 1995-96 Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 match at Coulsdon, won by Gary Staines with Belgrave's men 4th, their best result in years, and Jim Estall taking the veterans' series title. Our best men's league result in years REEBOK SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 4 COULSDON, 17 FEB 96 Belgrave's senior men finished 4th on the day in the last Surrey league match of the season, their best result in years and at last some real encouragement for the team and reward for the huge effort put in by Alan Mead over the winter. There was already a confident atmosphere before the race with most of the recognised Belgrave distance runners reporting for their numbers. Then Gary Staines strolled up with Linda. This was Gary's second consecutive League race, only a week after his victory in the South of Thames "Senior," a really unexpected bonus for the team. One could immediately sense the positive effect this had on everyone else. And now we are really beginning to get an engine room. Not just the old reliables, Graham Adams, Jim Estall, Roger Alsop and Phil Carstairs, but add to that list Bruce Barton, the new revelation Dave Beaver the much improved Alex Luce, and don't forget new second claim member Steve Hewes who will hopefully be scoring for us next season. Yes, there is already an air of excitment about next season. As the runners climbed the long haul up to the downs for the first time, Gary looked very comfortable sitting in the first group. Then the already mentioned Belgrave vests stretched from the early twenties to the fifties with Junior Galley looking relaxed after his Caribbean holiday (perhaps a bit too relaxed) and Said Chettati, struggling hard against the effects of his fast for Ramadin. Then there was the reliable Mike Nouch, Pete Gilbey and Marlon Anderson. By the time they reached the steep hill after two miles Gary was controlling the race from the front with Dave Taylor of Herne Hill, not long out of hospital, struggling to keep in contact. Graham Adams, Jim Estall and Roger Alsop were all packing together in the early twenties with Bruce Barton running a sensible race a few places further back, followed by Phil Carstairs, dropping slightly, Dave Beaver and Alex Luce. The pattern continued at the front until the last quarter of the race when Gary sped away from a very tired looking Taylor to win with ease by a margin of nearly half a minute. Next for Belgrave up the steep hill the second time was Jim Estall, but only just ahead of Graham Adams and Roger Alsop. It was the determination and 1500m speed of Graham that enabled him to lead the trio at the finish. For Jim, this final flourish gave him the individual veterans' title for the whole series. Only just behind was Bruce Barton in 30th, ever improving in his first real season on the country, a very good run on a tough course. Next Belgravian was Steve Hewes showing the benefit of those ten mile training runs with Roger Alsop and company but he was only just ahead of Dave Beaver, Phil Carstairs and Alex Luce, all finishing in the mid fifties. Poor Said had to stop to be sick on the second lap subsequently losing next scoring place to Mike Nouch. To make things worse he then lost out to his 3000m adversary Junior Galley who closed in 93rd. This result moved Belgrave up to 6th overall in the league well away from relegation danger and hopefully providing a platform on which to build for next season. We really need to strengthen the middle order so that the final scorers are in the fifties, not eighties and nineties, plus we need the the occasional guest appearances by some of our stars: Darren Mead, Matt Yates, Chris Sweeney and a fit again Kassa. We shouldn't always have to rely on Gary. Yes, it could be a good season next winter! But while the seniors were congratulating themselves on at last showing signs of a revival, the youngsters were also pleased with their performances. Another battling performance from Amir took him to 4th place and individual Under 17 winner for the 1995/96 series. Kevin Quinn and Peter McDonald were next in but one to watch in the next couple of seasons is Steve Beaver - an Under 15 but chasing the other three home. Steve Beaver was first Under 15 on the day and yet another individual winner for Belgrave in his age group. Our Under 13 team was again headed by David Bates and Paul Graham and if these lads and their team-mates can continue to apply themselves in future seasons the way they have this winter, then the Bels will have some fine runners moving up through the ranks. items.s: Matt Yates wins the "Parker Bowl" Report and results of the National Cross Country Championships at Newark, where 1500m runner Matt Yates was 66th, Belgrave completed no team and Janine Brown gave the club its best female 'National' performance. Matt Yates wins the "Parker Bowl" REEBOK NATIONAL CC CHAMPS NEWARK, 9 MAR 96 The Belgrave men's team is always full of surprises. At a time when 14k of cross country seems unpopular among our members, 1500m star Matt Yates fancied having a run and, donning a brand new pair of spikes and a Belgrave vest to tackle the Showground and farmland of Newark, proceeded to give us our best individual position since .. well, you tell us. The official results also showed the name of K.Tadesse (Bel) at 50th but all we can say is that it wasn't our Kassa or anyone else we knew running under his number - a shame, because 50th and 66th would have given us a good start for the team race - if we'd had a couple more men prepared to give it a go. Bingley were phenomenal. In a field of approaching 2,000 finishers they had six scoring men home in 32 with two others inside 100. Tipton's team were also all placed inside the first 50 but maybe we'd give them all something to think about the following week at the relays. In fact we failed to complete a team in any category. Our Under 17 Men came closest and would have placed 21st but for the fact that the "Vest Police" disqualified Peter McDonald for failing to wear a Belgrave singlet. The fact that at that time with our stocks run down we simply did not have one to fit him cuts no ice with folk like the "VPs" and one can only hope that such actions don't put the young man off the sport. Janine Brown, running in the youngest girls' age group gave us our best ever performance in female "National" cross country races and we'll be watching this talented athlete's progress with great interest in the years to come. items.h: Bels. fifth in National C.C. Relay
items.sum: Report and result of the English National Cross Country Relay Championships at Berry Hill, Mansfield, where Belgrave's team of Graham Adams, Matt Yates, Darren Mead and Gary Staines finished 5th on the club's debut in the event.
items.s: Bels. fifth in National C.C. Relay Report and result of the English National Cross Country Relay Championships at Berry Hill, Mansfield, where Belgrave's team of Graham Adams, Matt Yates, Darren Mead and Gary Staines finished 5th on the club's debut in the event. Bels. fifth in National C.C. Relay ENGLISH NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPS. BERRY HILL, MANSFIELD, 16 MAR 96 We felt that we needed a high profile win to give the team a boost and looking at the fixture card this National 4 x 5k Relay seemed to be the one where we could do the business. For a start we "only" needed four class runners and secondly, it was the week after the National Cross Country Champs. when all the opposition would be "knackered" while we had been resting up. When organiser Dave Denton acknowledged the entry he couldn't help adding the note: "Potentially the winning team, Alan - if you can get them all out!" Well, we had a darn good try, but it wasn't to be. For one thing, we'd failed to grasp that clubs like Bingley and Tipton and Border have enough top class runners to turn out week after week. Secondly, in a race of only four legs, however good your top men are, they simply run out of race track when trying to make up ground over a mere 5k. In damp and freezing conditions 'Gerry' Adams got us under way and while the announcer gave us plenty of air-time due to his pleasure at seeing the Bels making their debut in this Northern dominated event. 'Gerry' found himself running his heart out in an attempt to give us a good start but was actually on the receiving end of some startling running and was disappointed to complete his leg 17th of the 73 starters. He looked a bit dispirited but generally, with the hills and soft going, the times seemed to be getting on for a minute slower than a genuine track 5k and he would have been pleased with a 14:42 on the all-weather oval. In the meantime Coventry Godiva had gone clear at the front with an 8 second margin over Border AC. Border's 'B' team were 3rd, Tipton 4th and we were 37 seconds in arrears. Next up was Matt Yates and he set about the teams ahead as if it was war. He had some large gaps to bridge but nevertheless, Birchfield, Morpeth, Liverpool and Sheffield were just some of the teams that fell to his all-devouring stride and he must have been delighted at out-running Sale's Kevin McKay by ten seconds. Border had gone ahead now with a 14:58 from Russell - the day's fastest at that point - while Bingley had gone 2nd and Tipton were up to 3rd. The gap from first to our own 11th had grown by another 6 seconds. Dave Denton hit the mike again: " ... and Belgrave are now moving through the field as Matt Yates hands over to Darren Mead ... great to see him in action again ..." Five more clubs fell by the wayside as Darren took his new Nike vest past Chelmsford, Sale, Derby ... Border were still holding on at the front and we were now 6th with Gary eager to take his turn in the chase. Those at the very front were not letting up any and we were now about 50 seconds in arrears and knew that it was too much even for Gary. But one thing was for sure - it was going to be exciting. Amazing! What actually happened was that Gary ran faster than any man had done that afternoon - so far. Although in a period of very heavy mileage for his forthcoming London Marathon attempt, his 14:43 had him rocketing past Loughboro's Bruno Witchalls. But up ahead, Bingley's Hawkins clocked 14:40 to run down Border and take the lead, only to be chased by Coventry's Troumans who went even faster with a 14:32 to all but win on the line. Virtually all the day's fastest times were clocked on the last leg by runners in the first five and Gary was rendered powerless to make any major advances. Looking back, we had to be pleased, and as Darren said after the event, "Next year ..." 1, Bingley 59:56; 2, Coventry Godiva 59:56; 3, Border 1:00:15; 4, Tipton 1:00:28; 5, Belgrave 1:00:49 (G.Adams 17th 15:42, M.Yates 11th 15:07, D.Mead 6th 15:17, G.Staines 5th 14:43); 57 teams finished; 73 started. FOLLOWING a Peterborough 10k course record of 28:33 from Paul Evans 6 days earlier and an equally impressive 63:31 Reading Half-Marathon win from Gary Staines on March 31st, finishing touches were added to London Marathon preparations at Portsmouth's BUPA 5k on April 13th. 'Five k' is a totally different proposition to 26.2 miles so we couldn't interpret wins/losses here into marathon pointers but no runner worth his salt wants to give anything away anything to a rival so Evans must have been pretty pleased with his best ever 13:48 behind 19 year-old Kenyan Philip Mosima but more importantly ahead of rivals Staines and Martin. A nice way for the East Anglian to celebrate his 35th birthday. Gary Staines' 13:59 showed that moving home from Earlsfield to Banstead during the week had not taken too much out of him and so the scene was set for 'London' the following week. items.sum: Report and results of the Belgrave-Nike Road Relays at Wimbledon (dated '23 Mar 1966' in the heading, a misprint for 1996), won by Belgrave 'A' in both the men's 6-stage and women's 3-stage races, with Gary Staines and Gabby Collison fastest.
items.s: Gabby and Gary the fastest as Bels. scoop the prizes Report and results of the Belgrave-Nike Road Relays at Wimbledon (dated '23 Mar 1966' in the heading, a misprint for 1996), won by Belgrave 'A' in both the men's 6-stage and women's 3-stage races, with Gary Staines and Gabby Collison fastest. Gabby and Gary the fastest as Bels. scoop the prizes BELGRAVE-NIKE ROAD RELAYS WIMBLEDON, 23 MAR 1966 It looks as if this 6-Stage promotion for men and 3-Stage for women is likely to become a permanent feature of the fixture list as Thames Valley's race seems destined not to return. We hadn't necessarily intended holding the event again but with Nike's impending sponsorship and the need - don't faint you old timers - to have a few run-offs to assist with selection for the Southern 12-Stage, the wheels of organisation began to turn again. The lap was extended to a more acceptable 2 miles 1013 yards and in spite of the low-key advertising, 29 men's teams and 10 women's teams faced President Snowy Brooks for the start. The initial stage gave us a three-way Belgrave clash as Dave Pamah (preparing for the track season and with no recent form) battled with Junior Galley (well into marathon training but desperate to do the 12-Stage) and the spritely Dave Beaver. Within just over 13 minutes selection problems had been eased a little as all three of our men's teams came in well up but with Dave Pamah holding the aces in spite of blowing up at 2 miles while actually in the lead. City of Portsmouth were 1st stage leaders while in the women's race Windsor had a 39 second gap over Helen Maskrey for the Belles. Now the fun started in earnest as "Stainsey" set out on what proved to be by far the fastest lap of the day (with one exception), gaining a 43 second lead for Belgrave in the process. What a runner - and he'd already done god knows how many miles and a hill session in the morning! Nikki Haines determinedly turned the screws on Windsor to draw up to within 4 seconds of the lead in the women's race, paving the way for a superb run from Gabby Collison whose last leg 14:19 was a full 40 seconds faster than any other female runner (and a good deal faster than many of the men). The men's 'A' team were also not to be headed again as Bruce Barton and Jim Estall laid the ground for a blistering run from Roger Alsop and a final flourish from Kassa Tadesse. But we dropped a hint that there was another fine run to come - and on leg four, this time running for the 'C' team Gary churned out another astounding run with 11:54 to put the 'Cs' in front of the 'Bs' again, a lead they were to hold until young Kevin Quinn got the better of Leo Coy near the end. It really was an enjoyable event with the needs of the athletes paramount in the minds of the officials. Herne Hill's Jon Solly ran three stages paired up with Hare & Hounds' Wayne Oxborough who ran two - and yet they still managed to finish 2nd (although not eligible for prizes). The prizes donated by Nike were most generous and visiting team managers clearly stated their intention to return next year, should we continue. The race looks set to run and run. items.s: BVAF National Cross Country Champs. Report on the BVAF National veterans' cross country championships at Princethorpe College, Rugby, where Belgrave's M60 team was 4th, Pat Newell 4th M65 and Rex Bale first Belgravian in 46th. BVAF NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPS., PRINCETHORPE COLLEGE, RUGBY, 17 MAR 96 The small mainly M60 team of Belgrave runners were joined by Alastair Aitkin and Jeremy Hemming for the minibus trip up the M40 to Princethorpe College. The undulating grassland couse set in the lovely grounds of the college provided a tough test for the runners and an ideal view for spectators. With the M40 winner Nigel Gates finishing in 34:38 we had proof of the severity of the course. Unfortunately, it was not a good day for Belgrave. Poor Laurie O'Hara had been unwell all week and should not have run. He looked rather ashen when the bus picked him up at Iver, and he had to stop to be sick half way through the race. Even so, he went past Ron Higgs again but had to be content with 11th M60. Perhaps the best run was by Pat Newell, new to M65, who started very cautiously but worked through strongly to finish just outside the medals in 4th. Further back was Charlie Walker who kept going well to finish 10th M65 ahead of Bert Stroud and an unhappy looking Carl Cross. All that resulted in a 4th place for the M60 Belgrave team. Rex Bale was a lonely Belgrave figure in the M50's and ran well to finish first Belgrave on the day in 43:50 for 46th place. items.sum: Report and results of the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay at Thurrock, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 8th of 57 and then declined its National 12-Stage place.
items.s: Southern Comfort Report and results of the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay at Thurrock, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 8th of 57 and then declined its National 12-Stage place. Southern Comfort SOUTH OF ENGLAND 12-STAGE ROAD RELAY THURROCK, 31 MAR 96 As stated elsewhere, the new management crew could hardly contain their excitement over the team that was beginning to shape up in the weeks before the race and there is no doubt that had we been able to hold it together until the day we would have been right up there in the medals. But the art of team management is turning promises into reality - and we have a little way to go yet. Of our entered 24 names we soon lost Michael Kazimierski - not eligible until 1st May, Nigel Powley - similarly not yet available after switching from Colchester, Phil Carstairs - on holiday in America, Stu' Paton - last minute working, Gary Staines - urgently in need of a much longer race preceding 'London', and with the race just 48 hours away 'Gerry' Adams was unable to switch shifts at the Fire Station and Dave Pamah went down with a cold. One after the other the reserves were called upon and before we go any further we must thank them for filling in at the last minute - especially Mark Anderson who cut out his normal Saturday training run to stand by the following day at the race should anyone else fall by the wayside at the last minute. In the face of all of this our 8th place from 57 teams must be seen as a success and if we didn't do quite as well as we might have, we can draw comfort from the fact that next year our team is sure to be that much more powerful. We decided to start off strongly and then gradually apply the pressure in the middle, hoping that we could gain enough ground so that when the gaps built up later in the race our reserve men could hold on for a reasonable position - and that's just the way it worked out. Handling his long stage expertly, Roger Alsop set the ball rolling nicely with his 13th place in a time that was to stand up as second only to Darren Mead's - and only by 23 seconds at that. Similarly Rob Turner was our second fastest short stage man as he gained five places for 8th. Marcello had been suffering from a groin strain in the weeks before and had been a doubtful starter. He gamely plugged away but we were down to 14th with a quarter of the race gone. Up ahead the lead had been changing with each leg. GEC held the early advantage through Tony Whiteman, then it was Boxhill and London Irish before things began to settle down with Boxhill again leading but with Hounslow and Blackheath ominously moving closer. Our own stage four was taken by Alex Luce; with a sore throat he was not at his best and he lost seven places before we started to wind things up again as halfway approached. While Blackheath went ahead for the first time our own Jim Estall did plenty of damage himself as he clocked our third fastest long leg and recovered five places. Now it was up to Matt Yates to impose himself on the field. What an asset this man is. Half a minute faster than anyone else on the stage, he ripped the opposition apart to take the Bels up to 7th with a lightning 12:29; the second fastest by anyone on the day. Darren Mead was third fastest on his leg with 23:27 and now just Blackheath, Hounslow, Boxhill, Chelmsford and Aldershot remained ahead. As we expected, the gaps were now large. We couldn't in all honesty expect to gain any more ground and it was a case of hanging in as well as we could. Bruce Barton's short stage came and went - still 6th. In spite of cramping up badly Junior Galley lost only one place as Thames Valley got by. Forty-five year-old 'toughie' Pete Gilbey set out with Shaftesbury's international John Sherban on his shoulder, had him race past within seconds, but 14 minutes later came back home with the Shaftesbury man nowhere to be seen (he'd pulled a muscle). Last minute recruit for a long stage Mike Webb enjoyed his Essex outing, giving way to Old Gaytonians and finally a Friday night recruit Nick Kello celebrated his birthday (and the Team Manager's) by holding steady in 8th. Footnote: The top twenty teams qualified for the National 12-Stage but on the night of the race we took the decision not to take the place we had earned at Sutton Park. Several of our runners would be involved in the London Marathon and would therefore be unavailable, while others were off for warm weather training or other such activities prior to the track season. It was agreed that it was better to end the season on a relatively high note than take a team to the Nationals that would probably finish in the 40s. 1, Blackheath 3:41:43; 2, Boro Hounslow 3:42|:39; 3, Boxhill 3:43:31; 4, Chelmsford 3:45:27; 5, Aldershot 3:47:36; 6, Thames Valley 3:48:33; ... 8, Belgrave 3:51:37; 57 teams finished. items.sum: Report and results of the 1996 London Marathon, run as the club championship, in which Belgrave won the team race in 9:56:02 led by Paul Evans (3rd, 2:10:40) and Gary Staines (9th), with Stuart Paton's marathon debut.
items.s: London Marathon Team Champions Report and results of the 1996 London Marathon, run as the club championship, in which Belgrave won the team race in 9:56:02 led by Paul Evans (3rd, 2:10:40) and Gary Staines (9th), with Stuart Paton's marathon debut. LONDON MARATHON Team Champions LONDON MARATHON 21 APR 96 This race must go down as the classiest Club Championship of all time. Paul Evans was expected to produce his usual high standard run while for Gary Staines, it was his second attempt at going all the way, humid conditions making things difficult in his first attempt in Vienna just on 12 months ago. Then there was Jim Estall - as fit as a flea - and a whole bunch of others who may well spring surprises: Marcello Bizio, Stu' Paton, Junior Galley, Mike Kazimierski ... who would close in our team on what we hoped would be a winning occasion? What no-one bargained for was the unseasonably high temperature with the mercury being pushed to 21°C (70°F) by midday and there is no doubt that it had a great effect on the way the race turned out. Early on a large bunch including all the main players broke away with Paul Evans' blond head bobbing away in the midst. Gary's start was more conservative and by Tower Bridge he was conspicuous in the second wave of international runners with former winner Eamonn Martin already struggling just ahead. Looking for a time in the mid 2:20s, Jim Estall had set off at 5½ minute mile pace but he soon realised that this was not going to be the day for such a pace and eased off to 5:45s for fear of blowing up. Mike Kazimierski came past him at Rotherhithe so as this pair crossed the river it was 'Kaz' ahead with Jim tucked in not too far behind. Bouncing along, Stuart Paton looked in great shape, accompanied by Marcello and an incognito Matt Yates out for a training spin. Surely no team could match this. Six men through in about 200 places. The second half was murderous. As the leading bunch was whittled away around the Isle of Dogs Evans continued to look comfortable but Gary's pack seemed to disintigrate. For Stuart the signs of dehydration became evident. He had suffered similarly on a recent long training run so he knew he was in for a bad time. Junior and Jim were also feeling the heat but Mike Kazimierski's run was looking better and better although all of them were now running a long way down on their "hoped for" times. Well, we all know now that among the front runners Mexico's Dionicio Ceron was the iron man. When he made his break with just over 3 miles to go it was all over for the others as he powered on to his third consecutive victory. Belgium's Vincent Rousseau looked strong along the Embankment while Paul and the young African Kabiga battled it out for third and fourth. A good number of club members had gathered here to cheer on their team and when Gary Staines hove into sight in 9th place they jubilantly proclaimed their excitement at seeing that our second man through in the Club Championship was also the next Briton. What a second half he had run and tired though he was, a wry smile briefly flickered across his face at his Embankment reception. Now we wanted a third and fourth man through to complete the team. The gaps were huge - far greater than normal - but at last a Belgrave vest was spied ... and it was Kazimierski, some five minutes down on his projected time but running strongly and in the 50s. The trouble was, he was not eligible for team competition until 1st May. Then, drenched from tipping water over himself, Jim Estall came out of the Blackfriar's tunnel, but where now was our legitimate 4th scorer? It was some twenty minutes before a tired Junior came through followed by the battered remnants of our team. There had been all sorts of drama around 20 miles. Stuart had completely hit the wall and walked for ages between 17 and 19 miles before Dennis Williams of H/W got him going again and it was at this stage that Junior passed him. Marcello had reached 20miles in 1:57 but then took an hour for the last six miles, his groin injury having got to him again. Our chances in the team race seemed to be blown away. There were plenty more Bels to cheer on. Lionel Mann had an amazing run over quarter of an hour faster than last year while Paul Cooper was thrilled to bits with his effort. Then late that night came the news that in spite of everything we had indeed won the team race. All the teams had been equally decimated by the warm conditions but our scoring quartet's times added together came to 9:56:02 and we easily had the measure of any other squad. And just think, if Mike Kazimierski had been eligible we would have been home in 9:31:15 - a team time out of this world - not to mention the fact that just after the race Anthony Robertson (125th in 2:36:34) signed up for the Bels! One of the most interesting points had been Stuart's debut. As a class 1500m runner, his club-mates, in changing-room discussions, had him down as anything between 2:35 and 2:50, so was he disappointed with his run? Well, he'd like to have gone better and as he said, " ... with a 1500 if you run a crap race one week you can always run another one the next weekend - but there's no way I'm doing another marathon for a bit. Still, it's got to me. It's a whole new sport - and I will be having another go." 1, D.Ceron (Mexico) 2:10:00; 2, V.Rousseau (Belgium) 2:10:36; 3, P.Evans (Belgrave) 2:10:40; ... 9, G.Staines 2:12:54; 60, M.Kazimierski 2:31:44; 113, J.Estall 2:35:57; 125, A.Robertson 2:36:34; 736, J.Galley 2:56:31; 815, M.Bizio 2:57:28; 1008, S.Paton 2:59:49; 1320, A.Verdie 3:04:27; 2724, L.Mann 3:19:27; 2294, P.Cooper 3:15:13; 4587, R.Mann 3:32:53; 5162, L.Coy 3:37:17; 5153, M.Graham 3:37:12; 9144, E.Derouet 3:58:59; 10248, C.Henn 4:04:35; C.Preston ran but we have yet to find his time in the results and similarly D.Davies ran 3:56-ish. Relays Leo Coy's report and results from the McDonalds young athletes' National Road Relays at Sutton Park, where Belgrave finished a team in every age group for the first time, with the under 17s 22nd. MCDONALDS YA NATIONAL R. RELAYS SUTTON PK, 31 MAR 96 For the first time ever we managed to start and finish a team in each age group in this superb event, writes Leo Coy. Good organisation and a testing course, together with the most talented young road runners in the country, make this a great day out for everybody. Belgrave competed very well with David Bates giving the under 13s a good start. Likewise Steve Beaver in the under15s, where he was well supported by Robert Bignall. Jason Stevens proved the team manager wrong with an excellent solo run in the 'B' team. Highlight of the day was the performance by the under 17s. James Venning had a good start and Peter McDonald battled hard to lose just one place. He handed over to the 'Mighty Quinn' and Kevin zipped through the field to gain ten places. Amir was very impressive as he gained a further six places to 22nd. Well done team! Thanks to Dave Beaver, Steve Whorlow and the Venning family for their support. items.sum: Unsigned introduction to the Race Walking section reviewing the young race walkers' successes since the event was reintroduced in winter 1994/95.
e: RWA Younger Age Groups' Grand Prix Series
items.s: Race Walking Unsigned introduction to the Race Walking section reviewing the young race walkers' successes since the event was reintroduced in winter 1994/95. Since Race Walking was re-introduced to the Young Athletes in the Winter of 1994/95 it has taken off like an express train. In every age group the Club is now having major successes. From Young International down to County Championships the team has proudly represented the Bels. In 1995 we won no less than twentytwo National, Regional and County Medals, six English School Vests, two South of England Vests, two County AA Vests, and already we have been informed that at least three of the team will be representing the South this year, with another two or three on the borderline for selection. It is impossible to mention every Young Race Walker in this short piece, although they really do deserve it, so if your name has not been mentioned, please accept that everything written applies to you all. We have travelled far and wide, and if the British League Team think they travel a long way, try this for a year's travel - London (many times), Dublin, Weymouth, Chesterfield, Birmingham (three times), Coventry, Leamington Spa, Brierly Hill, Bexley (four times), Stoke-on-Trent, plus taking part in the Thameside League. In the 1994/95 season we finished fifth out of twentyfour teams in the RWA Younger Age Groups' Grand Prix Series, and we only competed in half the matches. This year we are expecting to improve and we are fighting for second place with Sheffield RWC and Steyning AC (two of the country's top Race Walking Clubs). The Under 15 Boys won their 1994/95 series and are expected to be in a similar position again when September comes around. The Girls, although small in number, are also improving on their previous year's position. items.sum: Steve Whorlow Snr., the younger age group walking team manager, reports on the young walkers' championship golds, new club records and the team's spirit.
e: Kent County AAA Road Walking Championships
items.s: Race Walking Excites The Club Steve Whorlow Snr., the younger age group walking team manager, reports on the young walkers' championship golds, new club records and the team's spirit. In February we took a near clean sweep of the Kent County AAA Road Walking Championships with five Golds (out of six), followed by four SEAA Road Walking Championships Golds in March, and with numerous Silver and Bronze medals. We have been very successful in these Championships and expect to continue on the Track this summer. By the time you read this the event will be over, but in May the National YAG Race Walking Championships are due to be hosted by Belgrave Harriers in Folkestone and are expected to be the highlight of this Club's race walking year. As it is home ground for many, and with the fanatical family support that the team has, even more success is expected to come our way. Club Records are beginning to fall after many years of sitting on the shelf - and not just by a few seconds. In the Girls' records Laura Fryer has knocked 2 minutes off the Club's Under 13 3000m track record and she has also taken the 2km, 2.5km and 3km records. Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith took the Under 15 2km road record in Dublin with 11:28 and Lucy Asling the Under 11 1km and 1.2km road and 1000m track records. In the Boys' Section records have gone to Nigel Whorlow in the Under 15, 17 and 20 age groups. He now holds the Under 15 2km and 2.5km road and 3000m track, the Under 17 2.5km, 3km road and 5000m track, along with our best ever times for Under 17 and Under 20 at 11km road records. Richard Banham and Stephen Whorlow are sharing most of the Under 13 records between them. All these marks, along with many others that have stood for a long time, are expected to fall during 1996. This can only be good for the future of Race Walking in the Club. We have become known throughout the country as the best TEAM in terms of support towards each other. Every athlete without question supports every other member of their team. No disappearing after the finish, they get their breath back and cheer in those that are still coming home. Cheering those in other races is also the norm - and not just our own team, because we have made many friends throughout the country who also deserve our support. This in turn gives the Club a name for good sportsmanship. We also have a great family support being built up. As the Younger Age Group's Walking Team Manager it has been the most exciting year I have had with the Club, and working with Carl Lawton and other Senior walkers, we should be able to make Race Walking secure in the Club for many years to come. The Club has supported the event well and we hope that our successes have made the unexpected expenditure worthwhile. It has now moved out of being a minority section of the Club and Race Walking is now on a par with the Young Athletes Track & Field and Cross Country sections within the Club. Steve Whorlow, Snr. items.s: New Year's Day Walks Victoria Park, 1 Jan 96 Report and results of Loughton AC's City New Year Walks in Victoria Park, an RWA Grand Prix event where Belgrave's young walkers finished second overall to Leicester. NEW YEAR'S DAY WALKS VICTORIA PARK, 1 JAN 96 On New Year's Day 13 Young Athletes travelled to Victoria Park, London, to take part in Loughton AC's City New Year Walks which was also an RWA Grand Prix event. It was another successful day in most of the age groups. In the Under 11 Girls' race (1km) our youngsters showed us what the future has to offer - and it looks very rosy. Lucy Asling took 1st with Dannielle Johnson 2nd and Rebecca Andrews 3rd. Not surprisingly they also took the team race. We only had one Under 13 Girls' entry but that was enough because fast improving Laura Fryer gained her first win in a RWA Grand Prix event. In the Under 15 Boys we had similar success with Chris Stanford taking a very good 3rd but with the withdrawal of two of our walkers after only 500m it was left to the younger boys of the team to bring home the joint U15/U13 team prize. Well done Chris Stanford, Stephen Whorlow and Robert Bignall. In the Under 17 age group we again took two of the minor prizes. An unwell Kelly-Anne decided she still wanted to race and was rewarded with 2nd in the Ladies under 17 race. Nigel Whorlow took 3rd in the Youth's event even though he walked for three-quarters of the race with a loose shoe lace. (Never agin Nigel!) Overall the Club gained 285 hard won Grand Prix points and stood second only to Leicester - possibly the top Race Walking Club in the country. items.s: Molly Barnett Grand Prix Coventry, 3 Mar 96 Report and results of Belgrave's young walkers at the Molly Barnett Grand Prix in Coventry, where four fourth places left the team without a trophy. MOLLY BARNETT GRAND PRIX COVENTRY, 3 MAR 96 Another long journey, to Coventry, where our youngsters again set walking alight with their enthusiasm. A quote from the Race Walking Record (April 1996) remarked on the increase of numbers and shows how they are now being accepted as a regular force in YAG Race Walking " ... and it's not all down to the Belgrave travelling show making the trip for the first time - they did have fourteen finishers, about one third of the increase ". The races were of mixed age groups which does not always lead to good racing as the youngsters tend to go off fast with the older walkers. In the Under 13/15 Girls' race Laura Fryer came 14th (4th under 13), losing out on 3rd by 5 seconds. Chris Stanford placed 7th in the equivalent Boys' event, having an "off" day but still recording a pb of 10:52. Richard Banham led home our Under 13 Boys with 25th. Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith was 19th in the Women's 5km (4th U17) and to add to the team's misery of just missing out, Nigel Whorlow also came home 4th in his Under 17 Men's 10km, 15th overall. With so many 4th places it meant that the team came home for the first time in many months without a trophy between them - leaving them even more determined to succeed at Weymouth. items.label: June 1996
items.h: P.W. "Jimmy" Green: A man of many talents
items.sum: Profile of P.W. "Jimmy" Green, founder and long-time editor of Athletics Weekly, coach and Belgrave's longest-standing member, introduced by Clive Shippen, marking his 87th birthday.
items.s: P.W. "Jimmy" Green: A man of many talents Profile of P.W. "Jimmy" Green, founder and long-time editor of Athletics Weekly, coach and Belgrave's longest-standing member, introduced by Clive Shippen, marking his 87th birthday. CLIVE SHIPPEN writes:- In 1954, with the aid of several army physical training instructors, I was able to create a track and field team to represent the School of Military Engineering, Chatham. It was built from raw material and required much honing and refinement if it was to succeed at Army Championship level, so competition was essential. With this in mind I contacted the nearby City of Rochester A.C. to see if they could assist in both competition and training. It was thro' this approach that I first met P.W. "Jimmy" Green. He was a stalwart of the local club and heavily involved in their management and coaching. His response was most supportive and we soon arranged some matches between our teams. I did not realise at the time that he was Editor of Athletics Weekly, then in its 9th year of publication, nor indeed that he had been a member of Belgrave during the War years. Our discussions soon became most animated when he knew I was a Belgravian too. The Military School team benefitted from his help and went on to reach the Army finals the following year. I had not expected the Editor of AW to be so actively involved in club athletics. He seemed to know everyone and it was in no small measure due to him that the City of Rochester '5' was a major event in the racing calendar at that time. No mean athlete himself in earlier days, he had achieved much by 1954; yet he was still only half-way through a life-time in athletics. We kept in touch during the 'fifties and 'sixties via the London Brighton Relay mainly, a passion we both shared, and I sent him race analyses and the occasional article. He has now reached the head of Belgrave's membership list, and it seems appropriate that the following profile should feature in The Belgravian. Born on the 20th March 1909, P.W. "Jimmy" Green spent his formative years in the Tolworth/Surbiton area of Surrey. It was after surprising himself by winning an Open schools 100 yards race that he was approached by Billy Dear of Surrey A.C., a well known figure in cross-country running. Dear invited Jimmy and his friend Bert Pryor to visit his home and see his showcase of medals and trophies. The youngster stared at the case in awe, marvelling at the display and signed up on the spot. When 14 years old he joined the R.A.F. as an apprentice and went to Halton for three years. He continued his sprinting with moderate success in the first year but then took to cross-country running in his second year. He later returned to the Old Malden Fields to pit his new-found fitness against Surrey A.C. runners and found cross-country specialist George Constable on the line. During the five mile race Constable and the front men went off course shortening the race to 3¾ miles. Jimmy found himself just behind the leaders with the finishing straight (100 metres of cinder path) now in sight. In a flash the young newcomer was up on his toes taking them all by surprise with his sprinting ability. It was shock win and Constable did not take it too well; but Jimmy had left his mark with the Surrey AC members who were mostly amused at the upset. After finishing his R.A.F. apprenticeship he was posted overseas first to Palestine and then Iraq. In his four-year posting he was unbeaten in Services races until his old friend and International Sam Ferris joined him for a second stint in the desert. They had last been together when representing the R.A.F. against Middlesex and the Civil Service. Jimmy eventually returned to the U.K. and concentrated on half-miling where he enjoyed much success. But he no longer felt the R.A.F. to be the life he needed and he bought himself out. He went into the retail business, owning two shops, but after only a few months of operation World War 2 was declared and Jimmy found himself straight back in the R.A.F. Posted to R.A.F. Detling he met Charlie Smart who had been similarly posted. They became firm friends and trained regularly at the United Services Ground, Chatham. Additionally they thrashed their way round the Detling Aerodrome perimeter every lunch hour. Jimmy had never known training like it. Encouraged by Charlie he joined Belgrave who were one of the few clubs to keep going during the war. He was a member for five years, until Surrey A.C. resumed activities in 1946. Charlie persuaded him to step up his track distance to 2 miles, in view of his strong finish in the mile, and he was soon joining Len Herbert, Doug. Main, Les Cohen, Tom Carter and Tom Morrell in the two-mile team races in which they were invincible at that time. Etienne Gailly, the Belgian who so very nearly won the 1948 Olympic Marathon was also one of the Belgrave group. When peace arrived in 1945 Charlie Smart went to Germany with the Control Commission where he was unbeaten over 5,000/10,000 metres for two years and was the U.K.'s second ranked 6 miler. Before they parted the two friends had discussed Jimmy's conviction that Athletics deserved a magazine of its own. Coverage at that time was restricted to newspaper columns and various sports magazines. Armour Milne and others had brought out modest gazettes but they were unable to survive for long. If it had not been for his posting to Germany Charlie might well have joined his friend in this ambitious enterprise. Jimmy decided to go it alone. Despite contrary advice from other friends and associates he approached John Langdon Ltd. of Maida Vale and convinced them that it was a viable proposition. Athletics was published for the first time in December 1945. It was a monthly production and remained so for 5 years before it became Athletics Weekly. Although the work-load on the magazine steadily increased and it gave became more and more successful Jimmy continued to give much of his precious time to coaching; enjoying nurturing youngsters from school and taking them through to senior status. Amongst his successes were that formidable duo of the 1960's Brian Barrett and Ken Caulder who finished 1st and 2nd in the National Junior Cross-Country Championship and went on to gain senior international vests. Many older members will remember the remarkable 'Roy' Beckett whom Jimmy converted from miling to 3 miles. He put him through a tough cross-country regime in the winter and was criticised by other coaches of the day for subjecting a track athlete to such work. Beckett went on to win track races at 1 mile, 2 miles and 3 miles in personal bests. His outstanding race, which brought everyone to their feet at White City was the A.A.A. 3 miles event of 1951. He entered the finishing straight shoulder to shoulder with hot favourite Chris Chataway and in one of the most excruciating finishes seen at these Championships won by a mere inch. Jimmy's coaching had been vindicated. In 1982 Surrey A.C. amalgamated with Belgrave and Jimmy Green was once more a Belgrave Harrier. His continuous membership of the two clubs has now reached 71 years, which heads our current membership list. In 1987 Athletics Weekly was sold to EMAP Pursuit and in 1994 he stopped coaching at the age of 85 years; four years after receiving the Master Coach Award. His career has been packed with a whole range of experience. He represented the A.A.A. at 880 yards, 1, 2 and 3 miles; ran for the R.A.F., Kent, Cambridgeshire and Bedfordshire; coached athletes to international standard; edited a national magazine; organised meetings and was a Grade I Starter. His son Tim was a promising middle distance runner, until injured in a road accident, and his grandson Clifton is the A.A.A. U15 Javelin title holder who has been likened to a young Steve Backley. Athletics is certainly in Jimmy's blood, and there is no doubt that a large proportion of it is coloured claret and gold. On April 20th he celebrated his 87th birthday. Belgrave Harriers wish him many many happy returns. "Jimmy's" career has been packed with a whole range of experience: an athlete representing the A.A.A., R.A.F., Kent, Cambridgeshire and Bedfordshire at one, two and three miles, a Grade I Starter for some 40 years, a Senior Coach from an early age and now Master Coach, organiser of athletic meetings, President of Kent County A.A.A., President of City of Rochester A.C., Medway A.C., and Surrey A.C., sports shop proprietor, innovator in the design of athletic shoes and clothing, breeder and racer of greyhounds, athletics tour organiser, founder of "Athletics Weekly" and Editor for 22 years until it was taken over in 1987. P.W. "Jimmy" Green as pictured on the Editorial page of the very first edition of Athletics. The photo actually dates from his R.A.F. days in 1930. Left: Reporting the 1964 Tokyo Olympics with his successor as Athletics Weekly Editor, Mel Watman. Above: "Jimmy" presents the "AW" 10 mile Two-Man Relay Trophy to a youthful Portsmouth AC pairing of Bruce Tulloh and Martin Hyman Left: It's Poly Marathon day, 19th June 1948, and her Majesty The Queen is introduced to some of the runners before they set out on their 26 mile journey from Windsor to Chiswick. Cecil Ballard, of Surrey A.C. is presented to Her Majesty with "Jimmy", no. 31, next in line. P.W. "Jimmy" Green P.W. items.s: Men's T&F Rankings 1995 Belgrave men's 1995 track and field ranking lists by event with world/British age-group positions, dates of birth, venues and dates, compiled by Hazel Mead and kept as scans because of the small print; John Regis heads the sprints, with photos of Callum Taylor, Ian Tullett and Terry Lawton. Men's T&F Rankings 1995 They're a little later than normal but nevertheless, we feel sure that you'll enjoy browsing through last season's best performances and hopefully they'll provide the spur to aim that little bit higher in 1996. As by now most international/national rankings have been published we are able to include World and British positions per age group just before the name of any athlete who has made those lists. Remember that these positions relate to the age group shown after the athlete's name. Wind assisted marks are shown at the end of each event except where we do not know of a non-wind assisted performance. Any errors or amendments to Belgrave Rankings, [address withheld]. Men's Rankings compiled by Hazel Mead Hitting the Belgrave Rankings for the first time, New Zealander Callum Taylor, gained selection for his country's World Championship 4x400m squad. Callum is pictured on his way to 2nd in the 4th BAL match at Enfield. Belgrave's highest flyer in 1995, Ian Tullett cleared 5.30m to take British League Match 4 at Enfield. But Mike Edwards is keen to wrest back the lead and is rumoured to have recently vaulted 5.60 in training. Veteran Vaulter Terry Lawton prepares for SCVAC League Final action at Colindale last September where he equalled his pb of 3.10m to place 8th in the UK among M50s. 100 metres 100 metres (continued), manual, wind assisted and 200 metres 200 metres (continued), wind assisted and 400 metres 400 metres (continued) and 800 metres 1500 metres 1500 metres (continued), 3000 metres and 5000 metres 5000 metres (continued), 10000 metres, 80, 100, 110 and 400 metres hurdles 400 metres hurdles (continued), 1500, 2000 and 3000 metres steeplechase and high jump Long jump and triple jump Triple jump (continued) and pole vault Shot putt (7.26kg) and shot putt (6.25kg) Shot putt (5kg, 4kg, 3.25kg), discus (2kg, 1.75kg, 1.5kg, 1.25kg) and javelin (800g) Javelin (800g, continued; items.label: June 1996
items.sum: Report on Du'aine Ladejo winning the 1996 European Indoor 400m title in Stockholm in 46.12 after a poor 1995, looking ahead to the Atlanta Olympics.
items.s: Ladejo back on track Report on Du'aine Ladejo winning the 1996 European Indoor 400m title in Stockholm in 46.12 after a poor 1995, looking ahead to the Atlanta Olympics. Track & Field Ladejo back on track In 1994 Du'aine Ladejo had a brilliant summer season, winning the European Games 400m Gold Medal and going on to collect further hardware at the Commonwealth Games. It all started that year with a win in European Indoor Championships in Paris. Everything seemed to go wrong the following season but after a miserable 1995 it looks as if the man's back on track, following his 1994 path to glory by collecting the 1996 European Indoor title at Stockholm and becoming the proud owner of four European Gold Medals. The Stockholm track did not turn out to be a favourite with the athletes but it gave no worries to Du'aine who coasted to a 47.84 win in heat three with Saber of Italy fastest of the round in 47.29. Surely a 46.74 has never looked so easy as it did with his semi-final and barring accidents the final on March 10th looked a formality. It was. With 22.10 at halfway he was already out on his own and in total command. Stretching away for another relaxed run he won in 46.12 - a personal record for indoors - but looking for all the world as if he could have gone to low 45s. Frenchman Hilaire was 2nd in 46.82 with Saber third, 46.86. Now for the summer season and the Olympics in Atlanta. A certain American by the name of Michael Johnson would have to be everyone's favourite but let's face it, any American who makes the Games is going to be red hot. Then again, Du'aine has to make the British team first and there are some seven other guys in the UK who are currently showing tremendous form and won't be easy to brush aside. But the Belgravian believes he can go all the way to the top and with such confidence anything could happen. items.label: June 1996
items.sum: Report on Dave Smith throwing the hammer 75.10 at the Inter-Counties Championships for a championship best, British Under 23 record and Olympic qualifying distance.
items.s: Olympic standard hammered! Report on Dave Smith throwing the hammer 75.10 at the Inter-Counties Championships for a championship best, British Under 23 record and Olympic qualifying distance. Olympic standard hammered! Our giant 21 year-old Dave Smith, representing Humberside, tore the heart out of other hammer throwing Britons hoping to gain selection for the Olympics when he all but put the 7.26kg implement into orbit at the Inter-Counties Championships on May 27th. He hadn't been feeling too well recently but you'd never have known it when with a previous pb of 71.54 he started the competition with 70 metres, broke new ground with 72.50 in round three and then hit a massive 75.10 to give him the Championship best performance, a British Under 23 Record and an Olympic Qualifying distance. He fouled on another near-75m throw and then finished up on 72.30. Tremendous stuff! Dave's new mark moves him up to fifth best Briton ever, all the throws ahead of him dating back to the 80s. Dave Smith Dave Smith hammer 75.10 at the Inter-Counties: championship best, British Under 23 record, Olympic qualifying distance; represented Humberside Dave Smith Dave Inter-Counties Track & Field Olympic Games Humberside

items.label: June 1996
items.sum: Note welcoming Jon Ridgeon's return to 400m hurdling after his 1993 achilles injury, with 49.87 at the Welsh Games.
items.s: Ridgeon returns Note welcoming Jon Ridgeon's return to 400m hurdling after his 1993 achilles injury, with 49.87 at the Welsh Games. Ridgeon returns How pleased we were to note the name of Jon Ridgeon among the Australian T&F results this winter. There couldn't have been many who would have expected him to come back again after that awful achilles tendon injury in 1993. But there he was, running 50 and bits for 400 hurdles in the Melbourne sunshine before moving on to California in early May and doing it again to prove that it was no fluke. Second only to Zambian Samuel Matete in the European Club's Cup in Turkey in mid-May, he then stole the headlines at the Welsh Games by coming down to 49.87 and showing every sign of remaining the fastest Briton for the remainder of the season. Will he make it to the Olympics? We earnestly hope so. If ever a man deserves a slice of luck it is Jon. items.s: Home win for the Women Report and results of Southern Women's League Division 3 match 1 at Battersea Park on 27 April 1996, won by Belgrave. Home win for the Women SOUTHERN WOMEN'S LEAGUE DIVISION 3, MATCH 1 BATTERSEA PARK, 27 APR 96 It was touch and go all afternoon but eventually, when the final result was announced it was Belgrave in front. The perfect start to the season. Natalie Law has moved up an age group since last season and now finds herself facing Seniors in SL competition but with new member Sabrina Scott for company, the sprints became a happy hunting ground in the quest for points. There were some good points on the field as well as our old favourites got back into the swing of things in this first match. It was the first time the pole vault was included as a scoring event and with our expert Julia Cockram an expected win became even easier when no-one else turned up to compete. As is often the case, the match result depended upon the outcome of the long relay and when Jackie Stone turned in a 63.0 on leg two we were home and dry but perhaps the best performance of the day came from Syreeta Stracey whose personal best of 5.15 in the long jump moved her up to a whole new level of competition. items.sum: Report and results of National Junior League Division 2 South match 1 at Crawley on 21 April 1996, won by Belgrave, where the junior 4x100m squad broke a club record set in 1965.
items.s: 31 year-old record goes in NJL match 1 Report and results of National Junior League Division 2 South match 1 at Crawley on 21 April 1996, won by Belgrave, where the junior 4x100m squad broke a club record set in 1965. 31 year-old record goes in NJL match 1 NATIONAL JUNIOR LEAGUE DIVISION 2 SOUTH MATCH 1 CRAWLEY, 21 APR 96 One of our oldest Club Records fell in the very first match of the NJL series when our young 4x100 squad removed a tenth from the time set in 1965 when a Belgrave team won the AAA Junior Championship. There's plenty more to come too, as each of the takeovers was extremely 'safe' and Andre Johnson on last leg took his foot off the gas with the line still 20 metres away. It was all a case of continuing in 1996 from where we left off last season; a fifth consecutive league victory for Team Manager Jon Coy and another huge points score. Peter Waterman caught the eye on the field. Still an under 17, he mopped up the hammer and shot events and scored heavily in discus as well. But perhaps the star of the day was Philip Idowu whose 14.68 triple jump so early in the season was a clear indication that he'll be over 15m in a month or two. items.s: SC Veterans' T&F League Mid-London, Match 1, Battersea, 29 Apr 96 Report and results of the Southern Counties Veterans' T&F League Mid-London match 1 at Battersea on 29 April 1996, where the veteran men tied for second and the veteran ladies were second. SC VETERANS' T&F LEAGUE MID-LONDON, MATCH 1 BATTERSEA, 29 APR 96 Our Veteran Men's run of supremecy came to an end with the very first match of the season when we were unable to turn out a team to do ourselves justice as Southern Champions. It wasn't just a lack of middle-distance men - we're used to overcoming that problem. No, we were short of sprinters as well, and with the ever-eager Reg Hopkins a little slower than normal due to a weekend marathon in his legs, Serpentine Runners turned us over and we lost our full quota of points for second place when the Mets. tied with us. No team in our division is a match for Serpentine's Women so we changed tack this year and our small Veteran Ladies' team took the field with the intention of only competing in the events they really wanted to do. The pleasing result was that we did just as well as normal with second team place and perhaps a better chance now of making the finals in September than the men! items.s: Southern League Division 3 Match 1, Battersea Park, 4 May 96 Report and results of Southern League Division 3 match 1 at Battersea Park on 4 May 1996, won by Belgrave. SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 MATCH 1 BATTERSEA PARK, 4 MAY 96 Having both our Southern League teams competing at the same venue and it being a home match as well was a blessing for Team Manager Bob Bridges. He was able decimate the division six outfit to bolster the 'threes' - not so easy when one team has been sent to the South Coast and the other is somewhere North of London. As a result, although we still had no steeplechasers, we started the 1996 season with a win. Maybe our Southern Leaguers can even get back to division two by the end of the summer. With Dalton Powell now living within easy range of London and with 17 year-old Marlon Dickson looking really sharp the sprints were well sewn up. Donal O'Riordan turned out in Belgrave kit for the first time and really looked a class middle-distance man as he strolled away from the field for an easy 1500m win. Our 400 hurdlers and relay runners were on a different level to the opposition and when Dave Pamah blasted a 55 second first lap in the 800 he had the field stretched over a full 150 metres by the end of the race. For a change we were not quite so powerful on the field although our veteran pairing of Mike Small and Snowy Brooks had the measure of most of their opponents. Mike was able to up his own Vets' Club Record in the hammer but it was a slightly downbeat day for our President as he injured himself slightly during the high hurdles. 100m: 1, D.Powell 11.1; 1, M.Dickson 11.1. 200m: 1, D.Powell 22.8; 1, M.Dickson 22.2. 400m: 3, D.Pamah 51.4; 3, T.Lawton 73.8. 800m: 1, D.Pamah 1:53.8; 1, Mark Anderson 2:05.4. 1500m: 1, D.O'Riordan 4:11.5; 1, P.Carstairs 4:22.3. 5000m: 2, J.Galley 15:48.4; 1, D.Beaver 15:57.2. 110mH: 3, L.Rogers 17.5; 2, S.Brooks 22.2. 400mH: 1, A.Daniel 59.3; 1, L.Rogers 59.6. 4x100m: 1, Belgrave 44.3. 4x400m: 1, Belgrave (B.Williams 52.1, M.Parper 49.8, A.Daniel 53.9, L.Rogers 53.9) 3:29.7. items.sum: Report and results of the first British League Division 1 match at Wavertree, where newly promoted Sale beat Belgrave into second place.
items.s: Sale catch us napping — Guardian Insurance British League Division 1 Match 1, Wavertree, 4 May 96 Report and results of the first British League Division 1 match at Wavertree, where newly promoted Sale beat Belgrave into second place. Sale catch us napping GUARDIAN INSURANCE BRITISH LEAGUE DIVISION 1 MATCH 1 WAVERTREE, 4 MAY 96 It was a solid enough start at Liverpool, second with all likely rivals behind us, but frankly we were stunned by the performance of Sale. Fresh up from Division Two they performed to their limits and were fittingly rewarded with a BAL Division One trophy to take back to Manchester. Only the pole vault and discus gave us maximum points but plenty of 2nds, 3rds and 4ths came our way so we were never really in any danger of being caught by the other clubs. ... And Sale themselves don't expect to be top of the heap by the end of the season, looking to the one-per-event Cup competition for their best chances of success. But nevertheless, those red and green vests caught us napping nicely and took the gloss off the start of our season. It was good to see new Belgravians Lee Newman, Tom Lerwill, Dave Smith, Chris Rawlinson and Andy Walcott scoring heavily and our team is beginning to have a distinctly youthful look when you stir in the mix of Juniors Philip Idowu, Geoffrey Ojok, James Hilston and Richard Aspden. The 200 turned out to be one of the hottest events of the afternoon as Sale's Owusu Dako and Haringey's Solomon Wariso delighted in having a pop at European Champion Du'aine Ladejo. Then again, they didn't exactly hang about in the 400m where this time our Dave Nolan got shunted into second by Welshman Jamie Baulch. Sale's Kevin McKay used the craft gained over years of international competition to get ahead of Tom Lerwill in the 'eight' but we were piling up the points steadily and with 'bankers Neil Owen, Kevin Brown, Leith Marar, Mike Edwards and Fred Salle all winning - and decathlete Simon Shirley plugging any gaps - we eased away from our opponents. items.s: SC Veterans' T&F League Mid-London, Match 2, Battersea, 13 May 96 Report and results of the second Southern Counties Veterans' T&F League match at Battersea, where Belgrave men finished second to Serpentine and the women third. SC VETERANS' T&F LEAGUE MID-LONDON, MATCH 2 BATTERSEA, 13 MAY 96 The writing's on the wall. It was a close match and we had some good wins, especially in the M50s, but it looks as if there will be no 'A' final for the Bels this year. Not only would we have to beat Serpentine in each of the remaining matches but someone is also going to have to push them down to third in one of them and it just doesn't seem likely. But every cloud has a silver lining. The 'B' final is still a possibility and on this occasion we were able to welcome back two prodigal sons in Alan Painter and Derek Clack. They are both taking tentative steps at the moment but you know that Mr. Painter when he's got a sniff of a record. He's 50 next year and no doubt has Tony Stone's 800m record in his sights - as long as Leo Coy doesn't get to it first. items.s: Rosenheim League Match 1, Battersea Park, 15 May 96 Report and results of the first Rosenheim League match at Battersea Park, won by Belgrave, highlighted by Mike Edwards Jnr's UK-leading 5.45 pole vault. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE MATCH 1 BATTERSEA PARK, 15 MAY 96 The chilly conditions were no barrier to Mike Edwards Jnr. In gathering gloom he turned on one of the most spectacular performances ever seen at Battersea track. He'd come along on the Monday to support his dad in the Veterans T&F match, liked what he saw and decided there and then to have a crack at the Rosenheim on the Wednesday. Coming in at 4.90 (to win the competition) he then took 5.10 at his second attempt to remove club-mate Ian Tullet's name from the record books as ground record holder, and then went on to 5.25 (first time), 5.35 (third), 5.45 (second) for a UK leading mark for 1996 and then failing at 5.55 where his first try was oh! so close. It's one thing watching an international standard 'vault from the stadium at Crystal Palace but stand next to the uprights at track level when the bar is at near Olympic qualifying height and one really gets an idea of the courage of these guys. Spontaneous applause from the crowd on the long deserted 100m straight marked yet another of those magic Rosenheim moments. As a team we were clear winners, making an early claim on the trophy for a third consecutive year. 100m: 2, P.Goedluck 11.3; n/s 1, M.Livingstone 12.1; 2, C.Allen 12.1. 200m: 2, B.Williams 23.1; n/s 1, C.Smeal 24.2; 2, S.Hughes 26.0. 400m: 1, M.Parper 49.8; n/s 2, G.Taylor 54.6; 3, D.Akinbogun 58.2; 4, S.Smullen 60.0; 6, J.Stone (W) 63.8. 800m: 1, G.Adams 1:56.6. 1500m: 1, D.O'Riordan 4:14.1; n/s S.Beaver 4:41.1; D.Beaver 4:41.6. 3000m: 5, J.Galley 9:20.0; n/s P.Carstairs 9:42.1; S.Smullen 10:11.2. 400mH: 1, J.Squirrell 55.7. items.h: Avrupa Sampion Kulüpler Kupasi Atletizm — 22nd European Champion Club's Cup
items.sum: Leo Coy's report on the 22nd European Champion Clubs' Cup in Istanbul, where Belgrave placed 3rd, the best British placing ever outside the UK, with a club record 3:09.30 in the 4x400m relay.
items.s: Avrupa Sampion Kulüpler Kupasi Atletizm — 22nd European Champion Club's Cup Leo Coy's report on the 22nd European Champion Clubs' Cup in Istanbul, where Belgrave placed 3rd, the best British placing ever outside the UK, with a club record 3:09.30 in the 4x400m relay. AVRUPA SAMPION KULÜPLER KUPASI ATLETIZM 22nd European Champion Club's Cup Bels. 3rd - top British placing ever outside of the UK Dave Smith got our team off to a solid start in the Hammer. With Team Managers, supporters and team mates watching he caused a few flutters as he had three no-throws! But showing good experience for his age he put everything right in the 5th round with a mighty 68.80 to finish 5th. Jon Ridgeon made a welcome return to the team with 2nd place behind Samuel Matete in the 400m hurdles. Du'aine followed this with a casual win in the 400m flat and we were looking good. In the 100m Jason Fergus made his Club debut and was placed an excellent 4th. Richard Aspden produced a season's best in the High Jump but could only share 7th place in a very high standard competition. Similarly, for Derek Browne, the Triple was probably the strongest event overall and he had to settle for 8th. At this stage Larios were out in front with Fiamme Oro in second and we were vying with Racing Club for 3rd place. Matthew Yates ran an excellent 1500m and was just pipped on the line for 2nd while Darren Mead placed 6th with a good run in the 3000m and the sprint boys came through after a slow start to take 4th in the 4x100m relay. The Shot Putt was of a very high standard, the first three being over 19 metres, and Lee Newman did well to finish 5th. At the end of the day we were placed 4th behind Larios, Fiamme Oro and Racing Club. The team talk arranged for 11pm had to be held outside as our hotel was on fire but we were safe in the hands of Fireman and Captain Phil Goedluck! The message from Bill and John was that we had a real chance of finishing in 3rd place ahead of Racing Club, so knowing what we had to do, we went into day two. Nigel Bevan got us off to a great start with a first round effort of 74.36 and this proved to be the best throw of the competition to make Nigel our second individual winner. RCF were placed 7th and we had moved into 3rd! Andy Tulloch, making his first appearance for the Bels in place of an injured Neil Owen, got 4th in the high hurdles - but Racing Club were first. Haroun Korjie gave us another 4th in the 200m, ahead of our main rivals and then Matt Yates, doubling up by taking on the 800m, placed a solid 6th but more importantly kept ahead of the French challenge. On the field Kevin Brown had a good competition to get up to 5th in the Discus while Fred Salle was unlucky with three no-jumps in the last three rounds of the Long Jump where at least one of his leaps was over 8 metres. He ended up with another 4th but RCF had fought back with 1st! Olympic Champion Tarasov was waiting to enter the 'Vault as Mike Edwards went out but at least he shared the points equaly with RCF. Justin Chaston was next up in the 'Chase and he led Lambruschini until 600m out when the Italian kicked away - a great performance by Justin. Darren Mead had a really hard double by holding on to 6th in the 5000m after the previous day's 3k and just failed to catch the slowing RCF man. With one event to go we were a clear third ahead of Racing Club who now had a battle on their hands to stay fourth with Belarus and Dukla Prague close behind. Our finest moment came in the 4x400m relay. Tom Lerwill ran a storming leg on first, coming through late and handing over in third place - 48.0 seconds. Jon Ridgeon was next, holding second with a brilliant 46.8 before handing over to Chris Rawlinson who sat in 'til the last bend and then cruised through into the lead - 47.2. Now it was Dave Nolan leading all the way, giving the opposition no chance of catching him as he lengthened his lead down the straight - 46.9. A superb new Club Record of 3:09.30 which ensured third place overall and the best ever British performance in the European Clubs' Cup on Continental soil. It was a brilliant team effort, not only by those who competed but also by the reserves - Lewis Samuel, Roger Alsop and Leith Marar - the Team Managers - Bill and John - and the supporters. The noise generated while the long relay was in progress out-did every other team. Well done to Phil Goedluck and his fine team, a performance all the more creditable since the first two clubs are totally professional outfits sponsored by Larios Gin and the Italian Police Service respectively. The event ended with a banquet for all the teams at the Princess Hotel. The hosts arranged an excellent evening with beer and wine flowing in plenty, an authentic belly dancer and some traditional folk dancing. Belgrave received further awards: Du'aine got the best track runner award and our relay team won best team award for their 1st and 4th places. Derek Browne finished runner-up in the Euroclubs Belly Dancing competition with some lovely moves! A great end to an excellent weekend and the Belgrave Office will be decorated with still further pieces of silverware. But the most moving moment was yet to come. Watched by a coachload of his team mates Haroun said goodbye to his Turkish friend ... "Haroun, I love you!" It was a very touching moment as tears flowed from the love-lorn young lady's eyes - and from the eyes of thirty hysterical passengers! items.s: Southern League Division 3 Match 2, Southampton, 18 May 96 Report and results of Southern League Division 3 match 2 at Southampton, where Belgrave finished second to Harlow in miserable conditions. SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 MATCH 2 SOUTHAMPTON, 18 MAY 96 In the most miserable of conditions the chance of a second win just slipped out of our grasp. Incessant rain and a strong wind put paid to the pole vault competition before it began but Jamie Webb, rather than go all that way for nothing, turned out in the 'B' 400 hurdles and surprised himself by picking up a second place. Poor Mike Bazire probably wished the long jump had been cancelled as well. He had intended taking only one leap, for a few points, but paid for it by putting his back out and making it impossible for him to take any further part in the afternoon's activities - in turn bad news for Team Manager Bob who then had to fill in most of the blanks himself. Donal O'Riordan strained a thigh muscle in the 800 which meant no 1500 for him later on - it's easy to see how the 12½ points difference between ourselves and Harlow opened up. But there were some good performances to enthuse about as well. Richard David took advantage of the wind (no gauge!) to run a pb 100m, good jumping from Matt George, and Dave Beaver collecting most unaccustomed points for us in the 5k. Mike Small scored well in the throws with Ben Cascoe back in the team to help things along so all in all, not a bad team performance - and we've still got two matches at Battersea to come. 100m: 2, R.David 11.0; 2, M.Parper 11.6. 200m: 4, M.Parper 23.2; 1, B.Williams 22.7. 400m: 5, G.Taylor 56.7; 5, R.Bridges 77.2. 800m: 5, D.O'Riordan 2:06.3; 4, Mark Anderson 2:08.2. 1500m: 4, A.Luce 4:22.3. 5000m: 2, D.Beaver 16:28.7; 2, S.Chettati 16:49.8. 110mH: 2, M.George 15.7; 4, R.Bridges 28.6. 400mH: 2, A.Daniel 60.7; 2, J.Webb 70.9. 4x100m: 3, Belgrave 46.6. 4x400m: 2, Belgrave (G.Taylor 56.7, B.Williams 53.0, A.Daniel 54.2, R.David 51.2) 3:35.1. items.s: Rosenheim League Match 2, Tooting, 29 May 96 Report and results of the second Rosenheim League match at Tooting, won by Belgrave 17 points clear of Croydon. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE MATCH 2 TOOTING, 29 MAY 96 With five wins and six second places there was no stopping the Rosenheim team who finished 17 points clear of Croydon for a second match win. Donal O'Riordan bounced back from mild injury for the closest of victories in the 800m while for Jon Squirrel in the one lap race it was just too close for comfort: he got barged by the man supposed to be in the next lane out but actually in his own! Great running from Junior Galley who came through strongly over the last two laps in the 3k while Bruce Barton made his first competitive track appearance of the season in the steeplechase. As usual we had several juniors competing alongside senior colleagues and Michael Parper came up with a pb 22.4 in the 200m which augurs well for 400m races to come. Peter Waterman putts a mean 7.26kg shot for a sixteen year-old and is busy working his way through our age-group records while James Hilston restricted himself to the high jump while recovering from shin splints (in his non-take-off leg). 100m: 2, R.David 11.2; n/s a 1, B.Williams 11.1; 2, M.Livingstone 11.6 n/s b 2, D.Akinbogun 12.0. 200m: 3, M.Parper 22.4; n/s a 2, P.Turner 23.5; n/s b 3, C.Husbands 25.5. 400m: 1, J.Squirrel 49.6; n/s 1, G.Taylor 54.2; 5, J.Stone (W) 65.6. 800m: 1, D.O'Riordan 1:59.5; n/s 2, M.Anderson 2:01.9; 3, S.Smullen 2:05.5; 4, A.Luce 2:05.6. 1500m: 2, D.Beaver 4:21.7. 3000m: 2, J.Galley 9:01.7; n/s C.Dickinson 9:23.9; S.Beaver 10:18.8. 2000mSC: 2, B.Barton 6:39.0. 4x200m: 1, Belgrave (M.Livingstone, G.Taylor, C.Husbands, B.Williams) 1:35.8.
