items.label: February 1997
items.h: Lerwill wins silver in World Champs.
items.sum: Account of Tom Lerwill's 800m silver and 4x400m relay run at the World Junior Championships in Sydney, from Clive Shippen who attended each day.
items.s: Lerwill wins silver in World Champs. Account of Tom Lerwill's 800m silver and 4x400m relay run at the World Junior Championships in Sydney, from Clive Shippen who attended each day. Track & Field Clive Shippen attended each day of the World Junior Championships in Sydney. I was very impressed: one could almost see him maturing during the championships themselves. In the first round he finished a comfortable second to 'British' rival James Nolan of Ireland whose pb was 1.38 secs faster than Tom's 1:49.18. In the second round he really turned on the pace; he had to, because he was up against Kenya's Japhet Kimutai (a name to watch) who stormed to a 1:45.63 win. But Tom chased him home with great fervour to clock a brilliant pb of 1:47.27 - a huge cut off his previous best. Nolan was behind him this time in 4th. What a joy it was on day three to see a Briton in the final of the 800 metres; such a change these days. And what a change it was to see that man get a medal, and especially the way he won it. The formidable Kenyan took the field through 200m in 24.93 and I was relieved to see Tom show restraint and slip into a trouble-free 7th. At the bell (53.34) he moved out and went into 6th, and down the back straight ran with power to reach 4th at 600 (1:21.12). Round the final bend he was nicely positioned and went to 3rd entering the straight. It was another Kenyan Mwengi Mutua who now moved away to win as the favourite Kimutai faded to 4th but Tom dug deep, kept his form beautifully and to the chagrin of the home crowd eased past Australian Grant Cremer to secure the silver medal. His time of 1:48.40 did not match that lightning fast semi but it was the way that he ran the race that impressed me. Many Juniors are impetuous at this level: they get caught up in the intensity and passion of the occasion. But Tom looked as cool as a cucumber as he ran his own first 300 metres. I also liked the strength of his running (lacking from the present crop of British runners) and his tactical sense. It was an outstanding performance and Belgrave have good cause to be proud of him. Result: 1, M.Mutua (Kenya) 1:48.21; 2, T.Lerwill (GB) 1:48.40; 3, G.Cremer (Australia) 1:48.46. Tom's efforts did not finish there as he was second runner in the 4x400 metres team. I was not too optimistic as none of the British 400m and 400m hurdles runners had reached their finals. However, they chased the Americans hard to finish second in their heat and nearly did the same in the final, except that Japan snatched the silver. What a tradition Britain has in this event: everyone seems to run above themselves. Again Tom was impressive. He took that awkward second leg where no one seems to know where they are until the break occurs on the back straight. Two runners shot past him but again he showed admirable control, overtook them both and finished very strongly to hand over in 3rd place which the team held to the finish. So he ran five quality races in five days. Watch out Kenyans. items.sum: Tony Jarrett had to name Belgrave hurdlers Andy Tulloch and Jon Ridgeon to score on BBC's Question of Sport.
items.s: Belgrave hurdlers earn Jarrett his points Tony Jarrett had to name Belgrave hurdlers Andy Tulloch and Jon Ridgeon to score on BBC's Question of Sport. Haringey's international hurdler Tony Jarrett was guest competitor on BBC's Question of Sport recently but he was forced to utter the names of Belgrave hurdlers to earn his points on the programme. In the video footage the name of the A.A.A. 110m Hurdles Champion for 1994 was required: answer - Andy Tulloch. And then for his home and away question "Who won a A.A.A. hurdle race 9 years after winning his first?" Answer - Jon Ridgeon. items.sum: Note that Adidas Running Team has signed the Cuban stars who competed for Spanish club Larios in the European Clubs championship.
items.s: Larios lose their stars Note that Adidas Running Team has signed the Cuban stars who competed for Spanish club Larios in the European Clubs championship. For some years now the European Clubs T&F Championship has been dominated by the Spanish Club Larios (Larios being Spain's top selling gin). With a huge budget the club were able to set up a deal whereby a great majority of Cuba's international team were able to perform in the Spanish club's colours. However, Adidas Running Team have now signed up the Cuban stars and for good measure have taken on board a couple of top Spaniards as well. It will be interesting to see if Larios now stay in the sport - if they don't then the European Clubs event becomes just that little bit more open. items.label: February 1997
items.h: AAA Championships & Olympic Trials, Birmingham 14-16 Jun 1996
items.sum: Report and Belgrave results from the AAA Championships and Olympic Trials at Birmingham, 14-16 June 1996, with wins for John Regis, Jon Ridgeon, Justin Chaston and Dave Smith.
items.s: AAA Championships & Olympic Trials, Birmingham 14-16 Jun 1996 Report and Belgrave results from the AAA Championships and Olympic Trials at Birmingham, 14-16 June 1996, with wins for John Regis, Jon Ridgeon, Justin Chaston and Dave Smith. The chase for places on Britain's team for Atlanta was on with a vengeance at the Olympic Trials at Birmingham's Alexander Stadium and the event surrounded by the most hype was that 400 metres. Dave Nolan ran 46.48 in his heat and then 46.68 in the semi - but one really needed to go sub-46 to get into the final, such was the high standard. Du'aine Ladejo went out hard, as did the Welshman Iwan Thomas but Roger Black was in the form of his life and coming strongly off the bend he came through for a British Record 44.39 while Ladejo had to be content with 2nd in a personal (and Club) best of 44.66. Thomas and Baulch also ducked well under 45 seconds in this classiest ever British one-lap race. John Regis had to dig deep and use every ounce of his strength to stay a millimetre or two ahead of Christie to take the 200m - both were given the same time to the hundredth. Vaulters Edwards and Tullett gained 3rd and 4th places but with Crawley's Buckfield setting a British Best of 5.71m to win, no-one else was going to be Atlanta bound unless they exceeded the qualifying mark. The same sort of fate befell Kevin Brown, 3rd in the Discus as Birchfield's big Bob Weir went over 60m but Hammer thrower Dave Smith confirmed his number one standing this season with another throw over 72 metres. Paul Evans, already selected for an event he did not want to do in the Olympics - the marathon - gave the selectors the option to slot him into the 10,000m by getting into the frame and Andy Tulloch also booked his ticket in the high hurdles while Neil Owen missed out by 2/100ths of a second and two places. Justin Chaston fought off the tenacious Keith Cullen to take the steeplechase but the parade event for the Bels was the 400m hurdles. No fewer than three of our club-men had made it through to the final: Rawlinson, Levy and Ridgeon, and this in spite of the fact that they had already all faced each other in the same semi-final. Down the back stretch the claret and gold colours were reduced by a third when Noel Levy, a great talent at only 21 years of age, hit a hurdle badly and took an almighty tumble. Ex-Gladiators contestant Chris Rawlinson held on as well as he could but could not quite match his semi-final time while Jon Ridgeon showed that he was the absolute master of the race. items.h: The 1996 Olympic Games, Atlanta, 26 Jul - 4 Aug 1996
items.sum: Review of the seven Belgravians at the Atlanta 1996 Olympic Games, with round-by-round results.
items.s: The 1996 Olympic Games, Atlanta, 26 Jul - 4 Aug 1996 Review of the seven Belgravians at the Atlanta 1996 Olympic Games, with round-by-round results. Atlanta Braves Seven Belgravians made it to the Olympic Games, a tremendous achievement. Justin Chaston, Paul Evans and Andy Tulloch all managed to produce their season's best performances at just the right time - you can't ask much more than that - while Jon Ridgeon was only just outside his best for the year and with good health and a full winter's preparation may well improve yet on his life-time best of 48.73 come the 1997 World Champs. Andy Tulloch's 13.56 was only a shade outside his best ever run and made him the new Belgrave sprint hurdles record holder. John Regis must have been a bit disappointed. He was unable to get back to the level of the early season form that he had shown in South Africa and for such a be-medalled athlete not to reach the final was galling. Also disappointed was Du'aine Ladejo who looked totally out of sorts and could not get near his 44.66 from the AAA Champs. Our giant Hammer thrower Dave Smith had his work cut out. Faced with a phalanx of Eastern Europeans who can heave their implement over 75 metres as a matter of course, Dave had to at least replicate his best of 75.10m to stand a chance of reaching the final and to be sure, had to beat the standard of 76.50m. This time around the feat was beyond him but for this young man Atlanta must be seen as a learning experience and future Games are sure to see him become Britain's best ever hammer thrower. No medals then - but how proud we are to have seen seven of our number compete in the Greatest Show on Earth. items.h: Match 2, Copthall, 9 Jun 1996: Somehow we salvage 3rd place
items.sum: Report and results of British Athletics League Division One match 2 at Copthall on 9 June 1996, where Belgrave recovered to finish third.
items.s: Match 2, Copthall, 9 Jun 1996: Somehow we salvage 3rd place Report and results of British Athletics League Division One match 2 at Copthall on 9 June 1996, where Belgrave recovered to finish third. British Athletics League Division One Somehow we salvage 3rd place We entered this local fixture still reeling from the 8 point defeat handed to us by newly promoted Sale Manchester in Match 1. Liverpool had virtually been a home fixture for them and we wondered how well they would travel away from home. Despite the loss of big point scorers Dave Nolan, Neil Owen and Chris Rawlinson to an International match in Estonia, we felt confident that we had retained enough fire power to shake the opposition. The feeling of confidence evaporated almost as soon as the match began. The first disaster saw Fred Salle pull up lame in the long jump run up and he retired without a single leap. Soon after Richard Aspden decided to open at 2.05m in in the high jump and failed to record a height. Multi-eventer, Simon Shirley became the 'A' string in both events and despite good performance we were suddenly 40 points down on the team manager's forecast. Languishing in an unlikely 7th spot up to half way it looked as though we had blown our league chances completely. Strong performances in the 800m and 1500m by Matt Yates in his UK track debut for Belgrave, plus the usual solid performances by all our throws squad brought a semblance of respectability to our score. Maximum points in the vault and solid relay performances saw us creep into 3rd spot - two places ahead of Sale. In the end we finished just 17½ points behind winners Birchfield, who moved into the lead position as we turned our thoughts to Match 3. 100m: (-2.0) 6, J.Fergus 10.87; (-0.9) 1, H.Korjie 10.70. 200m: (-4.2) 5, L.Samuel 22.18; (-5.0) 1, A.Walcott 21.71. 400m: 4, M.Kloiber 49.12; 5, P.Beaumont 50.51. 800m: 1, M.Yates 1:50.10; 3, D.Pamah 1:52.83. 1500m: 5, D.Pamah 3:53.73; 1, M.Yates 3:55.59. 5000m: 6, K.Tadesse 15:07.42. 5, J.Estall 15:37.21. 110mH: (-1.1) 4, I.Wells 15.84; (-2.3) 5, L.Antoine 16.24. 400mH: 6, P.Beaumont 56.55; 6, I.Wells 56.16. 3000mSC: 8, M.Bizio 10:22.2; 6, M.Hillier 10:24.8. items.h: Alexander Stadium, Birmingham, 6 Jul 1996: And now its all to play for
items.sum: Report and results of British Athletics League Division One match 3 at Birmingham on 6 July 1996, where Belgrave were third on the day and stayed second in the league.
items.s: Alexander Stadium, Birmingham, 6 Jul 1996: And now its all to play for Report and results of British Athletics League Division One match 3 at Birmingham on 6 July 1996, where Belgrave were third on the day and stayed second in the league. And now its all to play for With Birchfield now heading the league and Match 3 being a home fixture for the Birmingham based Club, we put out a 5 line whip in an effort to get maximum support. Our policy is to get as many of the team into a local hotel the night before to minimise the risk of the 'day trippers' not arriving . The first event proved a huge success with Atlanta bound Dave Smith and throws Captain Phil Spivey getting maximum points in the hammer. Geoffrey Ojok couldn't get his run up right in the long jump and failed to make the cut, while Birchfield gained a one two with the help of super vet Barrington Williams. This was followed by the first track event, the 400 hurdles, and so depleted were we that Neil Owen ran the 'B' leg. Rumour had it that he had been doing some over distance training which seemed to pay off until he hit the home straight. His 55.12 was a good début but below his expectations however, and he swore - never again. The start was depressingly familiar but the 800m raised spirits. Tom Lerwill showed tactical awareness and a kick which belied his youth. So effective was he that he held off Olympics bound Kevin McKay for a fine win and a notable scalp. Matt Kloiber showed that he was over his illness problems with a solid 3rd spot in the 'B' race. The short sprint got the experts reaching for their rule books as both Andrew Walcott and Birchfield's Michael Rosswess were disqualified for two false starts. Interesting! But no points. Marlon Dickson ran a PB to finish second in the 'B' race and into a headwind! Better points in the 3000m steeplechase, excellent results in the discus and a win in the high hurdles from a tired Neil Own saw a revival of fortunes. Ian Wells once again stepped into the 'B' 110 hurdles as it became apparent that our scheduled hurdler was still in London. (How did we get on without mobile phones?) From there on, the only wins were Lee Newman in the 'B' discus, Nigel Bevan in the 'A' javelin and a rather tasty victory in the long relay. We had been picking up good points in some events and losing them in others. No 'B' runner in the 1500m showed how difficult it was for us to find an uninjured middle distance man able to make the start line. So once again, third place on the day and we remained second in the League with, surprise, surprise, Sale moving back into the lead on 20 league points and three teams close behind on 19. What should have been a win could so easily have been a disaster and yet the team fought for every point to give us a reasonable chance of success going into the last match - a home fixture to boot! 100m: A.Walcott dq.; (-0.5) 2, M.Dickson 10.65; 200m: (+2.1) 3, A.Walcott 21.18; (+2.1) 4, M.Dickson 21.79; 400m: 2, D.Nolan 46.87; 3, L.Samuel 48.29. 800m: 1, T.Lerwill 1:49.18; 3, M.Kloiber 1:54.36. 1500m: 5, D.Pamah 3:51.65. 5000m: 5, K.Tadesse 14:55.90; 4, D.Mead 15:27.74. 110mH: (+1.0) 1, N.Owen 14.07; (+1.4) 6, I.Wells 15.82. 400mH: 7, I.Wells 56.08; 4, N.Owen 55.12. 3000mSC: 2, D.Mead 9:07.69; 4, B.Barton 9:57.37. items.h: Match 4, Kingsmeadow, 17 Aug 1996: Over the moon ... then sick as parrots
items.sum: Report and results of the final British Athletics League Division One match at Kingsmeadow on 17 August 1996: Belgrave won the match but lost the league title to Sale by 3 points after a scoring correction.
items.s: Match 4, Kingsmeadow, 17 Aug 1996: Over the moon ... then sick as parrots Report and results of the final British Athletics League Division One match at Kingsmeadow on 17 August 1996: Belgrave won the match but lost the league title to Sale by 3 points after a scoring correction. British Athletics League Division One Over the moon ... then sick as parrots This was it. A home fixture and the big one. We knew that any one of four teams could still win the league. With our strongest middle distance squad since the heady days of entering the league 14 years ago, we knew we were in with a shout. All we had to do was beat Sale by 12 points and we would be representing the UK in the European Clubs Championship again next year. The start went to plan. Maximum points in the hammer, a weak 'B' long jump and an excellent high jump with Richard Aspden taking the 'A' event plus an injured 400 hurdler in the form of Chris Rawlinson finishing second in the 'B' high jump. Chris, unable to run his specialist 400 hurdles for much of the season also scored valuable points in the high hurdles and long relay. Dave Nolan eased round in the single lap doing just enough to win the 400, nursing a split ankle bone which was to require surgery a fortnight later. Junior Michael Parper excelled in his first league appearance and should have finished second in the 'B' 400m but was impeded by the starter standing in his lane in the finishing straight. Matt Yates had two fine wins in the 'A' 800m and 1500m, while Paul Evans stamped his mark on the 1500m and 5000m, running in with Gary Staines in the latter event. Add to this the dream team of Justin Chaston and Darren Mead in the 3000m steeplechase and you can see that a middle distance squad doesn't come much better than this. Added to our injury woes was Kevin Brown. Kevin who has been such a loyal and enthusiastic addition to our throws squad insisted on throwing despite injury. Leith Marar took advantage to throw a season's best (until the Cup Final), and Kevin who also competed in the shot was destined for major surgery a week later. Ian Tullett was sidelined from the pole vault, yet another key man awaiting surgery. With so many of the team giving and willing to give 110%, the few non-appearances throughout the season were thrown into sharp perspective as the rest of the team roared on every effort. By the last event, the announcer had declared Belgrave clear victors. Dave Nolan was dropped from the long relay to prevent further damage to his leg and we gracefully received the trophy, the accolades and commiserated with Sale. The Sale team had just boarded their coach when an embarrassed League Secretary dropped the bombshell. The pole vault had been misscored, the Sale 'B' competitor's score had been omitted. Yes, Belgrave were still match winners but only by 8 points. We had failed to overhaul Sale's accumulative score by a mere 3 points. President Snowy Brooks was gracious as he presented the now jubilant Sale squad with that League Trophy. items.h: Semi-Final, Wavertree, Liverpool, 28 Jul 1996: Demented "Wellsey" saves the day!
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's Guardian Insurance Gold Cup semi-final at Wavertree, Liverpool, on 28 July 1996, where a timetable mix-up nearly cost the team; Belgrave finished second behind Sale.
items.s: Semi-Final, Wavertree, Liverpool, 28 Jul 1996: Demented "Wellsey" saves the day! Report and results of Belgrave's Guardian Insurance Gold Cup semi-final at Wavertree, Liverpool, on 28 July 1996, where a timetable mix-up nearly cost the team; Belgrave finished second behind Sale. Guardian Insurance Gold Cup Demented "Wellsey" saves the day! Our second visit within 2 months to Wavertree Athletics Centre, Liverpool, nearly proved a disaster. But as usual Ian Wells helped to save the day. This time as self appointed team manager. (Another event to add to his ever growing list. ) So what happened? Well ... the team travelled up the day before and enjoyed a leisurely breakfast before the advance squad set off for the track. As Bill Laws' car entered the car park a demented figure in claret and gold flung himself on the bonnet. "I've entered Phil Spivey - they're in to the second round of the hammer. Better move quick." As the timetable which Belgrave had received indicated the hammer was not due to start for 1½ hours, this was greeted with some derision. But Ian's demeanour bordering on the manic, put a quick end to the frivolity. Phil Spivey, Throws Captain and Mister Unflappable, moved purposely to the circle. He wasn't there to mess about and two rounds later he took the lead for maximum points. So what had gone wrong? After much scratching around it appeared that we had been sent the timetable for the second round fixture, which was considerably different from the one for the semi. A quick scurry back to the hotel to mobilise the rest of the team had some effect although a few were still sightseeing. Back to the track and disaster was averted - well nearly. Unfortunately, we hadn't got the message to Jim Estall who arrived for the 10,000m as the leaders entered their 3rd lap. After agitated protests Jim was allowed to run, but was not allowed to score. Our protest was not upheld. Soon after, Mike Edwards no heighted in the Pole Vault - thankfully a rare happening - but the tension grew. Neil Owen and Chris Rawlinson swapped the long and sprint hurdles due to Chris' continuing injury which meant he only had one good lead leg. Both scored good points with Chris' win being a bonus. Solid performances from the rest of our regulars helped us move into second place and a chance to put matters right in the Cup Final itself. items.h: Final, Copthall, 31 Aug 1996: A golden finish to the season
items.sum: Report and results of the 1996 Guardian Insurance Gold Cup Final at Copthall on 31 August 1996, Belgrave's third Cup win.
items.s: Final, Copthall, 31 Aug 1996: A golden finish to the season Report and results of the 1996 Guardian Insurance Gold Cup Final at Copthall on 31 August 1996, Belgrave's third Cup win. A golden finish to the season After 20 years sponsoring the British Athletics Leagues and Cup Competitions, this was to be Guardian Assurance's last match. The 1996 Gold Cup Final was to be a special event and with little sign of further financial support, we wondered what the future format would be. So everyone was determined to make it a big occasion and, once again, thanks to the wholehearted support of our middle distance squad, we triumphed for our third Cup win. Pride of place went to our distance men with wins by Matt Yates, Justin Chaston, Paul Evans and Gary Staines. Neil Owen blew the opposition away for another 110mH victory. Junior Geoffrey Ojok had a remarkable victory over Linford Christie, not unfortunately in the 100m, but in Linford's new event - the long jump. We're not quite certain how TVH's specialist jumper felt as he watched Linford struggle to 6.67m, but we do know that Geoffrey was determined to gain his scalp even if he himself was finding it difficult to hit his correct stride patten Linford made amends in the 100m with a new Cup record of 10.28 secs, but the Man of the Match Award went to Bob Weir of Birchfield who broke the Cup discus record with an impressive 62.40. Leith Marar threw a season's best to gain an impressive second place. Once again, our Young Athletes made an impressive contribution with Richard David easing his way to 48.85 in the flat 400m. Philip Idowu looked tired at the end of a tong season but Marlon Dickson looked better than ever, running both relays. Even he was surprised how easy a 49.1 leg felt. So, victory to the Bels with a comfortable 9 points margin over Woodford Green. We had expected Newham & Essex to be the main threat but Woodford had been recruiting strongly. After several years where they have floated between Divisions 1 and 2, they now look like a force to be reckoned with. Sale slumped to 5th, clearly unable to raise their game after their league victory, and Haringey, who had been relegated to Division 2 for 1997 suffered the ignominy of finishing last. 100m: (+1.3) 7, H.Korjie 10.73. 200m: (+0.6) 7, A.Walcott 21.81. 400m: 5, R.David 48.85. 800m: 2, M.Yates 1:52.29. 1500m: 1, M.Yates 3:49.81. 5000m: 1, P.Evans 13:53.23. 10000m: 1, G.Staines 29:40.4. 110mH: (+1.0) 1, N.Owen 14.00. 400mH: 6, I.Wells 55.41. 3000mSC: 1, J.Chaston 8:47.6. Over the last few years our Heavy Squad has provided the muscle from which a series of League and Cup title wins have developed. Last year Dave Smith and Lee Newman were welcome additions, while at the tail end of the 1996 season Matt Simson joined Belgrave to further strengthen an already impressive throws squad. Their contribution to our League and Cup successes may be judged from the following table which aggregates League Div. 1 points for A and B strings and then divides the totals by the maximum possible points to give the % performance and hence Ranking positions. The sprint and long relays are limited to 1 event each per Match, so that the maximum points possible for these events in 1 season are 64, while all other events could score 112 maximum. This is worked out on the basis that an A String win is worth 16 points and a B String win 12 points. For budding statisticians the complete scoring for a British League fixture is as follows :- A String: 16,14,12,10,8,6,5,4. B String: 12,10, 8, 6,4,3,2,1. It's great to have such people as Gill Fairclough to rely upon. Gill has been associated with Belgrave for many years, husband Tony being one of our star cross country runners from the '60s. Both Gill and Tony have gone on to put something back into the sport and do a great deal of officiating, particularly in Kent. At our home McDonald's YA Meeting at Crystal Palace Gill took on the arduous role of Field Events Referee while Tony was Track Ref. What would we have done without them? items.s: Men's Southern League Divisions 3 & 6 Report on Belgrave's 1996 men's Southern League season, with promotion won from Division Three at the final Bracknell match and the Division Six team abandoned, followed by Belgrave results from six matches; Division 3 Match 6 prints M.Small's JT and HT marks both as 41.08?. With a mostly young team our Southern Leaguers maintained a high position in Division Three throughout the summer . We say mostly young but where would we be without veteran Mike Small who regularly wins just about every throw going, setting veteran personal and club bests into the bargain. Things got a little harder as the season progressed and we lost sprinter Marlon Dickson, vaulter Jamie Webb and 400 flat and hurdles man Jon Squirrell to the British League team but to be honest, this just gave some of the younger men a chance to show their mettle - and they grasped the chance. Going down to Bracknell for the final match we needed 1st or 2nd team spot to clinch promotion. It wasn't made easier when Team Manager Bob Bridges went sick on the day. We abandoned our Division Six team entirely at this point as Don Anderson stepped in as Team Boss. Approaching the relays our boys felt they had done enough for the day in the hot sun and incredibly, with a match win and promotion beckoning, it looked as if we would fail to turn out a 4x400 squad. A quick chase round by Pat Mead rounded up a somewhat less than enthusiastic team who donned their spikes while Kenny Pereira occupied our lane and held up the event - much to the annoyance of the officials. They might not have wanted to do it but our lads ended up with a fine win with Richard David running a cracking 48.2 for the last leg. The match was ours. Promotion was secured and a sick Bob was 'phoned up and given the news. As we have said, we abandoned the Division Six team at the end. It had been a great struggle to fill out a team for much of the time - although we do have quite a few vets and youngsters who enjoy competing for our third team. The penalty for failing to fill out 50% of the events is an automatic drop of two divisions so it's Division Eight in '97 for the old boys. There is an advantage here, however. It's only one per event in Division Eight so things should be a little easier to organise here while our second team launches an attack on Division Two with the aim of going back to the first division in '98. items.s: Women's Southern League Div. 3 Report on Belgrave's 1996 women's Southern League Division Three season, in which the team stayed in Division Three, with Belgrave results from matches 2 to 6 and three captioned photos. After a win at home in match 1 hopes were high that we could maintain our effort and at last gain promotion from Division Three. Not to be. After several seasons of being short of under 15s, at Hayes and Sutcliffe Park we suddenly found ourselves scratching around for seniors to fill out the team and paid the penalty with two 4th places. It was a different story for match 4 at Aldershot. Sprinter Sabrina Scott turned out while in the 3,000 metres we were treated to a dominating run from Samantha Northey as she ran away from the combined Division One and Six fields to win by a street. Success wasn't confined to the seniors either as Debbie Hearn and Rebecca Lester both came from behind to outkick the rest of the runners in their 800m races. In the end four points covered the first three teams and it was 2nd for the "Belles". Two matches to go and we were slowly dragging ourselves back up the league table. At the Royal Navy track at Portsmouth our throwers were in good form with 16 year-old Michelle Stock winning the 'A' discus and 'B' shot, and Angela Patten and Gail Richardson also scoring good points. Andrea Abrams took charge of the long jump and Natalie Law and Sabrina Scott were unbeaten in both sprints and relays. Try as they could though, the under 15s were unable to come up with any wins this time, and we were 3rd team on the day. Holidays took their toll for the final match at home and wins were few and far between. Two victories that did stand out were Sam Northey's Under 17 3000m Club Record followed by her 1500m performance. Even spectating British League 800m/1500m man Dave Pamah was impressed! And so we stay where we are for another year. Jacqui Smiter has survived her first year as Joint Team Manager and we now set our sights on 1997. Can we get up to Division Two this time? items.sum: Report on Belgrave's promotion-winning 1996 National Junior League season, including the National Record 4x400m at Woodford, with results from matches 2 to 4 and two captioned photos; the first line of match 3 results is printed above its heading.
items.s: Men's National Junior League - Southern Area Division 2 Report on Belgrave's promotion-winning 1996 National Junior League season, including the National Record 4x400m at Woodford, with results from matches 2 to 4 and two captioned photos; the first line of match 3 results is printed above its heading. If ever there was a team going places then this is the one. Many of our Junior Men's team have been with us since they were 13 or 14 and now they are doing battle as under 20s, a good percentage of them with another season to go in the same age group. With promotion in two successive years we go into 1997 in Division One with a real chance to make a name for ourselves. Each of the matches, with one notable exception, was won by an avalanche of points. Not surprising really when you consider that some of these guys handle themselves with distinction in British League matches, so so lining up against Division Two Juniors enabled them to make mincemeat of the opposition. At each meeting a "Man of the Match" award is made and on occasions a choice had to be made from five or six Belgravians who had turned in eye-opening performances; 10.8 hundreds, 21.9 200s, 48 second 400s, 1:51 800s, 15 metre triple jumps, low 14 sprint hurdle runs, the list goes on and on. One man who didn't get a man of the match award was Marlon Dickson but for most supporters he was the "Man of the Season" as he scorched to win after win. Continuing his success from match 1 he went on to score doubles in each of the remaining meets with 10.9/22.0, 10.8/21.7 and 10.9/21.9 not to mention having a large part to play in the relay teams. Our ancient sprint relay record went in match 1 and at Tooting it was the turn of the 4x400m to go the same way as Michael Parper and Richard David both went sub-50 for their individual splits. Michael had already impressed with his 48.9 individual win while Steve Scott's 14.3 sprint hurdles victory took him to the top of the national rankings for the year. But it was Phillip Idowu's performance that was rated most highly as he leapt out to 15 metres for the second week in a row. Woodford was the one exception teamwise. A poor turnout left gaping holes in our team which in turn led to only 3rd team place but there was plenty to savour in the way of record performances. Tom Lerwill made an appearance before setting off for Sydney and the World Junior Championships. First up he cruised to a relaxed 800m win which at 1:51.5 was just a tenth shy of the National League Record. Later his 48.2 400m equalled the league best but it was the long relay that was most eagerly anticipated as we had gathered together James Hilston, Richard David and Michael Parper to join with Tom in a crack at the 4x400m record. Of course some of these lads are no mean sprinters over the 'hundred' and first they wanted to hand out some stick in the short relay. Steve Scott blasted leg one and overtook each man outside him before handing on to James who ... popped his hamstring as he took the baton! For an instant his instinct was to run on ... but he fell ... while the last two runners stood and waited for a baton that never came. Now what? With one of our key men clutching an ice pack to his thigh in the St. John's hut we were a man short ... or were we. We had reckoned without the courage of Marlon Dickson. Having already recorded his normal double he was now the natural choice to stand in for James. He wanted to do it, but never having run a 400 in anger before you can imagine his feelings as he was talked into running lap one. With dry mouth went to his mark and when the starter's pistol sent the runners away we knew that record was on again as Marlon kept his speed in check but flowed to a marvellous 49.2. What a debut - and he must have two to three seconds more under the bonnet! With an already enormous lead Richard David and Michael Parper stretched it still further and when Tom Lerwill finished with 47.6 for his stint that National Record had been blown away by SIX WHOLE SECONDS! With a virtually full team for the final meeting at Battersea it was win after win throughout the afternoon. In circumstances like this it is difficult to pick out special performances for mention - but here's two. Peter McDonald took miles out of his best 3000 metre time as he ran 9:24.3 (and still had the 'chase to come) and Joe Panton, always good for a low 52 400m, tried his hand at the two lap race and timed it to perfection as he turned on his speed in the finish straight to record a winning first ever attempt at the event. Well done boys. We await the '97 season with bated breath. items.sum: Report on Belgrave's unbeaten 1996 Rosenheim League season, ending in a narrow win over Herne Hill in the final to keep the Rosenheim Plate, with a captioned photo and results from matches 3 to 6 and the final.
items.s: Rosenheim League Report on Belgrave's unbeaten 1996 Rosenheim League season, ending in a narrow win over Herne Hill in the final to keep the Rosenheim Plate, with a captioned photo and results from matches 3 to 6 and the final. Winning streak stretches to ten! Coming out of match 3 at Wimbledon Park with a third straight win and a five point buffer over the next best team, thoughts began to centre on the possibility of our Rosenheim Raiders taking the series right through the summer without loss. Could it be done? The later matches are the more difficult ones though and great persuasion has to be used to get our team to the unpopular venues of Croydon and Sutton. Wimbledon saw some super sprinting and Mike Edwards tucked away another ground record when he cleared 4.85 for a n/s pole vault. It was also good to see that a small nucleus of our Women's Team were beginning to keep the lads company and tackle the non-scoring events. On to Croydon then. It might not be our most favourite venue - but then the other clubs didn't seem to like it much either and once again our team took their match tally over 60 points for win number four. Ben Williams collected a fine sprint double and Mike Small, as usual, kept things ticking over in the throws. For Jonathon Squirrell it was a chance to show what he can do in his favourite event - the 400m hurdles and he stormed round for a clear win. At Sutton Arena it was Richard David's turn to notch up a sprint double while Gavin Mason returned to the team to collect top points in the 400m. Gerry Adams had a crack at an unfamilar event when he lined up for the 2000m 'chase - not sure that he really enjoyed himself but it was more points in the bag as we cruised on to team win number five. So ... to the final Eastern Division match at Tooting. Had any Club ever won every match in a season? Herne Hill's Kevin Kelly assured us that it had been done before - so we needn't worry ourselves on that score! The match got under way and James Hilston had a remarkable run in the 100m. He was left for dead when it appeared there had been a false start and he only belatedly began running after standing up and then realising that there would be no recall. How he got up to 2nd we'll never know. Only four individual wins this time but how nice to get a Belgravian home first in the 3000 metres as Roger Alsop did everything right during his 7½ lap stint. You'd have thought that 17 year-old Marlon Dickson's 21.6 200m had to be the event of the evening but something special was being planned by our Junior Men. James Hilston, Richard David and Michael Parper teamed up with Marlon to turn on one of the best 4x200m relays ever seen. Averaging 21.97 per man they ran clean away from the opposition and just kept on going. Remember they are all Juniors but their final time of 1:27.9 was just a watch's tick over the league record and will surely be the fastest club time of the year. It was a Junior Club Record by over three seconds. And so we'd done it. Six out of six. But the real battle was to come. All summer long Stan Allen had been saying that Herne Hill's aim was just to reach the final and one had the feeling that now they'd got there they were gearing themselves to teach the Bels a thing or two. Essentially our team had been the usual mix of talented Under 20s, a couple of veterans and a couple of seniors on the verge of breaking out of the Southern League and into the BAL team. We went into the final with the same mix and found some very unfamiliar faces drafted into the opposing teams. Again Richard David took the 100m but it was the 400m where he really impressed. Running in the non-scoring race he blitzed to 48.7. Dave Pamah provided more front running in the two lap event as he totally ignored the field and made it hot and fast all the way - let the others hang on if they could. We had struggled to find a high jumper for the meet but James Hilston, carrying a ham-string injury, had no thought of us losing any points. The injury was not to his take-off leg and he felt he'd be able to do himself justice. Justice? He equalled the league record with a mighty 2 metre leap! There was drama too in the triple jump where Mat George was having a disastrous evening. It was neck and neck with Herne Hill so every single point counted - and Mat, expected to be fairly well up there, had a series that read: foul, foul, foul, rubbish, foul. Some quiet encouragement from the Team Manager and wallop - 13.28 and second place. Our big man Mike Small made his way from throw to throw, picking up two second places but it was all very, very tight. As Division Winners we had taken a 4 point advantage into the final and as it turned out, we eventually won by just that margin. Herne Hill had matched us for every point on the night and had even scored as many wins as we had. But the Rosenheim Plate was ours for another year. Seven wins out of seven in 1996 and ten in a row all told. There's no way the other local clubs are going to take that lying down in '97! Twenty-one times Race Walker Laura Fryer caused us to go to the record lists to mark up yet another best but the top score went to Peter Waterman. Seven times he improved his Under 17 Men's hammer mark finishing up with 58.16. But competing in Southern Senior and Junior Leagues he set a further sixteen records with heavier weights in shot and hammer to end up with the top tally of twenty-three records. items.label: February 1997
items.h: Don't be surprised when Michael Johnson runs under 43 seconds
items.sum: Bob Bridges sets out his rule of thumb for 400m pacing from 200m bests and argues it shows Michael Johnson could run under 43 seconds.
items.s: Don't be surprised when Michael Johnson runs under 43 seconds Bob Bridges sets out his rule of thumb for 400m pacing from 200m bests and argues it shows Michael Johnson could run under 43 seconds. To start off with it might be an idea to go to the spare room, root through that pile of athletics magazines lying in the corner, and dig out Athletics Weekly for August 21st 1996. Turn to pages 32 and 33 to read Play The Percentages Game by 400 metre coach Mike Smith - and now read on. ... The one thing missing from the article is how fast you should run the first 200m of a 400m race. Now everyone is different so I have to generalise to a certain extent but I believe that the first 200m should be run one second outside of maximum - and this is what I tell my athletes to aim for. The differential between first and second 200s should be 1.5 seconds. Both of these are conservative figures. To test the theory: The 1995 season saw James Hilston run a 200m best of 22.4 secs. (He was injured through much of 1996 so we'll take no notice of more recent times.) Therefore, his first 200m in a one-lap race should be 23.4 and using the remainder of the above formula - 23.4 x 2 + 1.5 = 48.3. His best time that year was actually 48.35. We are talking here about a relatively novice level when compared to international athletes so let's move on and test the theory with some of Britain's finest in 1996: Roger Black. Best 1996 200m 20.56. Therefore 21.56 x 2 + 1.5 = 44.62 (actual best 44.34). Mark Richardson. Best 1996 200m 20.6. 21.6 x 2 + 1.5 = 44.70 (actual best 44.66). Jamie Baulch. Best 1996 200m 21.97. 21.97 x 2 + 1.5 = 45.46 (actual best 44.57). As you can see, the times of 1 sec. and 1.5 secs. are quite conservative at top level but it is not easy to judge as most of the top 400 metre runners do not run that many quality 200 metre races and it is difficult to know what their potential 200m best really is. Except one, and that's Michael Johnson. Apply the above formula to Michael's times. His 1996 200m best of 19.32 gives us 20.32 x 2 + 1.5 = 42.14 secs. Or even using his old 200m World Record figures of 19.66 - 42.82. What I conclude from this is that either Michael Johnson is scared of 400s or he needs a kick up the backside. He had a very low differential of only 0.35 secs in last year's World Champs 400m final (21.65 and 22.00) and I believe that he ran the first half too slow. If he had run one second faster, still only 20.65, and kept his same second half then a time of 42.65 was feasible. I know it would be difficult to achieve this at a major championships with all the preliminary rounds but the above figures are conservative and in a one-off at a Grand Prix it should be possible. So don't be surprised when Michael Johnson runs under 43 seconds ... or maybe even under 42 ! Bob Bridges Bob Bridges Bob Bridges Mike Smith Mike Smith 400 metre coach; author of Play The Percentages Game in Athletics Weekly James Hilston James Hilston 200m best 22.4 and 400m best 48.35 in 1995 Roger Black Roger Black Mark Richardson Mark Richardson Jamie Baulch Jamie Baulch Michael Johnson Michael Johnson World Championships

items.sum: Explanation of Belgrave's withdrawal from the girls' McDonalds Young Athletes League after an unsuccessful 1996, for lack of young female members, with results from three matches.
items.s: McDonalds Young Athletes League Girls Division 2 South Explanation of Belgrave's withdrawal from the girls' McDonalds Young Athletes League after an unsuccessful 1996, for lack of young female members, with results from three matches. It has to be said that our attempt to move into the Girls' McDonalds Young Athletes League in 1996 was not successful. Probably the main problem is that we just do not have enough young female members - and those that we do have are not too keen on turning out in the YA League on Sunday when the odds are that they have competed in the Southern Women's League on the Saturday. The fact that the SWL includes events for younger age groups is obviously faced by other clubs as well as ourselves but without the numbers the task is impossible. So, increasing our female membership has to be addressed first - or does it ? We don't want to overload those that are running our women's teams - so maybe we need more people to take responsibility for organisation - and where do they come from? In the meantime we have withdrawn from the league for now and will concentrate on Women's Southern and Thameside Leagues. items.sum: Report on Belgrave veterans' 1996 SCVAC track and field league season, in which the men and women both reached the auxiliary final behind Serpentine, with results from matches 3 and 4 and the auxiliary final.
items.s: Veterans' Track & Field Mid-London Division Report on Belgrave veterans' 1996 SCVAC track and field league season, in which the men and women both reached the auxiliary final behind Serpentine, with results from matches 3 and 4 and the auxiliary final. Double win for the "Serps" The competition is always tight between Serpentine, Metropolitan Police and Belgrave as far as the men's matches go. We are so strong in the throws and pick up points all over the place in over 50 events thanks to Captain Snowy. Just to level up the race for points, however, we always seem give ourselves the handicap of going into each match with an almost total lack of middle-distance runners. We've got enough of them in the club but they just don't seem interested in track competition. Ian Vaughan-Arbuckle was a welcome addition to our over 50 runners and Rex Bale filled in when he could. Nice too, to have Derek Clack back in the team while the ever eager Mick Graham will do anything to get on the score sheet - but that was it as far as 800m, 1500m and 3000m and steeplechase were concerned - for both age groups. As a result, as South of England Champions we failed to even make the main final this year and just scraped into the auxiliary final as runners up in our division. By the time of the auxiliary final we were able to welcome some MD runners into the side but by then the sprinters and jumpers were suffering from a variety of pulls and twinges and as the match slowly slipped away from us we pulled Snowy out of his 'kamikaze' decathlon-in-one-day points quest and put things on ice until 1997. There is absolutley no stopping Serpentine Runners in the Women's matches and as we do not now have anything like a full team it's just a question of doing the events that take one's fancy and enjoying the outing. Amazingly this resulted in a tight competition where we just lost out to the Mets. at the end of the season by one league point - and then the 'Girls in Blue' announced that they were pulling out of the auxiliary final and offered us their place. With the same tactics in the final the Belles cruised into 5th spot - one place better than the men - and rounded off their season with a 4x100m run for the pure joy of just being out there and doing it. With two of the team over 50, another knocking on the door and one over 60, there was no way they were going to win but the sight of our W60 throws specialist Barbara Dunsford giving it some down the finishing straight was one to treasure. items.s: Boys of Summer Numbered captions and photo credits for the centre-spread photo feature of nine Belgrave men from the 1996 track and field season; photos 1, 2, 7, 8 and 9 are on page 30 and photos 3 to 6 on page 31. Centre page photo captions - starting top left and working clockwise. 1.At 16 James Tuson's a bit of an all-rounder. Last season, in his first year as an U17M he high jumped 1.80, long jumped 5.75, tripled 13.10 and cropped up regularly in sprints and relays. James is our U17M T&F Captain for 1997. 2.Clearly our most prolific points scorer in British League matches, Discus thrower Kevin Brown's 1996 best of 58.66 ranked him 3rd in the country. His all-time best is 59.50 from '95. He's not averse to heaving the shot either and pictured overleaf is about to take 2nd place in BAL match 3 'B' event at Alexander Stadium. 3.Lee Newman specialises in Shot and uses the spiral technique. His 1996 best of 18.85 was a pb that placed him 4th in the country but in indoor competition this winter he has already shown signs that his best is due for revision yet again. 4.At Kingsmeadow for BAL match 4 Paul Evans and Gary Staines toy with the opposition in the 5,000 metres before running in together for 'A' and 'B' wins, separated by the electrical timing by 1/100th! 5.One time Gladiators contestant Chris Rawlinson set personal records of 14.52 and 50.36 for the two hurdle races in '96 - as well as gaining an international vest. He's no mean decathlete either with a score of 6,291 dating from 1995. 6.Ian Tullett catapaults himself to 5.20 at Copthall. What great service our pole vaulters have given us over the years. 7.Yet another Belgrave thrower to set his best ever performance during 1996. Leith Marar reached out a further 20 cm to 55.58 to rank 8th in the country for the Discus. Leith was second only to Kevin Brown when it came to points scoring in BAL matches. 8.Mike Edwards vaulted to 5.40 to win at Copthall in BAL match 2 but his season's best of 5.45 came at Battersea in a Rosenheim event. 9.Matt Yates scored some great double wins over 800 and 1,500 metres. Pictured at Copthall where he had already taken the 'A' 800 event, he controls the 'B' 1,500m before sprinting away from the field. Photo credits: Paul Beaumont - 5 and 7. items.h: McDonalds Young Athletes League Boys Southern Premier Division: Bels make it to the National Finals
items.sum: Report on Belgrave's young male athletes reaching the Southern Premier Division top three and the National Final in 1996, praising team managers Leo Coy and John Powell and naming their successors.
items.s: McDonalds Young Athletes League Boys Southern Premier Division: Bels make it to the National Finals Report on Belgrave's young male athletes reaching the Southern Premier Division top three and the National Final in 1996, praising team managers Leo Coy and John Powell and naming their successors. With the fortunes of our younger athletes reported in detail in our Youth In Action magazine we will more or less restrict ourselves here to publication of the results to keep the historical information contained within the pages of The Belgravian intact. However, we must report that 1996 saw Belgrave's young male athletes attain their most impressive achievements yet. True, we have been in the Southern Premier Division before, but it was only a brief showing in 1994 before dropping back down again. This time it was different. With three team wins and two second places not only did we finish up with a top three placing but we made it to the National finals at Alexander Stadium, Birmingham, something that no other club has managed to do when only just breaking into the Division. The standard at this level is ferocious in an arena where the very cream of the nation's Young Athletes do battle for their clubs. It's pretty ferocious off the field of competition as well as clubs vie for every possible point and rival teams invoke the rarely used rule of deducting points where clubs do not provide enough officials. Managing the team involves the nightmare task of bringing together maybe sixty boys, transporting them across the country and then making sure that they compete in club kit, adhere exactly to the competition rules and turn up at the start of their event on time. And as for the final, involving an overnight stay in a hotel in the Midlands ... Surfice it to say that the Belgrave Team Management pairing of Leo Coy and John Powell was equal to every crisis. Not only must we congratulate our athletes and their Captains but we must underline what an amazing achievement it has been for these two men. But things move on. As reported elsewhere, Leo is moving to Ireland and will no longer be seen in his familiar role as Team Manager. John Powell is also moving on, but in his case to manage our Under 20 Men's team as they too shoot for top team honours. Taking their places will be two new managers who will carry Belgrave's hopes for even more success: Laurence Rogers and Barbara George. We wish them luck. Sean Eaton ran to 3rd and 4th places in the Under 13 National Rankings for 100 and 200 metres with 12.3 and 26.0, times set when he was still eleven years of age. With another summer in the age group we can expect fireworks from this boy in 1997- but then with an Aunt like GB international Lorna Booth would you expect otherwise. With another summer in the age group we can expect fireworks from this boy in 1997- but then with an Aunt like GB international Lorna Booth would you expect otherwise. items.s: News notes on Chris Sweeney in the Northumberland All-Terrain Marathon, Paul Evans in the Dam to Dam 10 miles and IAAF World Cross Challenge, and Matt Yates's third place at Belfast. In the Northumberland All-Terrain Marathon at the beginning of August Chris Sweeney found hinself running on beach, woodland and track to take part in this made for TV all-terrain event. Unfortunately Chris had to come out with a hamstring injury before its conclusion. He's now slowly getting back to fitness and its a shame that such a fine runner picks up so many niggles. 4m Road Holy Island 14, 19:25. 4m Hill Ingram 13, 23:30. 1m Plessey Woods 7, 4:41. 2m Track Hexham 9, 9:08. 3m Beach Embleton Bay 16, 15:25. 3m Harbour Seaton Sluice 13, 15:23. In the Amsterdam to Zaandam Dam to Dam 10m. Josephat Machuka averaged 4:31.8 per mile to set a World Best 45:18.world best. Paul Evans with 46:36 was the only man in the first 12 not an African! After the opening rounds of the IAAF World Cross Challenge Paul Evans found himself lying 26th in the international standings. A 17th place at Durham over 9.3k in 29:54 was followed a week later with 15th in Belfast over 8k in 24:15. Matt Yates looking more confident under new coach Bruce Longden challenged for the lead in the middle distance men's 2k and ended up placing 3rd to John Mayock, his 6:17 was just two seconds down. items.s: Hilary keeps the flag flying on the roads Hilary Saw finished second W45 in the 1996 Surrey Road League while studying and working, with her race results listed. Despite attending degree course lectures three nights a week at London University together with the associated coursework and in addition to her full time job at the Public Record Office, Hilary Saw has kept the Belgrave colours flying on the roads, finishing as second W45 in the season-long Surrey Road League. Hilary's results were as follows: Herne Hill 10k & Surrey Champs. 16th female 49:10; Epsom All-Sorts 10k 51st, 51:24; Epsom Fun Day 5m 32nd (2ndW45) 39:43; Coombe Hill 5m 53rd (2nd W45) 39:17; Tadworth 5m 161st, 40:48; Dorking 10m 50th female 86:47; Dysart Dash 10k 298th, 53:29; Elmbridge 10k 276th (8th W45) 50:44; Belgrave & Surrey 5k 12th female 23:32; Vets AC 5.2m 6th female (1st W45) 40:38. items.s: Men's Track & Field Rankings 1996 Belgrave's 1996 men's track and field rankings for every age group and event, from 100 metres to decathlon, with photos of Michael Parper, Steve Scott, Jamie Webb, Kevin Brown and Tom Lerwill; the event lists on pages 35-40 are kept as page scans and the relay lists on page 41 are transcribed. Here they are again - as deep as ever. How far up (or down!) can you go in 1997. As usual, wind readings are shown where known and the numbers before the athlete's name indicate World/British ranking for their age group - again where known. In the odd case where a Junior (U20M) athlete is ranked nationally among Seniors then their senior ranking is additionally shown in brackets. Wind assisted marks are shown at the end of each event except where we do not know of a non-wind assisted performance in which case they have been included in the main list to preserve the 'pecking order'. Notification of any errors or additions should be sent to Belgrave Rankings, [address withheld]. Men's Track & Field Rankings compiled by Hazel Mead Eighteen year old one-lap racer Michael Parper came back to the Belgrave Rankings with a vengeance, clocking 48.54 at Bedford in the AAA U20 Champs. One of four Belgravians ranked in the Junior UK Top 20 for the 400m event, Michael has been elected our Under 20 Men's Captain for 1997. Steve Scott - number one U20 in the country over the 99cm 110m hurdles with two more years in the age group! Every year another improvement. In 1996 Jamie Webb raised his best 'vault another 15cm to 4.40m and broke into the British League team for the first time. Left: Kevin Brown finished the season as Belgrave's most prolific points scorer in British Athletic League matches. His 80 points put him 10 points clear of fellow thrower Lee Newman. Apart from his exploits in individual 800m events, Tom Lerwill had a part to play in two of our 4x400m records of 1996. In Istanbul he joined Ridgeon, Rawlinson and Nolan for a 3:09.30 clocking and pictured above, he anchored our under 20 squad to a 3:17.1 National Junior League record with a 47.6 effort. 40.47 1 Lenny items.sum: Note on Belgrave's record-breaking 1996 relay season, including a 4x400m club record at the European Clubs Championship and new under 20 club relay marks.
items.s: Best ever year for relays Note on Belgrave's record-breaking 1996 relay season, including a 4x400m club record at the European Clubs Championship and new under 20 club relay marks. In the European Clubs Championship a new 4x400 metres Club Record was set by Messrs. Lerwill, Ridgeon, Rawlinson and Nolan, and there's a couple of names there who went on to set superb individual performances as the season progressed. But talking of relays, Juniors Scott, Dickson, Johnson, Hilston, Parper and Lerwill wiped up the previous 4x100, 4x200 and 4x400 marks. With some of them only just turned 17 their Under 20 Men's 4x200 mark, set during a Rosenheim League match, averaged 21.9 per man and the time has stood up as the fastest Club time in the UK this year - in Senior competition, let alone Junior. Their 4x400 removed 6 whole seconds from the National Junior League Record and was close to the British Junior Best Ever. Even with Lerwill exiting the age group in 1997 that mark is still in danger. items.s: Hewitt-Jones Road Relay, Walton, 14 Sep 96 Report of the Hewitt-Jones Road Relay at Walton, where Belgrave's senior team finished third behind Aldershot F&D and Boxhill Racers, with B team and M40 results. First fixture of the 'winter' season and a minibus laden to the gunnels with a cheerful band of runners. What more can a Team Manager want. The old Walton Relay has been suffering from poor entries in recent years. Times change and the 'road' course now takes in five or six hundred metres of woodland to avoid some of the traffic and miss the pot-holes in the layby no longer maintained by the council. But this year entries were up again and to avoid a mass of runners surging out onto the road at the start, the ladies and veterans were sent on their way some five minutes after the senior men. Fresh from a good track season Dave Pamah gave the Bels a flying start. Boxhill were away through Haywood but Dave's powerful finish, delayed until the pack were out of the woods, carried the claret and gold to 2nd and his 15:59 stood up as our fastest of the day. Roger Alsop disposed of the 'Boxhill Billies' but Jackson of Aldershot was not to be denied as he set the day's fastest and gave his club a lead they were not to relinquish. On a flying visit from Dublin, Derek Kelleher took charge on stage three and with twin Dave urging him on, set off like a champion. Sadly he had a bad day, blowing up at the foot of the hill and finding himself unable to respond as our rivals pounced. He was so dejected afterwards. Never mind old chap, it can happen to the best. Herne Hill were now in 2nd while we were 5th - but we had a strong second half up our sleeves. Dave Beaver took us forward again with yet another 'blinding' run and had our next man Said Chettati racing flat out to get to the take-over zone ahead of him. It might have looked hilarious but the Team Manager was having kittens. Not the best way to start his stage but Said held on to his position, resisting the Hare & Hounds man breathing down his neck. No problems on the last lap as Gerry carried the Bels away from any danger of finishing out of the frame, gaining half a minute on AFD and a whole minute on Boxhill. It was good to get a full 'B' squad out as well as a veterans' team, and youngsters Steve Beaver and Kevin Quinn should be delighted with their efforts. 23 teams started, 20 finished. items.h: Great North Run, Newcastle 15 Sep 96: Tyneside Triumph
items.sum: Report of the 1996 Great North Run half-marathon, where Paul Evans was second to Benson Masya and Belgrave won the team race, with results and Paul Evans' Great North Run record.
items.s: Great North Run, Newcastle 15 Sep 96: Tyneside Triumph Report of the 1996 Great North Run half-marathon, where Paul Evans was second to Benson Masya and Belgrave won the team race, with results and Paul Evans' Great North Run record. It was Paul Evans' sixth trip to the North-East for the Great North Run Half-Marathon and it was reckoned by many to be his best chance yet of pulling off a victory with the field not quite so packed with Kenyans as in recent times. Even when the organisers enrolled three time winner Benson Masya at the eleventh hour the Belgrave Harrier could still claim to be at least equal favourite for the Kenyan had not shown his customary form in recent outings. For Gary Staines it was his second attempt at this classic, the race forming part of his preparations for the Chicago Marathon and as he gets more and more comfortable with the longer road races he moves ever closer to Paul's shoulder. The race was an absolute treat for Belgrave supporters glued to the television as a small but elite group broke away from the masses and included Masya, the Spaniard Antonio Serrano, Basildon's Eamonn Martin and Rob Denmark and the Belgrave trio of Evans, Staines and Kassa Tadesse. With Jim Estall out of TV camera range we could not see our fourth placer but knew that our "oh-so-reliable" super-vet was sure to be forward enough to clinch the team race should things continue in this vein. Denmark was first to fall away with bad blisters and at 10k Serrano accelerated to shake the rest up but it was at the 10 mile point that the decisive break came as Benson Masya decided that the others were too close for comfort. He didn't pull far away and for the rest of the race, particularly on the downhill run in to the coast it seemed that Paul might just get back to him but it was not to be. Gary easily got the better of his Chicago rival Martin for 4th and Kassa managed a tremendous sprint to beat Morpeth's Hudspith across the line for 7th. Great to see Kassa running well again. Sure enough, a steady run from Jim had him home in 60th spot and when the times were added up we had the beating of Morpeth and Bingley by around seven minutes. As after the London Marathon there was some comment on the fact that our men wore two designs of vest - the fully professional Evans and Staines clad in their Nike kit (as per their contracts) with the other two wearing traditional claret and gold. But as a letter from Woodford Green's Terry McCarthy later stated in AW: ". what a can of worms this rule is .. " The letter was headed "Forget the vests, Belgrave boys were best." items.s: Past, present and future photo feature on Dave Beaver's running, from racing Dave Bedford in the 1977 London Cross Country Championships to his Belgrave success now, and his 15-year-old son Steve, with an invitation for young runners to join their Sunday runs. After 15 months of running with the Bels, Dave Beaver seems more surprised than anyone with his success. Last season in his first race for us he went into our scoring ten in the Surrey League ... and at Lloyd Park this winter in race three of the series he became our first man home. A member of our winning Surrey CC Team he very nearly earned himself an Inter-Counties run. All this through keeping son Stephen company and advising him on his training runs. But then talent will out. You've got to remember that this man,at the age of 15 in 1975, set what is probably still a UK Age Best for 5,000m of 14:54.6! And of course, in 1978 he placed 2nd to Steve Binns in the National Junior CC Champs at Luton. Past Left: It's November 26th 1977 at Parliament Hill and showing no fear, eighteen year-old Dave Beaver (253), racing in the classic Polytechnic Harriers singlet, locks horns with "Bootsie" Dave Bedford (284) in the London Cross Country Championships. Bedford won with Dave 4th and Bob Treadwell (329 in the photo) 2nd. Present Still blowing hard after the traditional Christmas Day work-out - running in the Lauriston Paarlauf. Dave is regularly at Belgrave Hall on Sunday mornings, ready to run at 10:30am, and will be delighted to pass on his experience to any youngsters between the ages of about 15 to 20 who want to run with him and Stephen over distances from five to eight miles. Future Right: It can't always be easy having a father who's done it all himself but 15 year-old Steve Beaver enjoys his running and proudly wears his Surrey vest in an Inter-Counties meet at Southampton. Far right: Showing all the style of a thoroughbred, Steve heads a mixed bunch during an Open Meeting middle-distance race at Tooting. items.h: Reebok South of England Road Relays, Rushmoor Arena, Aldershot, 28 Sep 96: Good ol' boys see us through
items.sum: Report of the South of England Road Relays at Aldershot, where an understrength Belgrave senior team finished 16th and the M60 team took third, with results.
items.s: Reebok South of England Road Relays, Rushmoor Arena, Aldershot, 28 Sep 96: Good ol' boys see us through Report of the South of England Road Relays at Aldershot, where an understrength Belgrave senior team finished 16th and the M60 team took third, with results. On the journey down to Aldershot we were reliably informed that this was the first time we had tackled the event as a senior team since 1991. Our informant, Roger Alsop, went on to let us know that he was the only survivor from that team five years ago when he turned in the slowest time for the Belgrave outfit. Now he vowed to be the fastest. The intention was that we should aim for a place in the top 20 and thus qualify for a place in the National 6-Stage when we might well be able to pull in most of our "top-guns" but as race day neared, of our 36 entered names only six were available on the day and it was going to be touch and go. Poor Charlie Dickinson, who had not intended even running in the veterans event and hadn't even got his racing shoes with him, found himself dragged into the senior squad within minutes of the race starting. With 110 teams toeing the start line Gerry took his turn as lead-off man and after his two circuits of 2,961 metres (5,922m in all) brought us home a respectable 17th. The melee of the second leg saw wholesale changes in the team positions and Said slipped back six places although he was pleased with his time in relation to Cap'n Gerry's. True to his word Roger Alsop put up the fastest Belgrave time on leg three and underlined yet again that he is entering the 96/97 season at a totally new level of fitness. Junior Galley was next up, suffering from lack of sleep after the arrival of a new baby Galley a few days earlier, and when a plucky Chas. Dickinson completed his stint we hovered just on the 20 mark. There was excitement all round on the last leg. Blackheath had led from stage 3 and must have thought they had the race in the bag but Chelmsford's Keith Cullen believed otherwise and flew round for the 3rd best clocking of all time, taking his Essex team to victory. For the Bels. a tanned Jim Estall gobbled up four of the teams ahead and all things considered we had to be pleased with our 16th place. Mission accomplished! Jim's effort was superb, the only other veterans to run faster times being Invicta's Mike Gratton (18:51) and Cambridge Harrier's Alan Camp (18:56), while Julian Goater could only offer a 19:08. An unexpected third place for the understrength Belgrave M60 team made their journey to Rushmoor Arena worthwhile. Missing both Laurie O'Hara, who has been off colour all summer, and new 60's star Tony Verdie who couldn't turn out, our four were delighted to pinch their bronze on the last leg when Woodford Green ran out of runners. Most pleasing was the return of Mike Newton who has been troubled by a succession of illness problems over the last couple of years. Mike ran a blinding 24:57 just fractionally slower than the fine first leg run by Pat Newell which had put Belgrave in 6th place. Pat hadn't long returned from walking the Pennine Way, so must have found the hills at Aldershot a piece of cake! A rather unfit Charlie (Linford) Walker ran a steady leg in spite of having to return to touch Mike after a false start. Carl Cross too ran steadily on the last stage and it was here that Belgrave's strength in depth showed as we eased into the medals above teams with just one or two faster runners. It was good to see the M50's team out again with Richard Pearson, now elevated to that age group, running very strongly. 110 teams started, 88 finished. items.s: Great Caledonian Run 10k, Edinburgh, 29 Sep 96 Short report of the Great Caledonian Run 10k in Edinburgh, won by Kenyan C. Kelong, with Gary Staines fourth and Kassa Tadesse sixth. Only Britons, including Gary Staines, had previously triumphed in the Caledonian run but with the course changed to take in the rugged slopes of Arthur's Seat, it was the Kenyans who overcame the additional adversity with Kelong and Nziku racing it out between them to decide the winner. A fast start by mountain racer Tommy Murray had been followed by our own Kassa Tadesse's storming ascent of the 1,000ft hill. Staines and Longwood's Pearson seemed to be tucked in nicely but the descent made them look decidedly uncomfortable and as the field ran onto the Royal Mile the Africans were away. 1, C.Kelong (Kenya) 29:11; 2, R.Nziku (Kenya) 29:11; 3, A.Pearson (Longwood) 29:38; 4, G.Staines 29:56; ... 6, K.Tadesse 30:13. items.s: Great South Run 10m, Portsmouth, 6 Oct 96 Report of Gary Staines' third win in the Great South Run ten miles at Portsmouth, a second ahead of Lameck Aguta, with Kevin Quinn 97th. Looking totally at home back on the South Coast, Gary Staines put the finishing touches to his Chicago Marathon preparation with a scintillating victory against classy opposition. It was his third win in the event and what a trio of times - 46:11, 47:00 and 46:57! Commonweath Games 10,000m Champion Lameck Aguta joined Gary and and Skyrac's Whitehead as Ian Cornford of Shaftesbury forced the early pace. Only Degefu from Ethiopia managed to bridge the gap from the main pack but before long it was the Belgravian taking the initiative. As the others dropped off one by one it was left to Aguta and Staines to chop and change in front while the Ethiopian tucked in behind. As the Kenyan went ahead for the final stages now it was Gary tucking in behind as the windiest stretch of the race was reached. Just a few hundred metres to go and it was was a delighted Staines who had the race totally under control as he came home by a one second margin. Back down the field young Kevin Quinn did not impress coach Billy Bull by turning out in this ten-miler. Seventeen year-old Kev. insists that it was only a steady run. 1, G.Staines (Belgrave) 46:57; 2, L.Aguta (Kenya) 46:58; 3, F.Degefu (Ethipoia) 47:14; ... 97, K. items.h: Reebok Surrey CC League Division 1 Race 1 Brockwell Park, 19 Oct 1996: Matt Yates leads "The Revival"
items.sum: Report of the first Surrey League Division 1 race of 1996-97 at Brockwell Park, where Matt Yates was second and Belgrave third team behind Borough of Hounslow and Thames Hare & Hounds, with senior and youth results and photos of the team and the start.
items.s: Reebok Surrey CC League Division 1 Race 1 Brockwell Park, 19 Oct 1996: Matt Yates leads "The Revival" Report of the first Surrey League Division 1 race of 1996-97 at Brockwell Park, where Matt Yates was second and Belgrave third team behind Borough of Hounslow and Thames Hare & Hounds, with senior and youth results and photos of the team and the start. The charge, with the Belgrave flag flying bravely in the breeze. The start of another league campaign. We'd finished strongly at the end of the previous season with a 4th team place and as our President and Team Manager arrived early to hoist the new Belgrave flag aloft, hopes were high for a continuance of the upward trend. "What's this ... a revival ?", called out South London Team Manager Mick Firth as the club colours proudly flew over Herne Hill territory in the stiff breeze. We could only hope so, for traditionally we seem to start off with an abysmal performance. But a revival it was. Before too long around thirty Belgrave runners and a dozen supporters had gathered at the foot of the mast and with Stu' Paton hurling good natured abuse at all and sundry our team gathered themselves for the strength-sapping uphill start. From the very beginning Matt Yates was in the thick of the action as AFD's Jackson forced the pace up the slope with Marriott (HW), Major (SLH) and an unknown Thames man also in close attendance. Not so far back, in his first scoring run for the Bels., Steve Hewes had made a blistering start that he was shortly to pay for. Going into the second lap the Thames man, now identified as 2nd-claimer Larry Matthews from Salford, made his break and forced open what began to look like a winning lead. Matt was going well in the chasing bunch with Roger Alsop and Jim Estall also claiming forward positions. But the revelation for the Bels. was the battling performances from our middle order men. Grouped together in two's and three's it was by no means certain who would fill out the scoring ten. It was far from over up front as well. The nearer the leader got to the finish, the more contorted became his features as the others slowly reeled him in. Climbing the last hill it looked as if Matt might just have the Midlander in range as he left Simpson and Major behind in a last ditch assault but once the hair-pin turn at the top had been negotiated and they dropped back down the slope to the finish we could see that the Belgrave man was going to have to settle for the runner-up's slot. Borough of Hounslow had the team race sewn up with six men in the first dozen but we were looking as good as anyone else at this stage as tremendous running from Roger gave him a final position of 13th with Jim first veteran home ahead of Herne Hill's Bob Payne by three places and twelve seconds. Way above expectations Bruce Barton and the Daves Beaver and Pamah came home in the 40s with Charlie Dickinson and Mike Webb also entering the funnel together in the 50's. Said Chettati and a shattered Steve Hewes closed in the team but with Mike Kazimierski and Phil Carstairs close behind we had plenty of back-up. Our last scorer was home ahead of his Thames counterpart but the Roehampton based club had too many men in the 'teens and thirties so it was 2nd for them and a highly pleasing 3rd for the Bels. Our best opening match since 1986 and before that 1973! The Belgrave youngsters were very thin on the ground and had to take last scoring positions to fill out the score sheet. But what they lacked in numbers they made up for in individual prowess as Amir celebrated his return to England with 2nd in the Under 17 race, Steve Beaver made an early bid to retain his overall Under 15 trophy and Denny DeEmmony opened a few eyes with his powerful running to win the youngest category by a full 25 seconds. 156 finished Left: Getting ready for the "off" at Brockwell Park. items.h: Chicago Marathon, 20 Oct 1996: Evans races to 3rd fastest ever British Marathon time
items.sum: Report of Paul Evans winning the 1996 Chicago Marathon in 2:08:52, with Gary Staines fifth and Tony Barden 26th.
items.s: Chicago Marathon, 20 Oct 1996: Evans races to 3rd fastest ever British Marathon time Report of Paul Evans winning the 1996 Chicago Marathon in 2:08:52, with Gary Staines fifth and Tony Barden 26th. Chicago - home of some world famous sporting outfits. The White Sox baseball team come from this part of the world as do the Bears Football team but on this occasion the “windy city” was the setting for one of the best ever British marathon victories. And while Paul Evans charged to the third fastest ever time by a Briton, Gary Staines took another minute off his best to place 5th and come home in 2:11:25 in only his third run out over the distance. What a pair. Gary had been aiming for the event for some time. Knee and back niggles had hampered his preparations but winning the Great South 10 miler from the outstanding African Lameck Aguta put him into the frame of mind where he felt he had a 2:10-2:11 in him and how right he was. Learning more about the race all the time, it surely must be on the cards that “Stainesy” also has a 2:08 to come when everything goes right. For Paul an outing in Chicago only came together in the last few weeks before the event. Originally he was pencilled in for the New York race a little later but amazingly the organisers of that event couldn't find room in their budget for him. New York's loss was Chicago's gain. Like Gary he went into the race with a super 10 miler behind him, a 46:36 clocking in Amsterdam's Dam to Dam race in September. The early pace was strong and both Belgravians felt uncomfortable early on. Half-way was reached in 64:12 but in the next few miles the pace dropped a little to just outside 5 minute miles. Paul was now feeling great, however, and his only worry was whether he should put in a burst to break things up a bit. Even this concern was removed when the Russian Svetsov took up the initiative and did the work for him. Basildon's Eamonn Martin and Gary Staines dropped away as only the American Lawson joined Evans in clinging on to the Russian's tail. A 25 metre gap opened at one point but at 18 miles three consecutive sub-4:50s put Evans in the clear. By 23 miles he was a minute up and enjoying the sensation of cruising to his first ever marathon win in eleven attempts. Gary was still lying 4th with only a quarter mile to go but a typical Eamonn Martin late charge shunted him back a place. With second-claimer Tony Barden in 26th it was a great day for the Bels. 1, P.Evans (Bel) 2:08:52; 2, L.Lawson (USA) 2:10:04; 3, L.Svetsov (Russia) 2:10:33; 5, G.Staines 2:11:25; 26, T.Barden 2:26:34.
