items.h: Three Gold Cup wins in a row
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's 1998 Gold Cup semi-final win at Wavertree, Liverpool, and final win at Bedford, a third consecutive Gold Cup.
items.s: Three Gold Cup wins in a row Report and results of Belgrave's 1998 Gold Cup semi-final win at Wavertree, Liverpool, and final win at Bedford, a third consecutive Gold Cup. Track & Field - Gold Cup Three Gold Cup wins in a row With 2 years as Cup Winners behind us we were conscious that a third consecutive win would represent a feat only previously achieved by Haringey AC at the height of their powers. SEMI-FINAL, WAVERTREE, LIVERPOOL, 19 JUL 1998 Two years ago when we had a cup semi at Liverpool we were sent the wrong timetable and arrived after the Match had started. We eventually scraped home in second place. We didn't intend to cut it so fine this time and despite other competing events we were determined not to take chances. Thankfully a number of team members put Club before Area and we sat back to witness some first class performances in difficult conditions. I say, we, because Sir Eddie had jetted into the UK just to support the team and in John Jeffery's absence he was co-opted as Joint Team Manager. Taking the final result into account Sir Eddie thought both he and we had done rather well. That is a bit of an understatement because despite the presence of two other BAL Division 1 teams (Sale and Border), we won 16 of the 20 events with an all time record score of 167 points. Bearing in mind that to win all 20 events would give 180 points you can see that this was pretty impressive stuff. The results speak for themselves but the highlights were: Matt Simson's first outing since his elbow operation which limited him to the single winning effort in the shot. Mark Miles moved down to the 800m and then won the 5000m in a personal best. Well it had to be a PB because it was the first one he had run. Afterwards he said he thought it was a jog although the sprint at the end was interesting. Jim Estall was the oldest on display but moved nicely to win the 10,000m. He puts the new fluency down to an extensive stretching programme, although there is no verification of room mate James Ellis Smith's assertion, that this routine started at 5.00 in the morning. We welcomed our newest and youngest member into the team – Ben Flint – who won the pole vault in difficult conditions. A few weeks before the Cup Final, Athletics 98 announced a GB/USA match in Glasgow for 1st September. Immediately we knew that some CUP FINAL team members would be called up. Luckily we persuaded the powers that be to delay flying most of their team from Heathrow until the last flight which was about 8.00pm. The only person we lost was Matt Yates due to some ruling that he couldn't compete on consecutive days. Mind you, Kevin Mackay did, so we never got to the bottom of that one. Anyway, we moved Jason Lobo to the 1500m, put Matt Kloiber in the 800m and persuaded Mark Miles to run his second 5000m and we were sorted. All we waited for now, was to see how Newham had been affected by the USA match. And as the afternoon unfolded it became clear that Newham could scrape a win. The start was nip and tuck. Mick Jones won the hammer in another PB. Paul Head of Newham second. Julian Flynn then had an unexpected win in the long jump over Newham's Chris Davison who was destined for Kuala Lumpur. Then the 10,000m where Newham's Ian Grime outkicked Kassa. Our 3 best shots and we were just a couple of points ahead. Newham then won the 400H and the 800m and we were in second spot with the rest nowhere. Ben Challenger competing for the first time since injuring himself in the Europa Cup, produced a stunning 2.26 to win the high jump but the Newham man was third. The discus was a 1,2 with Nick Sweeney well ahead of Newham's Paul Head. The 100m turned out to be historic due to the unexpected return of Linford Christie. His win had no effect on the team positions but Drew Walcott was a place behind the Newham man. Newham then pipped our men in the 110H, 400m and triple jump and we trailed by 6 points. Lee Hurst reduced the deficit in the 3000 s/c and Jason Lobo pulled back more points to finish a fine second in the 1500m to Kevin McKay. Birchfield then came to our aid in the shot with an unknown American outthrowing Newham Mark Proctor with Matt Simson third. Then it was down to John Regis who, although pipped by Sale's Allyn Condon, managed to squeeze 6 points out of the Newham man. The javelin saw Newham's Mark Robinson level the scores but then Mike Edwards' win in the pole vault and Mark Miles' win in the 5000m saw us start to ease away. The 5000m was thrilling and a slow tactical race saw a great burn up at the end. One which Mark Miles won, beating the favourite Darius Burrows with a devastating 1.58.0 last 800m. A fine win in the sprint relay widened our lead. We used the same team as Match 4 League with Chris Lambert as lead-off and then the long relay boys clinched a memorable victory. Good to see Dave Nolan run the first leg in his only outing of the season ruined by injury. From Your Album From Charlie Manning's album ... Above: Chas (18) tears into the lead on the first lap of a Club Championship 880 yards Race at Battersea Park. We are not absolutely certain of the year but it was probably 1955, one of the years when Charlie Walker, (4) at the back of the pack became Club Champion over the distance. Behind Charlie Manning can be seen a youthful Jim Heathfield. Can anyone put names to the other faces in the picture? Above: It's first day of May 1954 and the smiling band above are 5 to 6 miles into the Surrey 20 miles Road Race Championship held at Mitcham. Chas. (12) was 23rd gaining a Surrey County Standard with a time of 2:14:10. Len Adams (16) and John Baker (15) can also be identified. Above: Fortythree years later and the old codger's still on the move! 24th August 1997 and Chas. (174) lines up for the Veterans A.C. 1500 metres Championship at Kingsmeadow. His time was ... well we won't go into that ... but is this a good case for euthanasia? Maybe we should pay him not to wear our club kit! items.s: Belgrave Web Site - coming soon Notice that Charlie Manning will sponsor a Belgrave Harriers web site, with thanks to donors to The Belgravian including Barry Tilbury. Belgrave Web Site - coming soon Charlie Manning has very kindly offered to sponsor our proposed Belgrave Harriers Web Site which should be up and running this summer. Thanks to Chas., and while we are at it, many thanks to all those generous souls whose donations keep The Belgravian in business. Readers are often surprised to find that the costs of our gazette are met solely out of the normal running costs of the Club together with donations from members. Actually, we do get a few donations from non-members who like to read our mag. Recently a copy was sent to a prospective member - who subsequently did not join - but his coach was so taken with it and enjoyed his read so much that he sent in a donation of £10. Thank you Barry Tilbury (who passes on his best wishes to any that remember him). Receiving his letter of appreciation and donation was one of those moments when one realises why 'one does it'. Charlie Manning Charlie Manning sponsor of the proposed club web site Charlie Manning Chas. Barry Tilbury Barry Tilbury coach of a prospective member; donated £10

Track & Field - Women's Southern League Division Two Its Tough In Two ! — Reports by Jacqui Smiter — MATCH 1, BATTERSEA PK., 25 APR 1998 The weather was good for the opening match of the season. Expectations were that we would "make an impression" but lesson number one in Division Two was learned pretty quickly: it's a lot tougher than Division Three! From the very first event when Thurrock's Gowry Retchakan blitzed away from the 400 hurdles field it was a long hard battle to stay anywhere near being in touch. We had a good senior team with some new athletes making their débuts — and even had a reasonable turn-out of under 15s but the opposition was just too strong and we had to settle for fourth team place. Track & Field - Men's Southern League Division Two Southern League Bels unbeaten in 1998 LADYWELL, 2 MAY 1998 A tremendous string of results came from our Men's Southern League Team in 1998. From the instant that the gun was fired in the very first race at Ladywell it was Belgrave all the way, highlights being a Division Record from Darren Campbell in the 200 metres and a nice series of performances from a man getting into Decathlon mode — Du'aine Ladejo. Simon Shirley, decathlete and Commonwealth Games medallist, was also on hand to push the points score along but not all records were set by those with an eye on international events later in the season — John Druce celebrated his entry into the veteran ranks with an M40 Triple Jump club record. BATTERSEA PK, 16 MAY 1998 A home meeting gave the Bels a chance to pile on even more pressure in the push for promotion, our final tally being a huge 153 points. That must surely be the most we have ever scored in a Southern League match. It was nice to pick up maximum scores in the 1500 metres — we don't do that too often. Until the last time down the back straight it looked young Kevin Quinn's race but then Ray Foley threw in a blistering finish to gain a clear win. There was more fine sprinting from Ladejo and Marlon Dickson but once again two veterans got on the scoring sheet in a big way as Jim Estall and Steve Fowler took both first places in the 5k. Actually, we say two veterans but what about that Mike Small? At every single match he tackles two, three or even four throws — and usually picks up top points. MILTON KEYNES, 6 JUN 1998 At Milton Keynes much of the pre-match discussion was focused on "who was going to do our 400 metres 'A' string — Richard David or James Hilston. James has always had the edge in the past but this year has been suffering from a stomach disorder which has restricted his training and consequently his race performances. Richard, on the other hand, is looking stronger and faster than ever and was not far short of beating Michael Parper in the Surrey Champs. Somehow or other they came to an agreement — and then both of them got beaten by a very powerful Milton Keynes pair! Ray Foley ran for a point in the 800m prior to getting outgunned over the last half lap in the 'A' 1500m. The steeplechase was next up and as this match was looking a lot tighter than the previous two, he decided he'd have another run round for a point. As the race progressed he gained in confidence and technique and ended up leaving the meeting pondering an athletics career move to the 'chase. And the answer was, "Yes" — a maximum possible score of 30 league points had been achieved. However, we must not lose sight of the fact that this, our furthest match from London, saw us turn up with no 5,000 metre runners, just one 1,500 metre man, one 'chaser and a veteran triple jumper our only "competitor" in the 800 metres. Even our two 400 metre hurdlers were pressganged. There is no way that we will survive in Division One next season unless we get some middle distance men prepared to travel. It was good to see Nick Dawson back in action over 200 metres and James Flavin had a great afternoon: his first ever 400 metres hurdles resulted in a fine win in 58.9 and for good measure he ran 22.6 over half a lap for more top points. James Hilston's health problems, whilst restricting his 400 metres outings, did at least give him the chance to tackle a few more rarely attempted events — and he came up with an impressive triple jump win in 13.55. Let's pay tribute to a couple of other men who always get near the front and who have contributed so much to the season's success — sprinters Dotun Akinbogun and Joe Panton. items.s: Touch and go - but the girls just miss out Report and Belgrave results from the women's Jubilee Cup first round at Deangate in June 1998, where Belgrave finished second to Medway and went out. Touch and go - but the girls just miss out JUBILEE CUP, FIRST ROUND, DEANGATE, 14 JUN 1998 With just one per event there were high hopes that we might just sneak through into the second round of this knockout competition — even though only the winners progress. It was touch and go throughout the afternoon with good points collected by Sabrina Scott in the sprints and Sarah Roberts in the 400 metres and triple jump. Even joint team manager Jacqui Smiter got in on the winning act by picking up top score in the pole vault but in the end it was the local club that prevailed. If we'd had one strong middle distance runner we probably would have done it. All credit to young Debbie Hearn for turning out in the 1500 metres even though she was suffering from a bruised head, the result of a crash in Dad's van! 100m: 1, S.Scott 12.6. 200m: 1, S.Scott 26.3. 400m: 1, S.Roberts 57.2. 800m: 5, J.Stone 2:49.4. 1500m: 6, D.Hearn 5:37.6. 3000m: 5, J.Stone 13:36.3. 100mH: 4, J.Smiter 20.6. 400mH: 4, J.Smiter 79.6. Centre Page Photos by Mark Shearman Starting top left, clockwise:- Matt Yates (right) gave one of his best ever Games performances in Budapest, placing 6th in a highly tactical 1500 metres final. John Mayock (left) was 5th and Tony Whiteman (centre) was 4th. No medals but it was great to see all three Brits well in contention in a European Games final again. The mighty Mick Jones. In far-off Kuala Lumpur a Commonwealth Games silver medal in the hammer throw was repayment for all those hours of practice in a farmer's field in Dorking, Surrey. A Belgrave one-two in the European Games 100 metres! Silver for Dwain Chambers and gold for Darren Cambell. Relaxed and smooth, Darren Campbell eases to an impressive win in the early rounds of the 100 metres at Budapest. Giant Dave Smith, not quite up to his 1997 form but 5th in the Commonwealth Games hammer throw can't be bad. Dwain Chambers gives Papadias some eyeball contact after the Greek dared to head the Belgrave man by 1/100th of a second in the 100 metres first round. A late qualifier for the 'Europeans', Brendan Reilly had to settle for =9th in the high jump final after shooting for 2.32m and a top five position. The tall figure of Jason Lobo —800 metre action at the Bukit Jalil Stadium, Kuala Lumpur. items.h: Rosenheim Plate still in Belgrave hands
items.sum: Report and Belgrave results from the 1998 Rosenheim League Eastern Division matches, which Belgrave won on the way to a fifth consecutive Rosenheim Plate.
items.s: Rosenheim Plate still in Belgrave hands Report and Belgrave results from the 1998 Rosenheim League Eastern Division matches, which Belgrave won on the way to a fifth consecutive Rosenheim Plate. Track & Field - Rosenheim League Rosenheim Plate still in Belgrave hands Our mid-week Rosenheim League success story continued in 1998 as for the fifth consecutive time Belgrave's name was added to the two splendid Rosenheim Plates. Although the Eastern League Division and Final results were as emphatic as ever, just once or twice it looked as if we might get pipped for a match win as first Sutton & District got within 4 match points of the Bels. and then Hercules Wimbledon got almost as close with a 5 point deficit and then 4 points for match six as they made a fighting attempt to get into the final. Their tally for the whole season was higher than Croydon's but they just missed out by a single league point. Sutton & District were successful, however, and it was good to see their delight at having made it. We held our home, opening, match at Tooting in the vain hope that a few extra officials from other clubs might be encouraged to show up through not having to travel to Battersea — but it didn't work out that way and the triple jump was cancelled as a result of there being no judges. As usual we were strong in the sprints, not quite so strong in the middle-distance (no-one for the 1500m) and solid on the field. For match two it was a similar story — this time an empty 800m berth and no high hurdler — but we still hung on for the win. Match three: Croydon is always the most unpopular venue due to the fact that the meeting invariably starts late thanks to an over-running schools event. This year, however, the evening was enlivened by a super race from Ray Foley in the 3000 metres where he decimated his previous best by sticking to Herne Hill's (and Blackheath's) Dave Taylor like a limpet until with 600 metres remaining he just had to let go. Also a fine league record came from Lee Newman in the discus as he added some four metres to the previous best. But again we were short of an 800 metre man and, unusually, a pole vaulter. Back to Tooting as the second half of the league was entered. This time we looked a lot stronger but were hit early on in the meeting when the normally so reliable Richard David found himself ruled out of the 100 metres by two false starts. M50 Alan Painter came to our rescue by stepping into the scoring 800 metre race, thereby giving us our first full team of the series. There was fun at Sutton when the home club were unable to procure the services of a starter. Someone duly stepped in with whistle and handkerchief but of course, what with the dodgy starting and the gale at the athletes' backs, the sprint times were just a little bit suspect! A cagey victory came from Paul Coughlan in the 3 kms. where he studiously avoided doing too much work in the front rank with that ferocious wind down the back straight — and then let rip over the final 200 metres. And so to match six. We were already assured of being Eastern Division winners but still turned out a strong team that was boosted by a superb high jump competition. The league record of 2.00 metres had been shared by four athletes — and that became six as both Richard Aspden and Samson Oni went clear at their first attempts. Maximum points for us but it was far from over as both men also took 2.05 first time and then tackled 2.10. Non-scorer Samson came so close but had to give best to Richard at this height who then went on to unsuccessfully attempt 2.15. Ray Foley celebrated by waving to the onlookers as the announcer broadcast the fact that it was his birthday — and then helped himself to the present of six match points as he led home a Belgrave 1, 2, 3 in the 3000m. The final — and the stakes were increased. A nervous Team Manager left her squad in charge of John Jeffery, Ray Foley and the young sprinters as she went off to watch the European Championships in Hungary. She needn't have worried; a 'phone call from Budapest's Népstadion back home to London revealed that the Plate was still in Belgrave hands. Lee Newman was the star of the evening as he launched a massive discus series of — 55.93, 56.45, 54.55, 56.50, 54.66, x — to twice break his own Rosenheim Record. Marlon Dickson ended the Rosenheim season as he had started, by winning the 100 metres, but here we must pay credit to all the sprinters — Richard David, James Hilston, Dotun Akinbogun, Joe Panton, Michael Peacock, Nick Molloy and others. They have been a real driving force behind the Rosenheim win streak and in the last 4 x200 of the summer they turned on a spirited display to gain revenge over Herne Hill for match 6 and clock their fastest time of the season to boot. items.s: Mo's Vets make the final Report on Belgrave's 1998 Southern Counties Veterans League season, in which the women's veterans reached the final, with comment on scoring rules and Belgrave results from each match and the final at Colindale. Southern Counties Veterans League - Track & Field Mo's Vets make the final Well done Team Manager Maureen Jones. 1998 saw her take Belgrave's female veterans to their best ever season as they twice beat Serpentine to go into the Southern Counties Final. Their male colleagues, with Terry Lawton at the helm, were beset by the same problem that hits us from British League down to Young Athletes' League — a lack of middle-distance runners. The scoring became complicated enough the previous season when, instead of a straightforward two per event in the under 50 events and one per event in the over 50 on the track, and just the one in all events on the field, it became permissable to enter an over 60 in place of an over 50. Over 60s were then scored separately in their own events. This meant that if a team had an over 60 and no other team did, then the over 60 automatically gained maximum points even if they could hardly put one foot in front of another. This rule change seemed to go through without any discussion with the clubs in the league and quite obviously helped one particular club. This season it was revealed that points were to be awarded on an age-graded basis — virtually impossible to calculate on the night. Luckily all but one club in our Mid-London Division refused to have anything to do with this although when it came to the final, clubs had to elect to go into one of two finals — an age-graded final or a non-age-graded final. There is now a rumour that next summer, men's and women's teams must be scored together. This will virtually wipe out all the team's chances in our division except Serpentine. Hercules Wimbledon, Herne Hill, Met. Police have almost no veteran women, Metros have mostly women, while Belgrave — well, Maureen had welcomed single competitors from other clubs into the Belgrave women's team to augment our own six or seven veteran ladies in an effort to combat the Serps. Now they will be ineligible as they will have to score for their first claim clubs even though there might be just the one or two of them — so we will be considerably weaker ourselves. Perhaps, if this veteran competition is really required, we should look into organising our own Mid or South London competion on normal lines and not worry about the Southern Counties V.A.C. events. items.h: Lifetime Shot Putt best for veteran Mike Small
items.sum: Account of veteran thrower Mike Small's winter 1998–99 throws multi-events, including an M40 club hammer record and a lifetime best shot putt of 13.64 at Crystal Palace.
items.s: Lifetime Shot Putt best for veteran Mike Small Account of veteran thrower Mike Small's winter 1998–99 throws multi-events, including an M40 club hammer record and a lifetime best shot putt of 13.64 at Crystal Palace. Lifetime Shot Putt best for veteran Mike Small Veteran Mike Small's "summer season" for 1998 doesn't seem to have stopped yet! In October he was still turning in hammer throws in the 45-46 metre range and then from November through to January it was time to attack the throws multi-events. During the Tooting Throws Triathlon it all came together when he launched the hammer out to an M40 Club Record and his best throw since 1988 when he was a mere stripling in his mid-thirties! Three throws in his series beat his previous season's best and next summer he will be looking for 50 metres – which would be a lifetime best. The full series: 44.41, 48.30, 47.64, x, 45.50, 46.78. Mike's score in the throws pentathlon held in conjunction was 2163 – another personal best and a meeting record. A further best ever performance came in a throws pentathlon at Deangate in December. The 35lb hammer gave him the chance to record his best ever distance of 13.65 and his overall score of 3294pts was another pb and second on the all time list, just behind the British Record. January - and Mike improved yet again, creeping ever nearer to that M40 British Record. This time he notched up 3,380 points with a heavy hammer throw of 14.11. Latest news is of a lifetime best, indoors or out, while competing in the Crystal Palace Indoor Open Meeting in February. His 13.64 was just 12 centimetres shy of the M45 British Record - and Mike turns 45 this coming March. items.sum: Review of the Belgrave Under-20 men's 1998 National Junior League season, winning the Southern Premier Division and placing 3rd at the National Final in Cannock, with match results and final tables.
items.s: Under 20s near the very top Review of the Belgrave Under-20 men's 1998 National Junior League season, winning the Southern Premier Division and placing 3rd at the National Final in Cannock, with match results and final tables. Under 20s near the very top The 1998 season saw the work of six or seven years at last come to fruition. A small band of officials have been supporting this team since the days when Leo and Jon Coy ran the team. Then we were in the lower divisions of the South Thames area — and we gained promotion. Next season it was promotion again and every single year between then and now we have not failed to win our division and go up again. Team Managers have changed (currently John Powell is in charge) and the athletes have certainly changed. A good many of the lads that have competed for us in the National Junior League have gone on to represent the Bels. in Southern and British League — Marlon Dickson, Steve Scott, Richard David — but an equal number of talented young men have also fallen by the wayside — Rob Milner, Gavin Mason, Scott Thompson to mention just a very few. But they have all contributed to our reaching the Southern Premier Division in 1998 — where we won yet again. As a result of our high showing the team earned the right to compete in the National Final at Cannock where we placed an outstanding 3rd among the very best in the country. Many of the team still have one or two more years as Under-20s so there could be more to come. items.h: Young Bels. hang on in top division
items.sum: Report on the Belgrave boys' 1998 McDonald's Young Athletes' League Southern Premier Division season, from early last places to a final-match win at Bracknell that kept them up, with results of all five matches and the final division table.
items.s: Young Bels. hang on in top division Report on the Belgrave boys' 1998 McDonald's Young Athletes' League Southern Premier Division season, from early last places to a final-match win at Bracknell that kept them up, with results of all five matches and the final division table. Young Bels. hang on in top division All credit to John Dawson for taking over the Young Athletes' team at the beginning of 1998, hardly knowing what he was letting himself in for. It was a time of some turmoil in the management of our young male teams and it showed in match one where we not only got hammered in our home meeting, we also had to endure the acid comments of officials and team managers when just about everything that could go wrong, did go wrong! A much stronger team went to Croydon for match two but in spite of some brilliant individual results it was another last place for the team and relegation from the Southern Premier Division was beginning to look a certainty. The drama was not confined to the field of competition. An ambulance had to be called and the meeting held up while it drove down the 100 metre stretch to collect a young lad who had collapsed after his race. He was later pronounced to be fine — and yes it was a Belgrave boy. Then there was the innocuous attempt by one of our lads to query one of the results with the recorders—resulting in a completely "over the top" announcer broadcasting that a Belgrave lad was attacking one of his recorders! Who'd be a young athlete's team manager? The first week-end in June took us up to Enfield and here the tide imperceptibly changed. Still desperately short of under 13 boys (we only had one!) we nevertheless got out of the basement for the first time with third team place. Now faced with a trip to Norwich some hard decisions had to be taken. Relegation was still looking likely and morale was low. Should we pull out now and save the cost of further coach travel? It would look bad but at this stage did we care? Thankfully the right decision was made and 40-50 boys set out at sparrow's chirp for Norfolk. The lads really got stuck into the opposition and the result was a much more satisfactory second place. If we could just duplicate that result in the final match we would stay up. And so to Bracknell. You wouldn't believe that it was the same team that had suffered such a devastating defeat at Battersea three months earlier. Crowds of claret and gold clad youngsters sat on the sidelines waiting to compete. Race after race was dominated by young Belgravians and the final result was a resounding first! items.h: John Lambert to join John Dawson at the helm
items.sum: Notice that John Lambert will join John Dawson in managing the boys' young athletes team in 1999, with Reg Hopkins starting an under-13 Sportshall group, and an appeal for officials.
items.s: John Lambert to join John Dawson at the helm Notice that John Lambert will join John Dawson in managing the boys' young athletes team in 1999, with Reg Hopkins starting an under-13 Sportshall group, and an appeal for officials. John Lambert to join John Dawson at the helm Already plans are being laid for the 1999 season. John Lambert will be joining John Dawson to share the load of managing the team and with Reg Hopkins gathering some under 13s around him to tackle Sportshall athletics during the winter, we should at least start off with some lads in this age group come next summer. We still need lots of help with the officiating because for every official we are short at any match, we lose points. We need to take a track judge, timekeeper, and a team of field event judges (two to four bodies) to every meeting. If you are going to the meeting anyway why not consider becoming part of the team by being an official. It doesn't matter if you've never done it before because we have experienced officials on hand to show you what to do. John Lambert John Lambert joining John Dawson to manage the young athletes' team for 1999 John Dawson John Dawson Reg Hopkins Reg Hopkins gathering under 13s for Sportshall athletics in winter Sportshall athletics

items.s: Surrey County AA Sportshall Athletics Report and results of Belgrave's under-13 teams in the 1998–99 Surrey County AA Sportshall Athletics series at Westcroft, Guildford and Woking, including the club's first girls' team; the Guildford meeting is dated 10 Jan 1998 as printed. Surrey County AA Sportshall Athletics WESTCROFT LEISURE CENTRE, 8 NOV 1998 In our first outing in Sportshall Athletics since Leo Coy was the man in charge we didn't do at all badly with a team of just six boys. Team Manager Reg Hopkins must have been very pleased. Events were two, four and six lap individual races, long jump, vertical jump and shot, obstacle race, paarlauf and 4 x 2 laps. Note that "a lap" means starting in the middle of the hall and racing to the wall – up the reverser board and back the full length of the hall – up the reverser board at the other end and back across the middle. Terry Tsai, who showed much promise as a sprinter in the McDonalds League last summer, was fastest of the 22 competitors in the 6 lap race and Belgrave won the paarlauf and 4 x 2 lap relay. Well done to all who took part – Barnaby and Toby Hodgeson, Terry Tsai, Hugo Sells, Roy Collier and Phillip Doorgachurn. As a team they placed 8th of the 14 clubs who took part with 317 points. Herne Hill were match winners with 427. Under 13 Boys 2 laps: T.Tsai 24.9; B.Hodgeson 26.5. 4 laps: T.Hodgeson 59.9; H.Sells 69.4. 6 laps: T.Tsai 1:30.8; P.Doorgachurn 1:31.8; R.Collier 1:43.8. Vertical Jump: 28cm. SP: R.Collier 6.31; T.Hodgeson 5.83. Paarlauf: 1:50.7. 4x2 laps 1:42.4. Obstacle race: 2:22.5. SPECTRUM LEISURE CENTRE, GUILDFORD, 10 JAN 1998 Several of our team were unavailable due to sickness and then Hugo went and injured his knee in the high jump leaving us with ony three people to run in the relays. Luckily he was not badly hurt. Philip Doorgachurn has been doing well in Surrey League cross country races and he made good use of his fitness by racing to the fastest time of the afternoon — out of some 30-odd competitors — in the 6 lap race. items.h: Performance Ratings & Comparisons One mile to Marathon
items.sum: Rex Bale explains how to use a chart, from Tom Osler's 'Serious Running Handbook', to score and compare running performances from one mile to the marathon.
items.s: Performance Ratings & Comparisons One mile to Marathon Rex Bale explains how to use a chart, from Tom Osler's 'Serious Running Handbook', to score and compare running performances from one mile to the marathon. Performance Ratings & Comparisons One mile to Marathon — Rex Bale writes — Have you tried to compare your times for a variety of distances to see which is the best? There have been many published tables to help you to do this but a more flexible system is possible using the chart on this page. It also allows you to give yourself a performance score so that you can set targets, or perhaps in the case of veterans to stay as long as possible above a chosen points score. The steps to follow are as follows: 1) Divide your race time by the race distance to give a rate per mile to the nearest 10 seconds. 2) Pick out this rate per mile on the left hand vertical axis and follow the horizontal line to the intersection with the vertical line for the race distance. 3) Follow the diagonal line upwards to the right hand axis and read off the points score. Example: Running 10 miles in 61:40 (6:10 minute miles) gives a score of 1,770 points — the solid line on the chart. You will see that the points lie within a fairly narrow band — for example for the mile race, a four-minute mile scores 1,950 points whereas running it in only six-and-a-half minutes scores 1,570 points. You could use an age graded table, again published in running magazines from time to time, to adjust for age. Just multiply the rate per mile by the factor for your 5-year age group (0.88 for M50) and follow the steps above. This system works best for fairly flat road courses and track, not cross country where the terrain is less predictable. It is also not so reliable for marathons since as many of you will know only too well, anything can happen, and hitting "the Wall" is not accounted for in this method. Apart from this, I have personally found it very reliable and you will probably be surprised to find that your performance scores are very consistent over a wide range of race distances. This scheme was devised by Tom Osler in his 'Serious Running Handbook', one of a plethora of books to come out of the running boom in the late 1970s and early 1980s, mostly from the USA. items.s: Life Membership for John Davies Tribute marking John Davies's Life Membership: his football days, 1955–early 60s middle-distance career (800m 1:52, mile 4:10.4), 28 years with the Saturday Crowd, 68 marathons and the Bath Box he started. Life Membership for John Davies — Gordon Biscoe writes — Many will know of John and his background but if there is anyone who sees him only as one of the Saturday afternoon crowd who complains about his aching knees and waves the bath box under your nose we can enlighten you — he does have a past — and a very significant one. Like several of our other stars John's first sporting love was football where he played in the amateur ranks for Kingstonian, Wimbledon and Tottenham Hotspur (well we didn't say he was perfect!) However, in 1955 he decided a change was in order and turned to athletics. In May of that year he joined Belgrave and very quickly made his mark not only in our club but in the Athletics World in general. From 1955 to the early 60's John's track career as a middle-distance runner fell only just so very, very short of full international status, but it should be noted that at that time he was vying with some of the great names of the past — Hewson, Chataway, Brasher and Pirie to name but a few. These men all became his regular training partners and personal friends. Space does not permit a listing of all his achievements during this time but let's just record that he represented the A.A.A. on many occasions both at home and on the Continent, particularly in Sweden, and recorded personal best times of: 1:52 for 800m and 4:10.4 for 1 mile — all on cinders! He did not confine himself purely to 800's or miles, also becoming Club Champion at 3 miles and turning out regularly on the road and country when needed. In 1970 with his Track career behind him, John joined the 'Saturday Crowd' at Belgrave Hall and turned his attention to road running in earnest. That means he has now been going up to the Hall on a Saturday for 28 years — or from another angle, he's probably consumed something in the order of 1,456 cups of Brian Gorman's tea and eaten an equivalent number of sausage rolls! Amazing! And in spite of this he's completed 68 marathons including the London and is still with us! We must mention one of his other highlights, which was of course meeting Pam while training at Tooting. Pam, an International herself, must surely share in the credit for the honour of Life Membership bestowed upon John — for keeping our boy on the straight and narrow all this time! Throughout his 28 years as one of the Saturday Crowd John has performed an invaluable service to the Club in his own quiet unassuming way: helping out wherever needed, making new members feel welcome, advising and encouraging some of our younger ones and taking them out training. Then there's that Bath Box. It was his original idea to pass this around on Saturdays after training, to help offset some of our heating costs. Over the years he has literally raised hundreds of pounds. Second at the 'Valley' PUMA TVH ROAD RELAY STOCKLEY PK, 28 MAR 1998 In the second running of the revived 'TVH' road relays we moved up to the silver medals from last year's bronze. A super run from Gary Staines had him equalling the course record and taking the Bels. into the lead from the springboard of Graham Adam's opening stage but there was no denying the solid Shaftesbury outfit from thereon. A half-fit Bruce Barton kept us in the medals but then an uncharacteristic below-par run from Kevin Quinn had us slipping back to 4th. We were looking for a time perhaps a minute faster from young Kev. but even had he achieved it, the final result would have been exactly the same. A strong fight back by Roger Alsop took us to the line in 2nd and an overall time 16 seconds faster than that of '97. items.h: National Veterans C.C. Championships, Lloyd Park, 28 Mar 1998
items.sum: Report on the 1998 National Veterans Cross Country Championships at Lloyd Park, Croydon, where the club's new Laurie O'Hara Trophy was presented in memory of Laurie O'Hara and Jim Estall was second M40.
items.s: National Veterans C.C. Championships, Lloyd Park, 28 Mar 1998 Report on the 1998 National Veterans Cross Country Championships at Lloyd Park, Croydon, where the club's new Laurie O'Hara Trophy was presented in memory of Laurie O'Hara and Jim Estall was second M40. NATIONAL VETERANS C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS, LLOYD PARK, 28 MAR 1998 The National Veterans Cross Country Championships were held last March at one of our local venues, Lloyd Park in Croydon, and this provided a fitting occasion for Belgravians to gather in memory of the late Laurie O'Hara who had died almost exactly a year before. The Club had donated a new silver salver, the Laurie O'Hara Trophy, which was presented to the winner of the M65 race by Mrs Jean O'Hara, Laurie's widow, who had kindly attended the meeting with her son and his family. The start of the M50's and 60's race was preceded by a few moments silence. The end of the silence was greeted with a touching spontaneous applause for Jean and her son Laurie by the athletes, many of whom had known and raced Laurie in similar events for over twenty five years. Lloyd Park was bathed in warm sunshine for the event which was admirably organised by Southern Vets. The tough, undulating three lap course proved a true test for the runners, although perhaps a little over demanding for some of our less fit colleagues. It was also an excellent spectator course and it was good to see so many Belgravians who had come to run in spite of injury or lack of fitness, and others who had just come to support. Performance of the day was by Jim Estall, second in the M40 race. The M40 team actually got 6th place helped by an excellent run from John Mather who had been told "never run again". Pat Newell had been moving through nicely to the medal positions until his hamstring went at the end of the second lap and this cost our M60's a team bronze. Frank Gander was a revelation over the tough course and at the end looked as though he could go round a couple more times. Paul Evans' London Record Dented LONDON MARATHON 26 APR 1998 Paul Evan's marvellous record of achievement in this race took a dent when he was forced to pull out at 18 miles due to stomach cramps; his halfway time was inside 65 minutes. With Gary Staines taking on pacemaking duties and therefore only going half the distance it was therefore left to our redoubtable veteran Jim Estall to lead home the Belgrave contingent. It was good to see two Belles finishing within a few seconds of each other, just outside the top hundred. A couple more to join Nikki Haines and Rachel Weston and we might have figured in the women's team race. Dave McMillan looked absolutely awful as he clawed his way along Upper Thames Street with a couple of miles to go. He was some twenty minutes or so outside his target but one can hardly believe that this man, who spent months in a wheelchair recuperating from terrible injuries, was there at all. items.s: Belgrave - Nonsuch 4 x 2.25m Relay, Nonsuch Park, 9 Jul 1998 Report and results of the 1998 Belgrave-Nonsuch 4 x 2.25 mile relay, won by Belgrave 'B' after Ray Foley and Gary Staines swapped teams for a close finish. BELGRAVE - NONSUCH 4 x 2.25m RELAY NONSUCH PARK, 9 JUL 1998 This was the second time that Bill Law's company had sponsored this Dave Denton organized relay in our name and again the opposition from Alf Tupper ACM, Upton O Good, Epsom Oddballs and others enjoyed the chance to race our lads in claret and gold. Gary Staines started by carrying out a demolition job on Ray Foley's lap record while Kevin Quinn trimmed his best for this circuit. In his first relay for Belgrave Paul Coughlan extended the 'A' team's lead but just to make the finish more exciting, veteran Alan Black then ambled round giving Marcello Bizio the chance to take the 'B's ahead. Gary, going for a second circuit, was originally supposed to finish off for the 'B's who should then have been disqualified as he had already run – but he and Ray were busy swapping numbers and teams in an attempt to make the finish as close as possible and give each other the chance of some stiff competition at the end. As it turned out Ray was able to operate at 15 seconds inside his old lap record pace and Gary was unable to get near him in spite of running what became the second fastest lap of all time – and the 'A' team should have been disqualified – but wasn't. Confused? items.s: Yacht Handicap 3 miles, Wimbledon, 3 Oct 1998 Report and full result of the 1998 Yacht Handicap over 3 miles at Wimbledon, won by Tania Sturton from Vic Butcher, with Najibe Hliouat fastest man. YACHT HANDICAP 3 miles WIMBLEDON, 3 OCT 1998 The "Yacht" continues to maintain its popularity. The entry list was up slightly again and with a bit of effort we could surely push it well into the thirties once more. Things don't get any easier for Handicapper Arthur Bruce, however. He now has to work out projected times for athletes that range from 10 year old Louise Collier to septuagenarian Charlie Manning, from "come-back" specialist Vic Butcher to flying Moroccan Najibe Hliouat. Throw in a couple of runners who missed their proper start times – Steve Fowler went off at about 14:25 instead of 14:00 while James Skilbeck-Nelson set out much later than he should have done – and poor Jacqui Smiter's asthma attack in mid-race, and one can see that there was as much drama in the event as ever. Tania Sturton took advantage of Arthur's generosity to cut through those setting out ahead of her and reach home first with Vic Butcher in tow. Ex-long jumper Syreeta Stracey, now converting to middle-distance running, surprised by taking third place. items.s: League hopes 'blown away' in first fixture Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 Race 1 at Brockwell Park, 17 Oct 1998, where Belgrave men finished 6th and the young athletes took third (U17/U15) and second (U13). SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE DIVISION 1 – RACE 1 BROCKWELL PARK, 17 OCT 1998 League hopes 'blown away' in first fixture A "hoped for" place in the top four teams proved optimistic. A closely fought battle finally saw only 104 points covering positions 3rd to 8th with the Bels. near the back of that group in 6th. The Hounslow boys dominated the race, showing no regard for the blustery conditions. South London's Stuart Major, Hercules Wimbledon's Adrian Marriott, Herne Hill's Ian Munt and our own Najib Hliouat ran with them in the leading group which set out at such a fearful pace that Lee Hurst (30th in last year's 'National' remember), racing with a heart monitor for the first time, found himself running into trouble within the first mile. Najibe, it seemed, had bitten off more than he could chew and although still fighting with the leaders as the first lap came to an end, pulled out of the race at half way. Lee Hurst was now recovering from the blistering start and holding on as our leading scorer with Jim Estall making a great showing close behind and staking an early claim for the position of top veteran. What a pity that Veteran International duty will rule him out of the second match and thus not allow him to retain his title. And so to the finish. Hounslow, so strong at the front, had to go back a fair way to close in their ten men and thus let in the solid Thames Hare & Hounds team who always pack so well in the 20s to 40s. After that it was almost impossible to immediately judge the next seven teams. Will Cockerell scored for us for the first time and Italian Saul Armanini should be well pleased with his first run in Belgrave colours – he will be eligible to score for us come the new year. Hounslow were just as assertive at the sharp end of the youngsters' event and easily carried off both the under 17 and under 13 team races. Thanks to Reg Hopkins' persuasive powers, though, Belgrave were one of only three teams that managed to turn out a full quota of runners in the older lads' race and were repaid with third place, led home as ever by Manuel Garcia. No club had a full five in the under 13 contest where Belgrave numbered four boys who excelled in gaining second, top scorer being Philip Doorgachurn. 145 finished 13 finished 1, Thames H&H (5, 13, 15, 23, 29, 32, 42, 45, 48, 51) 303 2, Boro' of Hounslow (1, 2, 3, 21, 24, 33, 44, 55, 76, 77) 336 3, Ranelagh H (10, 16, 20, 36, 37, 47, 56, 59, 65, 74) 420 4, Herne Hill H ( 7, 17, 18, 35, 39, 41, 66, 67, 68, 73) 431 5, South London H ( 6, 14, 26, 27, 30, 60, 62, 63, 78, 83) 449 6, Belgrave H (9, 11, 22, 40, 49, 54, 58, 64, 71, 87) 465 7, Boxhill R (8, 25, 31, 38, 43, 52, 69, 70, 80, 82) 498 8, Aldershot F&D (12, 19, 28, 34, 46, 50, 72, 85, 88, 90) 524 9, Hercules Wimbledon AC (4, 53, 57, 61, 75, 79, 81, 84, 86, 89) 669 1, S.Haughian (Hounslow) 23:22 2, B.Whitby (Hounslow) 23:38 3, M.Simpson (Hounslow) 23:38 9, L.Hurst 24:36 11, J.Estall (M40) 24:46 22, R.Foley 25:06 40, C.Gilby 25:39 51, K.Quinn (U20M) 26:04 57, P.Carstairs 26:15 61, S.Armanini (n/s) 26:27 65, M.Webb 26:36 71, W.Cockerell 26:53 79, J.Galley 27:09 105, J.Mather (M40) 28:26 114, W.Minett (U20M) 29:03 116, R.Harding 29:09 136, R.Bale (M50) 32:09 141, L.Mann (M55) 36:28 1, M.Farah (Hounslow) 11:58 4, M.Garcia 12:58 16, C.Morris 14:10 22, J.Skilbeck-Nelson (U15B) 14:52 34, A.Wright (U15B) 18:02 32, N.Waller (U15B) 18:48 1, Boro' of Hounslow 25 2, Hercules Wimbledon AC 60 3, Belgrave H 86 1, S.Chapman (Hounslow) 14:50 5, P.Doorgachurn 16:45 10, R.Collier 18:50 11, J.Fitzgerald 18:54 12, B.Hodgson 19:00 1, Boro' of Hounslow 39½ 2, Belgrave H 67½ 3, Herne Hill H 83 Rob Harding, Ray Foley, Mike Webb, Clive Gilby, Kevin Quinn, Jim Estall John Mather and Lee Hurst steel themselves for the start of the first Surrey League race of 1998-99. items.s: 'Belles' start strongly Report and results of Women's Surrey CC League Division 2 Race 1 at Tilford, 17 Oct 1998, where Belgrave women were second to Wimbledon Windmilers. WOMENS SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 2 – RACE 1 TILFORD, 17 OCT 1998 'Belles' start strongly 17 teams closed in After a closely fought match at Tilford our women's cross country team showed their new Team Manager Jacqui Smiter that they have no intention in spending longer than is necessary in Division Two of the Surrey League. We saw some good running from Tania Sturton last winter and her 9th place showed that she has made good progress with the passing of another 12 months. Proving that her run in the Yacht Handicap was no fluke, Syretta Stracey turned in another impressive performance and with Cathy Eastham, Nina Mills and Sam Symonds to close in the team we were only narrowly beaten by the Windmilers. The rise in standard was not restricted to the senior women's team for Debbie Hearn was our highest placed runner of the afternoon when she came home 3rd in the under 17 race and Louise Collier and Genya Marek ensured that we were well represented in each of the other age groups. 77 finished 16 finished 30 finished 24 finished 1, Wimbledon Windmilers (6, 10, 14, 31, 48) 109 2, Belgrave H (9, 16, 22, 35, 37) 119 3, Stragglers (5, 23, 25, 26, 42) 121 1, S.Cook (Guildford & G) 19:38 2, S.Blackett (Dulwich Pk) 20:22 3, E.Carbone (Sutton & D) 20:30 9, T.Sturton 22:05 16, S.Stracey 23:14 22, C.Eastham 23:53 35, N.Mills (W50) 25:09 37, S.Symonds 25:10 1, A.Lucas (Sutton) 18:15 2, S.Doe (Ranelagh) 18:51 3, D.Hearn (Belgrave) 19:33 1, L.Vyse (Woking) 14:40 25, G.Marek 18:52 1, E.Secker (Kingston & P) 13:03 8, L.Collier 14:06 Jacqui Smiter Jacqui Smiter new women's cross country Team Manager Tania Sturton Tania Sturton 9th Tania Sturton T.Sturton Syretta Stracey Syretta Stracey Syretta Stracey S.Stracey Cathy Eastham Cathy Eastham Cathy Eastham C.Eastham Nina Mills Nina Mills W50 Nina Mills N.Mills Sam Symonds Sam Symonds Sam Symonds S.Symonds Debbie Hearn Debbie Hearn 3rd under 17 women Debbie Hearn D.Hearn Louise Collier Louise Collier Louise Collier L.Collier Genya Marek Genya Marek Genya Marek G.Marek S.Cook S.Cook S.Blackett S.Blackett E.Carbone E.Carbone A.Lucas A.Lucas S.Doe S.Doe L.Vyse L.Vyse E.Secker E.Secker Surrey Women's Cross Country League Yacht Handicap Tilford Wimbledon Windmilers Stragglers Guildford & G Dulwich Pk Sutton & D Sutton Ranelagh Woking Kingston & P Windmilers

items.s: Priory Cross Country Relays, Reigate, 7 Nov 1998 Report and results of the 1998 Priory Cross Country Relays at Reigate, where Belgrave men were 5th with Clive Gilby fastest and the women's team moved up to 6th. PRIORY CROSS COUNTRY RELAYS, REIGATE, 7 NOV 1998 Everyone seems to want to run on the first leg and this time Paul Coughlan got the nod. South London clearly led the field home thanks to Stuart Major's opening 13:15 while Paul's 7th place among a knot of other runners gave Kevin Quinn plenty of opposition to get stuck into. Kevin moved up two places before handing over to Junior Galley who dropped back one slot during his circuit. How this man runs on the grassy slopes without spikes we'll never know. Once again Clive Gilby was our fastest man, although not so fit as the same time last season when his 13:13 gave him 3rd fastest of the day. Clive's run gave us our highest placing throughout the race but also put an unfit Graham Adams, just off the plane from holidaying in the USA, in the unenviable position of setting out with Boxhill's Simon Fairbrother on his tail. Tony Barden finished off for the Bels. and then prepared to cheer on his partner Lisa Thompson running for the SLH women's 'B' team. The Belgrave women's team were a revelation. Fifteenth in 1997, this time around they cut their overall time by 3 minutes to move up to 6th – "Just one place lower than the men's team" a gleeful Jacqui Smiter announced. Tania Sturton set the ball rolling by reducing her time by 1:40 to set our fastest time of the day in coming home 8th. She had to be at her best because Debbie Hearn had taken the initiative at the start for the 'B' team and completed her lap just two places behind in 18:32 – last year she was our fastest with 19:07. Cathy Eastham maintained the pressure by holding on to 8th and taking a minute off her previous best while Syretta Stracey moved the team up another two places with an outstanding 18:21 and then looked as if she could hardly believe her performance herself. Vicky Pincott running for her first-claim club Horsham Blue Star's 'B' team clocked 19:43. items.s: Now Jacqui's team go top Report and results of Women's Surrey CC League Division 2 Race 2 at Brockwell Park, 14 Nov 1998, where Belgrave won the match and took the league lead. WOMENS SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 2 – RACE 2 BROCKWELL PARK, 14 NOV 1998 Now Jacqui's team go top 18 teams closed in In spite of the stronger field than in the first race of this winter's series the Belles, led home by Helen Maskrey, excelled themselves on Brockwell Park's rolling hills to take first team place. Another strong run came from Tania Sturton and with Syretta Stracey maintaining her 16th place, Cathy Eastham moving up two places and Sam Symonds no fewer that nine, a devastating blow was dealt to the other clubs in division two and – barring accidents – it is beginnning to look as if promotion beckons. Wimbledon Windmilers, leaders after the first race, crashed on this occasion and could finish no higher than 11th so with two races gone and two more to come Belgrave took a clear lead on the league table with 34 points while Dulwich Park and Stragglers are tying on 31. Debbie Hearn's training is obviously paying off. In the under 17 women's race she moved up to 2nd place, just six seconds behind the winner. Do you know we might just see her come home as a race winner before the season is out. Down in the youngest age group Louise Collier improved to 6th and with a couple more years in the same category is surely one of our stars for the future. 79 finished 16 finished 18 finished 1, Belgrave H (7, 11, 16, 20, 28) 82 2, Dulwich Park (3, 14, 18, 36, 39) 110 3, Stragglers (9, 23, 31, 34, 38) 135 1, S.Cook (Guildford) 22:15 2, M.Statham (Holl. items.h: So near to an historic double win
items.sum: Report and results of the 1998 South of Thames C.C. Association Junior race at Beckenham, won by Jason Lobo; Belgrave lost the team race to Crawley by one point after a recount but kept the Brent Shield.
e: South of Thames Junior Cross Country Championships
items.s: So near to an historic double win Report and results of the 1998 South of Thames C.C. Association Junior race at Beckenham, won by Jason Lobo; Belgrave lost the team race to Crawley by one point after a recount but kept the Brent Shield. SOUTH OF THAMES C.C. ASSOCN. "JUNIOR" RACE BECKENHAM, 14 NOV 1998 So near to an historic double win 20 teams closed in. 8 teams closed in. Due to the stringent barring clauses, one of which is the exclusion of all scoring members of a previous winning team, only two teams have ever taken home the winner's shield in consecutive years. Aldershot F&D did it in '73 and '74, and then again in '85 and '86. Belgrave have to go back to '45 and 46. As winners in 1997 the challenge was on. We lost two outstanding runners when Mark Miles found that he had to work and Najibe Hliouat went missing but there was still a chance that we might pull it off. Within seconds of the start Jason Lobo stamped his mark on the race. Loping away from the field, he added 25 metres to his lead with each circuit of the first two small laps and once into the woods was out of sight of the chasing bunch, eventually coming home nearly a minute clear. As Commonwealth Games 800 metre representative he has not done much in the way of cross country for the last few years – but we certainly hope he does some more! Paul Coughlan and Kevin Quinn made more conservative starts while Junior Galley, although much happier on tarmac, had "gone for it" in a big way. They were 9th, 20th and 24th after the opening rush and had moved up again as the Ash Plantation was tackled – 5th, 14th and 19th. Blackheath and Crawley also had plenty of men forward but at this stage the race looked ours. A mile or so later, however, it was very much closer. Paul was now in 3rd and Kevin 9th but Junior was finding the slippery banks far from his liking and had slipped back to 30th with Tony Binda and Mike Nouch drawing ever closer to him. Crawley, with four men in 13 and another to back them up, were now edging us by a single point. While Jason Lobo crossed the line in utmost comfort a battle royal was drawing to a close for 2nd and 3rd places. Our 'Kiwi' Coughlan and Klepacz of Portsmouth had both fallen on the last lap but as the funnel was approached it was the Belgravian who prevailed. He was "all in" but delighted to have got himself silver medal, having run out of his socks in more ways than one: he had actually left them at home and had raced without any! Maybe he should do it more often. A super run from Kevin had got him up to 8th – but where was our 4th man? Eventually it was veteran Tony Binda, finishing like a train, who closed in our four. Mike Nouch had also got the better of Junior on that last lap and now it was time to tot up the scores. The Crawley team manager told us that his men had 46. We had 44 and Blackheath 48. We'd done it – or had we? Something was not quite right and a recount by the Sussex men showed that their arithmetic was not quite so hot as their running – they now made it 43 and had in fact pipped us by a point. Never mind, it was a great race, and the eight-man Brent Shield stayed in our hands thanks to Junior, who somehow kept going when he really would have preferred to go home, and tough old dogs John Mather and Don Anderson. And think of the good news – with only Coughlan and Lobo barred we have the makings of another good showing in 1999. 126 finished 1, Crawley (7, 11, 12, 13) 43 2, Belgrave (1, 2, 8, 33) 44 3, Blackheath (6, 9, 10, 23) 48 1, Belgrave (1, 2, 8, 33, 43, 47, 57, 59) 250 2, Crawley (7, 11, 12, 13, 24, 56, 63, 72) 258 3, City of Portsmouth (3, 18, 20, 21, 51, 55, 67, 118) 353 1, J.Lobo (Belgrave) 32.25 2, P.Coughlan (Belgrave) 33:17 3, G.Klepacz (Portsmouth) 33:21 8, K.Quinn (U20M) 34:06 33, A.Binda (M40) 35:52 43, M.Nouch (M40) 36:28 47, J.Galley 36:45 57, J.Mather (M40) 37:43 59, D.Anderson (M40) 37:51 Mark Miles Mark Miles missed the race through work Najibe Hliouat Najibe Hliouat missing from the team Jason Lobo Jason Lobo won by nearly a minute; Commonwealth Games 800 metre representative Jason Lobo Lobo J.Lobo Paul Coughlan Paul Coughlan 2nd; raced without socks Paul Coughlan Paul 'Kiwi' Coughlan Coughlan P.Coughlan Kevin Quinn Kevin Quinn 8th; U20M Kevin Quinn Kevin K.Quinn Junior Galley Junior Galley Junior Galley Junior J.Galley Tony Binda Tony Binda M40; 4th Belgrave scorer Tony Binda A.Binda Mike Nouch Mike Nouch M40 Mike Nouch M.Nouch John Mather John Mather M40 John Mather J.Mather Don Anderson Don Anderson M40 Don Anderson D.Anderson G.Klepacz Klepacz 3rd Klepacz G.Klepacz South of Thames Junior Cross Country Championships Brent Shield Commonwealth Games Beckenham Ash Plantation Crawley Blackheath City of Portsmouth Aldershot F&D Portsmouth

items.s: Second on the Common but 'Thames' increase their lead Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 Race 2, hosted by Belgrave on Wimbledon Common on 21 Nov 1998, where the men placed 2nd and moved up to 3rd overall. SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE DIVISION 1 – RACE 2 WIMBLEDON COMMON, 21 NOV 1998 Second on the Common but 'Thames' increase their lead Our home match and things were looking a bit bleak as, with only twenty minutes to start time, we had as many non-scorers on the declaration list as scorers. And then it came together: Clive Gilby (took him longer to get there than he thought it would), Lee Hurst (with Carly having travelled from Manchester to Euston, to Waterloo, to Wimbledon), Ray Foley (with Anna and new baby Tess), Phil Carstairs (would he ever let us down) and others all arrived within a few minutes. By the time a claret and gold scarf was dropped to set the field on its way we had 14 scorers and 5 others on the line – but there were several expected Belgrave runners who never made it. Hounslow suffered badly as their international trio gave the race a miss but the other main protagonists from race 1 all joined battle again in the fine, crisp conditions. After the dash across the golf course and down the hill to the playing fields, five runners gradually detached themselves from the main field. Through the woods and then climbing back up to the end of the first lap it was Munt (Herne Hill), Matthews (Thames H&H), Major (South London), Marriott (Hercules Wimbledon) and Lee Hurst bowling along at the front with barely a whisker between them. Then came the main stream of the pack with another three Belgravians in the first twenty. Once again it looked like a tight race between 2nd and 4th but it was obvious that Thames Hare & Hounds were tightening their grip on the league with a full team of ten white vests bearing the saltire in the first 50. There was much chopping and changing among the leaders during lap two but the pattern had been set. Lee held on to his 5th while Clive Gilby showed a terrific improvement in form to get into the Surrey League top ten for the first time. Paul Coughlan might have been expected to have been a little jaded after his all-out effort in the South of Thames race the previous week but he and rival Ray Foley had great runs and as a result we had four home in the very thick of the action. It was good to have Mike Kazimierski getting back to fitness again. Steve Fowler always produces the goods when he turns out and Phil Carstairs was another to turn in a strong run. Our Junior Captain Kevin Quinn reached his best ever league position and scanning through the results we note that no other under 20 appeared ahead of him. The ever-dependable Mike Webb and Will Cockerall closed in the team with Saul Armanini showing once again that he'll soon be helping reduce our points score. Many thanks to the pointsmen who gave up their Saturday afternoon runs to assist with the race – to trail-layers Don Anderson and Tony Binda – to the timekeepers and judges and recorders – and the results team. By the time a pint of Guinness was being supped in the 'King of Denmark' where the results were being pored over by the core members of the team and their supporters, we could feel pleased with a day items.sum: Report and results of the 1998–99 county cross country championships (Surrey at Old Coulsdon plus Belgravians in Essex, Hampshire and Kent), with Jim Estall 7th and Ray Foley 8th in the Surrey senior men's race; the heading dates it 12 Dec 1998 while the Essex and Kent results are dated 9th Jan 1999.
items.s: County Cross Country Champs. 12 Dec 1998 Report and results of the 1998–99 county cross country championships (Surrey at Old Coulsdon plus Belgravians in Essex, Hampshire and Kent), with Jim Estall 7th and Ray Foley 8th in the Surrey senior men's race; the heading dates it 12 Dec 1998 while the Essex and Kent results are dated 9th Jan 1999. COUNTY CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPS. 12 DEC 1998 What a disappointing day. At Old Coulsdon for the 'Surreys' the steady drizzle soaked us all through and the liquid mud around the start area crept into trainers and kit bags alike. But the real 'downer' was the fact that barring our under 20 men, we were unable to complete a single team and, in the younger age groups, both male and female, we failed to turn out any runners at all. We really ought to be making a lot more of an impression in the Surrey County Champs. than we do. Ok so we won the men's race a couple of years back and the women's event a while before that but so often it's a struggle to find the runners who'll do it. This year, with Jim Estall and Ray Foley running so well and with Kevin Nash expected to take part we thought we had a really good start in the men's event. Graham Adams is coming back to fitness so Roger Alsop and Junior Galley were persuaded to make up the team. But as the gun was fired we were still only five in number and when the results were published later in the week we were amazed to find that Kevin Nash had run in the Hampshire event! Jim's run proved to be another cracker and Ray had his best ever 'County' run, even having the audacity to get up to our 'super-vet's' shoulder and overtake him for a brief period with a mile or so to go. Congratulations to team winners South London Harriers it was their first win in 23 years. We were also one short in the senior women's team race where Helen Maskrey led home Syreeta Stracey and Cathy Eastham who were surprised to find that the distance was a full 8 kilometres. Tania Sturton and Debbie Hearn kept the Belgrave flag flying in the 4.8 kms. race in which both the under 20s and under 17s ran together. James Venning came back from Southampton University to run in our under 20 men's team but running in the mud with spikes that were no more than 'rivets', it was not surprising that he had trouble keeping on his feet. New members Robert Palmer and Tom Knowles completed our team but we missed Kevin Quinn who was out with 'flu' and could manage no higher than 5th team. items.s: Promotion beckons for the Belles Report and results of Women's Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 Race 3 at Petersham, Richmond Park, on 9 Jan 1999, where the Belgrave women won the race and extended their lead for promotion. WOMENS SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 2 – RACE 3 PETERSHAM, RICHMOND PARK, 9 JAN 1999 Promotion beckons for the Belles 17 teams closed in Another win for the Belles meant that we are vitually certain now of winning the Division Two title this winter — but it could so easily have gone wrong. With only four Belgrave girls certain to run in the days leading up to the race (and you need five for a full team), team boss Jacqui Smiter was delighted to receive a 'phone call from Nikki Haines on the morning of the race asking if she could run. Nikki works for Adidas and spends a great deal of her time abroad these days, making it difficult for her to race as often as she'd like. Even then Jacqui had to go through a warm up routine when Tania Sturton and Helen Maskrey only got to the start with five minutes to spare — the joys of being a team manager! Conditions were cold and muddy but they seemed to suit Nikki who celebrated her return to the team by leading them home in 7th place. Helen and Tania weren't far behind and with Sam Symonds running well and Nina Mills closing in the team we'd done it, with some 20-odd points to spare. Our lead in the race for promotion was now up to 4 league points over Stragglers with Dulwich Park Runners a further point in arrears. In the younger age groups Genya Marek ran well among the under 15s and Debbie Hearn continued to make her presence felt among the under 17s, this time with 3rd place. In the youngest group of all it was a complete turn-around from recent years as we fielded no fewer than eight girls with the smallest lass of all, Louise Collier, spearheading the Belgrave pack. 1, Belgrave H (7, 9, 15, 25, 38) 94 2, Stragglers (10, 23, 24, 29, 32) 118 3, Dulwich Park (2, 11, 48, 49, 50) 160 1, K.Ramsey (Walton) 21:11 2, S.Blackett (Dulwich Pk) 21:23 3, E.Viljoen (Herc.Wimb) 21:41 7, N.Haines 23:00 9, H.Maskrey 23:22 15, T.Sturton (U20) 24:32 25, S.Symonds 26:01 38, N.Mills 27:29 85 finished 1, A.Lucas (Sutton) 18:13 3, D.Hearn (Belgrave) 19:13 16 finished Teams: 1, Sutton &D 19 2, Epsom & Ewell 14 3, Guildford & G 55 5, Belgrave H 75 1, L.Vyse (Woking) 13:40 20, G.Marek 17:13 30 finished 1, Herc. items.s: Young guns go for it! Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 Race 3 at Petersham, Richmond Park, on 16 Jan 1999, where Belgrave won the match but stayed 2nd overall behind Thames Hare & Hounds. SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE DIVISION 1 – RACE 3 PETERSHAM, RICHMOND PARK, 16 JAN 1999 Young guns go for it! A thrilled Adrian Marriott raised his arm aloft as he crossed the line for Hercules Wimbledon at the head of a good class field at Petersham to stake a clear lead in the individual competition. It had been a hard fought win and our own Kassa Tadesse, not as fit as he would like, had to suffer the indignity of placing outside the frame — nevertheless with our highest individual league position of the winter so far. But even though we had no-one in the first three it was a good day for the Bels. At last we were able to see what Kevin Nash is made of — and we like it. This young man's got great talent and at not quite 22 years of age we look forward to many more outings from him in the future. Another to make his début in the team and to earn instant respect was Hassan Raidi. At just turned 20 this young Moroccan really looks the business and with his countryman Najibe Hliouat, 21, setting out a little more cautiously than he did at Brockwell Park we suddenly found that we had exciting company for stalwart Jim Estall. Jim was suffering from backache but it was going to take more than that to keep him down the field. It was good to see Roger Alsop easing back into racing and he and Will Cockerell had a rare old ding-dong over the second lap, passing some ten or a dozen runners around the second lap as they closed in the ten. It is difficult to see now how the team positions can be changed much in the final race. Although we pulled back 50 points on Thames Hare & Hounds, they are still over 200 clear. Once again we have paid the penalty for a poor start at Brockwell Park. Down in the basement there seems to be no way that Boxhill Racers and Hercules Wimbledon can avoid the drop. items.h: A new course for our home races
items.sum: Notice that Belgrave's home cross country races on Wimbledon Common are likely to move to a new course next winter, away from the golf fairways, with the route described.
items.s: A new course for our home races Notice that Belgrave's home cross country races on Wimbledon Common are likely to move to a new course next winter, away from the golf fairways, with the route described. A new course for our home races The chances are that next winter we will be running over a new course on Wimbledon Common. A series of meetings have been held between the two golf Clubs that use the Common - London Scottish and Wimbledon Common - and athletic clubs: Thames Hare & Hounds, Hercules Wimbledon, Veterans A.C., Wimbledon Windmilers, Lauriston Runners and ourselves. Cross country races have often been held without a warning being given to the golfers and as a result, golfing tournaments have been held up. Additionally there has been some concern about runners being hit by golf balls as they race out of the wooded areas and across the fairways. For some time we have been thinking of reverting to our old course starting not far from the Pound near the corner of Cannizaro Road and Parkside and as a result of the safety concerns shown by both runners and golfers, now seems to be the time to do it. The course will head for the Windmill across The Plain, then pass the Mounds, turn left down towards Queensmere, go alongside the lake and up hill to the Windmill, returning to the start via what we know as The Avenue and Memorial Ride. Not once will we cross a single fairway. Shorter courses based on this circuit will be suitable for very young runners. The Common Rangers have agreed to help us with a bit of 'gardening' to smooth out the tussocks and remove some posts and as we will be using horse rides in a few places, riding will not be permitted on these stretches during advised race days. items.s: We actually finish a team in the 'Southern'! Report and results of the South of England (SEAA) cross country championships at Parliament Hill on 30 Jan 1999, where Belgrave closed in a senior men's team for once, placing 16th. We actually finish a team in the 'Southern'! SEAA C. C. CHAMPS., PARLIAMENT HILL, 30 JAN 1999 At last! It makes things so much more worth while when we can round up enough people to actually complete a team — never mind where they came — at least we've now got something to work on. After weeks of rain this was Parliament Hill Fields at its best (worst?). The initial climb up the hill was like a skating rink, the dips were full of black porridge and the ditch, well, there were runners going down like ninepins as they misjudged the downward slope and the leap across the mud. We had three girls in action but each in different age groups so were unable to close in a female team. When you look at the results, that Junior Women's race managed to bring together just three complete teams of four runners. Would it be possible for us to find three others to join Debbie Hearn for next year and who knows, maybe pick up our first Southern medals in aeons. Good running came from Tania Sturton, currently our only under 20, as she claimed our highest place of the day with 34th. It was pleasing to see that one of our Folkestone members from a couple of seasons back — Janine Brown — got up to 25th and actually closed in the winning Ashford AC's scoring four. Cathy Eastham did not relish 5 miles of 'Parly Hill' but did well to finish half-way down the senior field. Among the Senior Men Lee Hurst quite obviously did not enjoy the mud and at 66th was well down on his 12th of last winter. Blackheath's Mark Steinle was up and away by the end of the first circuit and seemed to float over the morass to come home half a minute clear. He was clearly the superior runner on the day but just how much the conditions affected the runners can be judged by the fact that his winning time was 4 minutes slower than last year. Phil Carstairs often seems to turn in a good 'Southern' and this one was no exception, while Italian Saul Armanini, in his first ever scoring race for the Bels, finished much further up the field than we anticipated. Saul is going to be a very useful man to have around. Mike Webb, back from a business trip to Singapore, and Rob Harding, who had an excellent run having left his push-bike at home for a change and taken the tube from New Cross, meant that we had five home in just outside the first quarter of the field. Finally the tall figure of Jerome Curtat, a native of Metz in France, kept himself going through the slime to close in our team. items.h: A sorry finish to the Men's Surrey League
items.sum: Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 Race 4 at Coulsdon (Farthing Downs) on 27 Feb 1999, where an injury-hit Belgrave team placed 6th and dropped to 3rd overall.
items.s: A sorry finish to the Men's Surrey League Report and results of Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 Race 4 at Coulsdon (Farthing Downs) on 27 Feb 1999, where an injury-hit Belgrave team placed 6th and dropped to 3rd overall. A sorry finish to the Men's Surrey League SURREY C. C. LEAGUE DIVISION 1 – RACE 4 COULSDON, 27 FEB 1999 Just to keep our feet firmly on the ground after team wins in our two previous outings, our perfomance in the final league fixture was, well, 'a disaster' is probably too strong a description when we still ended up in the top half of the division, so let's settle for 'abysmal'. There was nothing we could do about it really. Five runners came out during the preceding week with injuries and other commitments, two more overnight with colds and then another one having to work. Four more didn't make it on the afternoon — and then two came out after one lap of Farthing Downs. Miraculously, after losing fourteen men we still had ten scorers, thanks to race walker Mabon Dane who closed in our team. Thames Hare & Hounds turned out their strongest squad to retain the league trophy and Herne Hill also got it together in a big way, storming through from 5th league place to 2nd, pushing us down to 3rd. … And there was us thinking that the final team positions were unlikely to change in this last event. Hounslow's Junior international Sam Haughian was awesome as he destroyed the chances of Taylor and his club-mate Simpson — one of the best individual wins for a long time. For the Bels., we welcomed Charles 'bandana' Herrington into the team, unfortunately only as a non-scorer. Sporting claret head-gear, Charles was always our top scorer, ahead of Najibe Hliouat (before he called it a day) and comfortably up on Paul Coughlan, who was having a good run himself. Rob Harding is getting stronger with each outing while Phil Carstairs was way below his best and suffering from a cold which really should have stopped him running. Well, that's it for another league campaign. Our performances in the last few winters have been solid and we have established ourselves as a "top half of the league" team, but if we want to win it we are going to have to come out with all guns blazing in race one. items.sum: Notice that a cup bought with Bill Merryman's bequest will be awarded annually to the Young Belgravian of the Year for the most outstanding contribution to the Club.
items.s: The Bill Merryman Cup for the Young Belgravian of the Year Notice that a cup bought with Bill Merryman's bequest will be awarded annually to the Young Belgravian of the Year for the most outstanding contribution to the Club. The Bill Merryman Cup for the Young Belgravian of the Year When Bill Merryman passed away he left the Club a sum of money and it was his wish that we purchase a trophy to be competed for annually. After much deliberation the Committee have decided on a handsome cup which will be awarded annually to the Young Belgravian of the Year. It will be awarded to the young man or women that the Committee decides has made the most outstanding contribution to the Club throughout the previous 12 months - a contribution that is not necessarily one that can be measured in terms of athletic excellence or the most team points. LEAGUE DIVISION 2 – RACE 4, LLOYD PARK, 27 FEB 1999 While the men were struggling at Coulsdon, the women's race at nearby Lloyd Park saw the Belles turn on their strongest performance of the winter to win the final Division Two fixture and thereby make absolutely certain of a return to Division One for the 1999/2000 season. The win was emphatic with all five scorers closing in within a dozen places. Nikki Haines and Helen Maskrey led the way with Tania Sturton beathing down their necks and carrying off the prize for the best Under 20 throughout the overall competition. Both Syreeta Stracey and Cathy Eastham have come on tremendously throughout the season there is no doubt that we now have a nucleus of runners who should be able to maintain a Division One place. We just need a few more runners to commit themselves to racing and we'll then have the strength in depth that is so necessary to maintain upward progression.
