items.sum: Report and results of the 100th South of Thames Cross Country Championship at Sparrow's Den, West Wickham, on 13 Feb 1999, where Belgrave retained both the Dewar Shield and the Coleman Cup, with Najibe Hliouat 4th; photos of the winning team and the race follow on page 55.
e: South of Thames Cross Country Championships
items.s: Harriers swoop on Sparrow's Den Report and results of the 100th South of Thames Cross Country Championship at Sparrow's Den, West Wickham, on 13 Feb 1999, where Belgrave retained both the Dewar Shield and the Coleman Cup, with Najibe Hliouat 4th; photos of the winning team and the race follow on page 55. Harriers swoop on Sparrow's Den Dewar Shield & Coleman Cup Retained in 100th Championship Race SOUTH OF THAMES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP SPARROW'S DEN, WEST WICKHAM, 13 FEB 1999 Cross country days don't come much sweeter than this. Hard work during the preceding ten days resulted in thirteen men packing into their starting pen at Sparrow's Den, West Wickham, spilling over into the next pen as a friendly team without aspirations as to the team prizes offered to line up behind us. Just to remind you, the team that wins the Dewar Shield for the six-a-side championship race gets its scoring men barred from all subsequent races for the next ten years — and as we won it last year, we did not expect to be able to pull it off again. Therefore all effort was put behind the twelve-a-side race for the Coleman Cup. Various members of our team had other ideas though and in spite of the fact that this 100th running of the event was being held on Blackheath's patch and they seemed to have the strongest outfit, claret and gold was prominent among the leading colours streaming around the first circuit of the playing fields. It was Herne Hill who seemed to have the most men forward while Chris Knight of GEC Avionics took an early lead, chased hard by our own Najibe Hliouat. Up through the woods and then down again and it could be seen that Blackheath had three or four in the top ten and Portsmouth were also packing well. Halfway through the race and Najibe was becoming isolated as Knight drew ever further away to become a convincing winner. Paul Coughlan was chasing a whole mob of runners fighting for top ten positions and Roger Alsop was running way above his early winter form; he had to, because behind him four more Belgravians were disputing who was going to get into the scoring six. It was almost impossible to tally the scores of the four main teams but it did seem that we were just shading Blackheath for the championship while Herne Hill were slipping back a little. It was those Portsmouth vests that were difficult to pick up though and several onlookers believed that they might be the men in charge. As expected, the twelve man event looked more of a certainty, with Mike Kazimierski, Charlie Dickinson and Junior Captain Kevin Quinn hovering around the 50s and Rob Harding and Don Anderson closing in the dozen. Kevin had no intention of getting into the scoring six — he is still planning an assault on the Junior race next winter and doesn't want to get barred — but Chas. Dickinson did not appreciate him running a faartlek session and getting under his feet, eventually snapping with a "Sod off and get up the field will you!" The final circuit saw Will Cockerell come charging through, displacing Saul Armanini as sixth man and all but getting the best of Phil Carstairs as well. Both were breathing down the neck of Captain 'Gerry' Adams who in turn had his sights on Roger. Paul Coughlan's recent heavy mileage left him unable to jump the bunch ahead of him which included several black vests of the home club. Meanwhile, towards the front Najibe had been caught by Thames's Oxborough and then by Dover of Herne Hill, but he was hanging on grimly to his 4th place. A good crowd of Belgrave spectators including former Team Managers Bill Lucas and Gordon Biscoe were desperately urging on their men but it was going to have to be left to the man who currently does the pencil and paper work to tot up the numbers on the discs. While Team Manager Alan Mead came up with a Belgrave score of 95, John Jeffery was looking over the shoulder Blackheath's John Baldwin — and then came scuttling back with, "They've got 103." The Portsmouth man was bemoaning the fact that one of his forward placed runners had dropped out of the race with stitch, and they would have won it otherwise. News hound Martin Duff picked up on this in his AW report — but isn't having sound wind and fitness all part of the race? Our boys were cock-a-hoop and as our President rounded them up for a team photo' we now contemplated the fact that we have another six men barred from the race. Surely we'll be way down the field next year. Blackheath Harriers had laid on a fine celebratory buffet at their club house for this 100th race. Past winners were in attendance, including our own Denis Brickwood, Bill Lucas, Charlie Walker and Roger Alsop. Fine words were spoken and toasts drunk — it was good old traditional harrier evening. With Derek Crookes, in his 23rd year as the Association's Secretary, keeping the proceedings moving, Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and Committee man Alan Black also there, together with Past President Gordon Biscoe, we had as strong a Belgrave presence as there had been among the runners during the afternoon. … And when Marianne Black, Pat Mead and Jim Heathfield picked up three of the four raffle prizes our day was complete. 180 finished. items.s: Three in a row? Short piece noting that Belgrave's South of Thames team results are the best since 1945–51, giving the venue and date of the 2000 race and listing Belgrave men still eligible. Three in a row? We now have to go back to the post war years of 1945-51 to find a sequence of South of Thames team results that match what we have achieved in the last couple of winters. And remember, we only lost the Junior race before Christmas by one point! Surely we can't win the Championship next year and make it three in a row — or can we? The race will be held at Crawley on 22nd January 2000 and the distance will be reduced to 10 kms due to the fact that it will be held the week before the Southern CC Champs. items.s: Mean Fiddler! Short piece congratulating Hon. Treasurer Derek Manning on the club's Burns Night 1999 at Belgrave Hall. Mean Fiddler! Derek Manning comes up trumps again No, we're not casting aspersions on Derek's abilities as Hon. Treasurer. It's just that we must congratulate him on yet another triumph on the occasion of Burns Night 1999 when, with Lionel Mann masterminding the culinary side of things, we had the best 'do' at Belgrave Hall in years. All previous Burns Nights have been great occasions but this one exceeded them all: the Scotch, the Haggis, the Piper, the folk duo, the Ceilidh, Derek's performance as ventriloquist with brother Charlie as the dummy - but most of all that fiddler. Can't wait for next year Derek Manning Derek Manning Hon. He's done it again! First Belgrave man home in the Belgrave Open 7 miles on November 28th - John Hall. Above: The start of the Belgrave 7 miles Walk, 28th November 1998, won by Darell Stone of Steyning from Chris Maddocks of Plymouth who led for most of the race. Below: There's a fair few miles been walked by the legs belonging to these two gents. For Eric Hall (left) it was fifty years since his first turn-out in a Belgrave '7'. He placed 140th that day in 1948 (31st Belgravian home with another two behind him) in a race won by Harry Churcher. George Beecham (right) will be celebrating the half a century since his début in this race in 2000. items.label: March 1999
items.sum: Note explaining the new women's javelin specification for 1999, with the centre of gravity moved forward and old records to be disregarded.
items.s: Javelin Changes Note explaining the new women's javelin specification for 1999, with the centre of gravity moved forward and old records to be disregarded. Javelin Changes Watch out for changes in the women's javelin throw this coming summer. A new specification is being introduced and although the weight will remain the same, the centre of gravity of the new implement will be moved forward by 3cm thus, hopefully, reducing the chances of 'flat' throws. The change will make a difference to the distances thrown and as a result, old records will be disregarded and a new World Record (the longest throw of 1999) will be accepted as the new mark on 1st January 2000. So it's goodbye to Petra Felke's 80.00m throw from 1988. It is unlikely that all tracks will be able to restock immediately with the new style 600gm javelin so the best we can do is attempt to record on the result sheets which style of javelin was used. Petra Felke Petra Felke's women's javelin world record 80.00m from 1988

items.label: March 1999
items.sum: Tribute to Win Shepherd, the club's first lady President, on retiring from calculating Thameside League results after the 1998 season.
items.s: Win Shepherd retires from officiating Tribute to Win Shepherd, the club's first lady President, on retiring from calculating Thameside League results after the 1998 season. Win Shepherd retires from officiating It was the end of an era when the last Thameside League match of 1998 came to a conclusion. Win Shepherd, for so many years the lady (along with Jean) calculating the results, had decided that she would be retiring from officiating. Win, our first ever lady President, has been a part of our Women's Track & Field scene for so long that it is going to be difficult to believe that she's not there when the 1999 season gets under way. Hopefully she will get along to watch one or two meetings, but in the meantime, Win, we wish you well and thank you for the immense amount of work that you have put in over the years. Win Shepherd Win Shepherd retired from officiating after the 1998 Thameside League; calculated the results for many years; the club's first ever lady President Win Shepherd Win Jean Jean helped Win Shepherd calculate Thameside League results Thameside League

items.sum: Health news of members Arthur Penstone (broken leg), Ken Miller (operation) and Derek Jones (recovery from heart valve bypass).
items.s: Health news of members Arthur Penstone (broken leg), Ken Miller (operation) and Derek Jones (recovery from heart valve bypass). Arthur Penstone suffered a broken leg last Autumn and had to undergo a spell in hospital as a result. The plaster cast was off by December and Arthur is now getting around ok with the aid of a stick. Saturday afternoons are not the same without him pottering around fixing up the electrical bits and pieces but we look forward to seeing him back at Belgrave Hall soon. Ken Miller also went into hospital for an operation last September. Luckily he was not out of action for long because he was seen cheering on the Belgrave runners from his garden while they were contesting the Hog's Back Road Race. It's good to hear that Derek Jones has made a great recovery from his heart valve bypass operation last year and we look forward very much to seeing him back at Battersea Park this summer Arthur Penstone Arthur Penstone broke a leg in autumn 1998; fixes the electrical bits at Belgrave Hall Arthur Penstone Arthur Ken Miller Ken Miller hospital operation September 1998; watched the Hog's Back Road Race from his garden Derek Jones Derek Jones recovered from heart valve bypass operation in 1998 Hog's Back Road Race Belgrave Hall Battersea Park

items.s: St. Mary's University College, Strawberry Hill Full-page promotion for St. Mary's University College, Strawberry Hill, describing its sports courses and facilities, with a piece by Nic Cooper and contact details for Allan Staerk or Hazel Mead. Thinking about further education? Why not consider a College of the University of Surrey: St. Mary's University College, Strawberry Hill St. Mary's is one of the country's leading higher education establishments with a long association with the University of Surrey. It is situated in the borough of Richmond Upon Thames and is just half an hour away from the centre of London. It is a single site campus with all facilities on site. This includes halls of residence, lecture rooms, all sporting facilities and (most importantly) the Student Union. Sporting facilities include weight room, indoor sportshall, dance studio, gym, running track and sports injuries clinic. St. Mary's is an excellent place to study and being so close to London, it is also a great place from which to be able to train. Athletic tracks that are easy to get to are Hounslow, Kingsmeadow, Battersea Park and Crystal Palace and there are long runs available through nearby Bushy Park, Richmond Park and Wimbledon Common. Without even leaving campus you'll be able to use the weights room, take part in circuit training twice a week and run around the 'college mile'. So there's no excuse for not being able to carry on with your regular training even though you're at university. Courses Physical Education Concentrating on teaching but the skills gained will be useful in other careers such as coaching, sport management and personnel work. Sport Rehabilitation Students acquire a variety of skills in sport rehabilitation and sport massage and the course enables students to work specifically in the area of sport injury and rehabilitation. Sport Science Excellent stepping stone to careers in sports related fields. Ample opportunity to develop personal skills and to take additional coaching awards and sport massage. Subjects covered include anatomy and physiology, psychology of sport, sociocultural issues, biomechanics with an emphasis on athletics and practical sessions in many sports, again with an emphasis on athletics. Much of the specialised track & field programme is supported by well known and highly respected coaches such as Bruce Longden, Conrad Milton, Judy Vernon and Mike Smith. St. Mary's Athletic Club members include Belgravians Darren Thompson, Nic Cooper and Hazel Mead. The lecturers are very approachable and are always willing to help. Practical work is an important part of the programme which allows students to test theory against practice and makes the degree relevant to real sporting environments. In the second and third years, students are able to specialise in their chosen sports and have the opportunity to undertake a dissertation on any area of interest. From an athlete's point of view St. Mary's has a long tradition of sporting achievement and there are many clubs and societies that you can join. This includes a highly successful athletics club, that enters teams in cross country, road racing and track and field. In March 1999, our student athletic team will be travelling up to Glasgow for the British Universities Indoor Championships and in May the team will go to Bedford for the Outdoor Championships. During the winter students have competed in the London Colleges Cross Country League, the Hyde Park Relays and many other events. Last year four St. Mary's athletes were selected to represent British Students in the annual Loughborough v. A.A.A. v. Great Britain Under 20ís and we even had a representative in the Commonwealth Games in Kuala Lumpur. Nic Cooper writes: Training facilities for all athletic events are suitable for all standards and a number of internationals regularly use the impressively equipped weights rooms and physiology lab. Sports equipment is available for student use and covers all sports generously and includes alternative training aids such as video analysis and electronic equipment. On site there is a physiotherapy and injury rehabilitation clinic and massage rooms. Although these provisions are not exclusively for student use, reduced rates are arranged and students are willing to give massage for further practice. Staff are sympathetic to the needs of elite sports people studying at St. Mary's and consideration is given if international competition or training abroad is necessary. St. Mary's is an excellent place to study and live. The grounds are pleasant and relaxing and Twickenham is still only half an hour away from London and the other facilities across London that Belgrave athletes often use.
